title: “Make Me a Map”: Building a GIS Agent with Agent Bricks, MCP, and Lakebase
abstract: Geospatial workflows are complex—querying spatial databases and generating visualizations requires specialized expertise. We built an AI agent that takes a Slack message and returns a fully functional map application. What started as an internal tool for Solution Architects—replacing hours of manual data prep—is now used by customers too. The architecture: Lakebase serves as the spatial backend (Postgres-compatible with PostGIS), while our MCP server exposes Felt's mapping capabilities to Agent Bricks. Users ask for a map in Slack, the agent queries Lakebase, connects to Felt, and posts back a working map. This talk covers: Lakebase as a geospatial engine—Postgres compatibility in a serverless lakehouse MCP tools for live connections—wiring Lakebase → Felt directly Agent Bricks orchestration—multi-step GIS workflows from Slack Attendees leave with a pattern for building agents that produce working applications, not just answers.

title: 0 to 100 AI/BI Apps in 120 Days: Building an Enterprise Data and AI Platform From Scratch @ Alpura
abstract: In early 2025, Alpura faced fragmented data, multiple BI tools, weak governance and no scalable AI foundation. In just 120 days, we rebuilt the entire data platform on Databricks. Using the Medallion Architecture (Bronze, Silver, Gold), Unity Catalog for enterprise governance and Databricks Metrics for a centralized semantic layer, we created a governed, scalable lakehouse foundation. We consolidated more than five legacy platforms without disrupting operations and eliminated KPI inconsistencies by standardizing business logic. On top of this foundation, we rapidly delivered 100+ AI/BI assets, including 10+ production-grade applications such as a Walmart Scintilla analytics app and an Ambassador Program app — built in days, not months. Leveraging Genie AI, we enabled conversational BI to accelerate adoption. This session shares a practical blueprint for building an AI/BI factory at enterprise speed.

title: 10 Gigawatts of Renewables = 3.2 Billion Events a Day in the Databricks Lakehouse

Anyone can dump events into a bucket. Cleansed, shaped, and AI-ready in less than 4 seconds is data engineering.

title: 1000× Faster Retrieval: Indexed and Full-Text Search in the Lakehouse
abstract: Delta Lake and Iceberg excel at large-scale analytics, but they are not optimized for sub-second point lookups or full-text search. In operational workloads — such as security analytics, log investigation and telemetry — retrieval queries that require full scans or high-cardinality filtering can take minutes to hours, when seconds or milliseconds are required. I built IndexTables, an embedded, Tantivy-based indexing layer that runs directly inside Spark executors, enabling up to 1000× faster query performance while preserving the Lakehouse model. This session explores the architecture: object-storage-hosted indexes with ACID transactions, millisecond-latency aggregations over billions of rows, native time-series bucketing for efficient GROUP BY analytics and NVMe-backed caching with proactive pre-warming. Attendees will learn how Capital One is using IndexTables to complement Delta and Iceberg, creating lakehouse architectures that support both analytical and retrieval-heavy workloads.

title: 800TB, Zero Pipelines: How Ensemble Health Partners Built an AI-Ready Revenue Cycle on Lakebase
abstract: Ensemble Health Partners manages revenue cycle operations for 30+ health systems, processing 25 billion+ transactions across 800TB of healthcare financial data. Legacy SQL Server sprawl —1 5 individual databases with separate schemas —c reated silos that blocked cross-client insights and slowed AI innovation in an industry where providers operate on 1% margins. This session shows how Ensemble consolidated onto Databricks Lakebase as their AI-ready transactional layer, eliminating brittle pipelines and enabling self-service pods to materialize views directly from harmonized Delta tables. The results: 3–5% net revenue yield improvement ($30M+ per $1B health system), 20% organizational efficiency gain, and 10x reduction in failure rates — while powering agentic AI workflows for denial prevention, AR follow-up, and payer-behavior prediction at scale.

Importantly, GSB achieved this with a much smaller team than the major banks, demonstrating practical expertise and delivery experience that other organisations can learn from. To date, GSB has migrated and integrated 85% of its enterprise data onto the Databricks platform and is on track to shut down its legacy warehouse by 2026. Databricks AI capabilities are already delivering material value across traditional ML and gen AI use cases - e.g. a home-loan churn model was built by a single employee and matched the accuracy of a 3rd party model. On top of the enterprise data foundation, Genie Spaces now enable business users to self-serve insights faster and with improved accuracy. GSB is also accelerating value creation in areas such as complaints analysis and sentiment using GenAI.

title: A Unified Approach to Data Exfiltration Protection and Egress Monitoring to Build Secure Agents
abstract: Data exfiltration is one of the most serious security risks organizations face. It can expose sensitive information, leading to reputational damage and regulatory penalties. The challenge is that exfiltration can happen in many ways, including external attackers, poorly configured AI agents, insider mistakes, or malicious insiders, and is often hard to detect until the damage is done. In this lightning talk, we'll break down where exfiltration risks come from and what they may look like in Databricks (spoiler: it's not always a malicious actor!). We'll then introduce a framework for categorizing protection controls across three levels: data platform, compute, and storage. Using this framework, we'll discuss what risks to address today, tomorrow, and in the future with readily available controls at each level. As we wrap-up our session, we'll give you a glimpse into implementing comprehensive egress monitoring: what's here now and what's coming. Walk away with a fresh perspective on data exfiltration risks and actions you can take today to secure and monitor your most sensitive workloads!

title: A Unified Future for Delta and Apache Iceberg™
abstract: Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg™ have converged on similar ideas: columnar metadata for efficient pruning, manifest trees for scalability, and deletion vectors for fast updates. Yet today, we maintain two separate metadata structures, duplicating work and diverging in capabilities. The next major evolution of Delta Lake reimagines metadata from the ground up. This talk introduces a unified metadata architecture where Delta Lake commits store content metadata directly in Iceberg v4's adaptive metadata tree. Delta Lake gains efficient tree-structured manifests and Iceberg interoperability while preserving the transactional guarantees that Delta users depend on. Join us to see the future of lakehouse metadata.

title: A–Z of Unity Catalog Business Semantics: Open and Unified Semantics for Agents, Apps and BI
abstract: Business semantics is the missing bridge between raw data and real understanding for humans and AI alike. In this comprehensive session, the product team behind Unity Catalog’s business semantics takes you from A to Z: what business semantics is, why it matters and how an open and unified semantic layer transforms the way agents, apps and BI tools consume your data. We’ll start with the foundations, defining and governing business glossaries, tags, and semantic metadata within Unity Catalog. Then we’ll show what’s new: the latest capabilities that make semantics flow seamlessly across AI agents, applications and BI tools from a single governed source. See live demos of how unified semantics improve agent reasoning, enrich app experiences and build dashboard trust. Whether you’re just starting or scaling enterprise-wide, walk away with everything you need to make your data universally understood.

title: Accelerating AI From Model to Impact at Workday With Databricks Apps
abstract: Workday needed to put trusted ML insights directly in the hands of sales, customer success and finance—fast. Before, delivering a single internal app required a bespoke full‑stack build and repeated reviews, stretching timelines to nearly a year. By shifting to Databricks Apps and building where the data already lives, Workday compressed delivery to weeks, launched three production AI applications in a single year, and scaled its flagship Sales Companion to 4,500+ active users. This session details the architecture and adoption playbook: Databricks Apps as the UI/middleware, MLflow‑powered components, retrieval‑augmented workflows for unstructured content, governed access with Unity Catalog and fast analytics via SQL Serverless—enabling conversational experiences that let business users self‑serve sentiment analysis, forecasting and KPI insights without waiting on the data science team or adding headcount.

title: Accelerating Corteva’s Data Source Onboarding With Lakeflow
abstract: Onboarding a new data source at Corteva used to take 30–45 days. Now it’s 4–7 days, about 85% faster. The Lakeflow-first strategy and Unity Catalog helped standardize the ingestion‑to‑consumption pathway across 6 domains. Lakeflow Connect, Spark Declarative Pipelines and Jobs make pipeline runs repeatable and config‑driven. A lightweight metadata layer centralizes data cleansing, and an incremental DDL tool pushes schema changes safely through each environment. This pattern now underpins Corteva’s operational analytics. It accelerates root‑cause analysis linking field variability to dryer‑bin stabilization, improves throughput across 35 seed sites, and strengthens seed quality. Today, the setup covers 5,000+ tables from 15+ sources, shortening time‑to‑insight and speeding partner onboarding. Attendees will leave with a reusable Lakeflow‑first ingestion pattern, a metadata‑driven data quality blueprint and a safe schema‑evolution workflow across environments.

title: Accelerating ITSM Modernization with Lakeflow Connect: Nationwide’s Platform Upgrade
abstract: This presentation shows how Nationwide modernized its ServiceNow platform, transforming it from a highly customized, rigid system into a modern, scalable ITSM and data platform by leveraging Lakeflow Connect’s native capabilities to efficiently ingest, store, and curate data for current and future analytics needs. Previously, legacy data was extracted via APIs into Oracle and scattered across siloed stores, creating governance gaps, slow refresh cycles, and poor data quality. By adopting a Lakehouse foundation with incremental and CDC pipelines, Nationwide now benefits from unified governance, clear data lineage, simplified security, and faster time to value. The reimplementation also simplifies integrations, accelerates reporting, and reduces technical debt, all while preserving historical insight.

title: Accelerating Rivian's Autonomy Flywheel: Geospatial Intelligence at Scale
abstract: Our team started on Geospatial journey with Databricks DBR 16.X, from legacy project migration and continued to expand by ingesting and processing three different geospatial datasets (HD USHR maps, public OSM and curated OSM (Overture)). We applied different optimization techniques to make spatial joins more performant and worked closely with Databricks Geospatial team in testing out incremental improvements in DBR, culminating in large scale performance increase on DBR 17.X bringing support to geospatial data types (GEOMETRY, GEOGRAPHY) as dedicated data types that could be stored in delta table. A significant optimization was observed in spatial joins, which could eliminate previously used optimization techniques, making data pipelines maintenance easier. All of these improvements enabled us to enrich internal datasets based on various road attributes from these datasets and use them in analytics, training and potential reinforcement learning applications where needed.

title: Accelerating the Monthly Financial Closing With Genie
abstract: Closing the books every month is still slow and manual for many finance teams. In this session, we will walk through a monthly financial closing for a mid‑size retailer and show how we tackle two of the most painful steps with Databricks One: reconciling gaps between CRM invoices and accounting numbers and running variance analysis to explain differences between actual results and budget. We will follow a finance controller using an AI/BI dashboard to spot issues, Genie in natural language to investigate root causes and draft variance commentary and a Databricks app to apply the corrections safely, update the numbers and generate the final reporting deck.Attendees will see how business users can make financial closing faster, simplify investigations and produce more reliable reports with less manual effort — all from a single, unified workspace.

title: Accelerating the Speed to Value of Analytics with Databricks AI/BI & Agents
abstract: After migrating from Snowflake, Addepar ventured deep into Databricks' native AI/BI suite. This talk shares our practitioner's roadmap for accelerating "speed to value" by building analytics directly where data lives. We explore why we chose AI/BI over external tools and how we serve as early adopters pushing the platform's limits.Key takeaways:- The AI-Assisted Analyst: Leveraging Databricks Assistant to chat through notebook discovery, bypass syntax struggles, and cure "analyst's block" with AI-suggested Dashboard visuals.- Metadata as Code: Why rich Unity Catalog metadata is the critical UI for accurate GenAI.- Metric Views > Tables: Defining semantics once for both Dashboards and Genie to ensure consistent answers, rather than relying on static tables or views.- Genie & Agents: Tips for "teaching" Genie spaces and early experiments using Agent Bricks to orchestrate structured analytics alongside unstructured knowledge agents.

title: Activating Alpha Generation With Multi Agent AI for Fund Screening
abstract: Investment professionals currently spend 12 hours weekly on manual fund screening, leading to operational inefficiencies and lost alpha opportunities. LSEG is leveraging Databricks to orchestrate Genie Spaces across the Lipper fund dataset of 350,000+ investments. Our solution enables users to perform complex fund screening using natural language. By employing a multi-agent supervisor to coordinate specialized Genie Spaces—such as Fund Universe, Performance & Risk, and Flows—users can execute queries like “UK equity funds with 3-year annualized return > 8% and AUM > 500m” against Lipper APIs and tables. This architecture streamlines the workflow sequence from report generation to portfolio optimization, allowing portfolio managers and analysts to identify investment strategies in minutes rather than hours. By leveraging Databricks Multi Agent Supervisor and LSEG’s trusted AI-ready data, firms can significantly reduce operational costs and improve decision-making efficiency.

title: ADBC and the Future of Universal Data Connectivity for Agentic Systems
abstract: Agents are becoming first-class users of the data stack, but they inherit 1990s-era connectivity: slow row-oriented APIs, heavy SDKs, and brittle system-specific connectors. For AI-driven workflows making fast tool calls across systems, this isn’t just slow—it’s terrible agent ergonomics, leading to failures, retries, and need for human intervention. This talk explains why ADBC (Arrow Database Connectivity) is emerging as the universal connector for agentic data workflows: a vendor-neutral API and driver standard that ships Arrow columnar results, enabling fast data access across languages and engines. We’ll show why this matters for agents: frequent queries, tight latency/cost budgets, and the need for safe, reliable access to the tabular truth. You’ll leave with a clear model for where ADBC fits in lakehouse architectures, why it aligns with Databricks and open standards, and a how to move from framework-heavy integrations to lean, CLI-first building blocks guided by agent skills.

abstract: MATCH_RECOGNIZE is landing on Databricks SQL — and it changes how analysts express row patterns. title: Agent as a Judge: Scaling AI Evaluation for the Agentic Era
abstract: Agents have arrived. Evaluation workflows need to catch up.The bottleneck is knowing what to evaluate. You can’t catch failures you don’t know exist, and in production agents, they’re subtle: unclear tool definitions, bloated context, brittle handoffs, and inefficiencies that compound across long sessions. Manual trace review is the only way to discover them, but it doesn’t scale. Blind spots accumulate.Agent as a Judge closes this gap. Where LLM-as-a-judge scores predefined criteria, evaluation agents do open-ended discovery. They work directly on raw traces, surface recurring failure modes, and turn those findings into targeted, high-signal evaluators — a step toward agents that improve agents.We’ll show how this works in Phoenix’s open-source evaluation agent, running on Phoenix’s own production traces. You’ll see what it surfaced, how it compares to human reviewers, and what it takes to trust agents with the work of evaluating agents.

title: Agent Evaluations
abstract: This hands-on course introduces learners to evaluating, governing, and securing agentic AI systems on Databricks. You'll begin by exploring the motivation for evaluation and governance frameworks and how they connect to the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. Next, you'll learn how to apply MLflow evaluation metrics and a variety of evaluation techniques, including online evaluation, synthetic evaluation, and building evaluation datasets from MLflow traces. The course then examines how Unity Catalog governance extends to agents' functions, models, and tools, ensuring proper access control, auditability, and compliance. Finally, you'll learn Databricks AI Security Framework (DASF) and how to secure agents with Mosaic AI Gateway, applying guardrails, rate limits, and policy filters to enforce safe and reliable usage. Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. Prerequisites Familiarity with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, including Unity Catalog for governance and model management Intermediate Python programming experience Familiarity with Generative AI fundamentals, including RAG architectures and their components (chunking, embeddings, vector stores) Basic knowledge of MLflow for experiment tracking and model lifecycle management General awareness of data governance principles, including access control, data lineage, and data privacy

title: Agent Ready Data Governance: Databricks on Databricks
abstract: When your data consumers shift from 10,000 humans to 100,000 high-speed agents, “governance” can no longer mean a wiki page or a PDF policy document. Agents don’t read wikis; they need semantic, machine-readable guardrails. In this talk, the Data Platform team discusses our pivot to “agent-ready governance.” We are moving beyond simple access control lists (ACLs) to a model where Unity Catalog provides deep semantic context, usage constraints and “rules of the road” that our 100,000 agents can natively understand. Join us to see how we ensure that our digital workforce operates safely, preventing the chaos of 100,000 bots making bad decisions at machine speed.

title: Agentic Admins: Managing Databricks @ Databricks
abstract: If we are building a future with 100,000 agents accessing our platform, relying on human administrators to click buttons and approve tickets is a non-starter. The math simply doesn’t work; human admin teams cannot scale linearly with an exponential agent workforce. This session explores how the Data Platform team is solving this by building “agentic admins” — autonomous systems capable of managing the platform for us. We will discuss the shift from manual provisioning to agent-led resource management, permissions granting and configuration tuning. Learn how we are architecting the control plane that allows a small team of humans to govern an army of 100,000 digital users without burning out.

title: Agentic Analytics on Databricks Lakehouse
abstract: Agents promise to scale instant access to data insights across organizations. However, most data warehouses were built for humans reading dashboards. Agents expose every assumption that breaks. Flawed semantics lead to hallucination, fragmented governance exposes improper data access, and cost/performance issues explode when one analyst becomes a thousand agents. In this session we'll walk through what agentic analytics looks like in practice on Databricks Lakehouse, demoing the patterns customers are running in production today. Following these patterns, you can dramatically increase your data team's impact across your organization while reducing time-to-insight. You'll leave with a clear model of approaches to agentic analytics at scale, and see why Databricks Lakehouse is built for it.

title: Agentic Data Engineering with Genie Code
abstract: Genie Code is an autonomous AI partner for data work, with depth across the data engineering lifecycle. We show how builders use it to iterate on Spark Declarative Pipelines and Lakeflow Jobs, accelerating authoring. It knows your data, grounded in Unity Catalog metadata, semantics, and governance policies. This grounding helps Genie Code take accurate and context-aware actions. Beyond authoring, Genie Code keeps workflows healthy, proactively monitoring and maintaining data and AI in production. We discuss how it autonomously detects, diagnoses, and proposes fixes the moment failures happen, with every agent running sandboxed, so production stays untouched.

title: Agentic Feature Engineering: How McAfee Drives Personalization With Agent Bricks
abstract: McAfee protects millions of users through products like Scam Detector and Social Privacy Manager. Iteration on adaptive pricing models was bottlenecked by slow, manual feature engineering. To unlock value from massive user signals, we needed to move from ideation to production fast. In this talk, we show how we built an autonomous feature engineering agent on Agent Bricks that cuts engineering cycles by 60% — replacing manual SQL with an agent that reasons, iterates, and converges. This is the next step in a journey where AI-assisted feature store and personalization have contributed to $54M+ in incremental revenue over three years. The agentic approach is how we make that capability reproducible, faster, and accessible without a team of ML specialists. Attendees will see a live blueprint of our agentic pipeline: Analyze & ideate: Agent loads domain context and playbook from Unity Catalog, analyzes baseline and proposes features via LLM reasoning Generate & evaluate: Agent writes code, executes in sandbox, evaluates against baseline and logs every iteration to MLflow. Converge & deploy: Best features publish directly to Unity Catalog feature store. Walk away with a reproducible blueprint for agentic feature engineering on Databricks.

title: Agentic PHI De-Identification Across Multimodal Healthcare Data on Databricks
abstract: De-identifying clinical data is essential for research and secondary use, yet current approaches are costly and require constant manual tuning as data distributions change. This session introduces an agentic approach to automating privacy-preserving pipelines on the Databricks Lakehouse.We present an Agentic De-Identification Framework that treats the pipeline itself as an autonomous agent, minimizing human effort while maximizing security and compliance.Attendees will learn how to use Agent Bricks to fit de-identification models and entity resolution logic to customer data; apply agentic de-identification across structured data, clinical notes, and imaging metadata using Mosaic AI Agent framework; and register core de-identification logic as governed Unity Catalog Functions.We conclude by showing how AgentOps is operationalized with MLflow tracing, Unity Catalog governance, and Mosaic AI Gateway Guardrails to deliver auditable, secure PHI protection at scale.

title: Agentic Security: Real-Time Threat Detection with Lakewatch
abstract: AI-driven attacks now operate at machine scale, with mean time to exploit collapsing from 23 days to just under 2 days. SIEMs as we know them today are going to disappear because this new agentic era you are dealing with unprecedented threats. That’s why Databricks announced Lakewatch, the Open Agentic SIEM. Instead of locking security data into proprietary systems with per-byte ingest licensing, Lakewatch lets teams store all their security telemetry in open formats, retain it for years, and run agentic AI across it. Security teams gain complete visibility across the enterprise and can deploy defensive security agents to automate threat detection and response at massive scale.

title: AI Agents for the Frontline: 7-Eleven’s GenAI Maintenance Assistant
abstract: Maintenance technicians at 7-Eleven rely on preventive maintenance, catalogue and parts documents for equipment like HVACs and ovens — often using only their phones. These documents span thousands of files in formats like PDFs and spreadsheets stored in shared drives, making it hard to find the right information quickly. High attrition and missed training sessions compounds knowledge gaps. To address this, 7-Eleven developed a GenAI agentic system using Mosaic AI, Agent Bricks and Databricks Hybrid Search that enables technicians to 1) Retrieve relevant maintenance documents with concise answers 2) Capture equipment images and receive troubleshooting solutions 3) Access parts information by equipment brand 4) Get solutions from the internet. This chatbot bridges knowledge gaps with instant access to institutional knowledge. We will walk through how we built this system, our evaluation methodologies and the three-step prompt framework including guardrails for safe internet searches.

title: AI Can’t Wait: How to Overcome GPU Scarcity and Keep Workloads Running
abstract: GPU scarcity, cloud capacity constraints, and regional outages are challenges enterprises simply cannot afford: they block model training and serving, and leave mission-critical workloads queuing or failing with no good recourse. By intelligently routing workloads to the optimal compute while preserving each customer's data residency, security controls, and compliance boundary, Databricks is solving both problems transparently. In this talk, we'll show how we're delivering GPU access to customers who are capacity-constrained in their home region, and offering enterprise-grade availability guarantees for serverless workloads without requiring customers to manage multi-cloud infrastructure themselves.

title: AI is a Data Engineering Problem
abstract: AI agents produce orders of magnitude more text data than traditional systems — conversation logs, agent traces, tool calls and coding assistant sessions. One company running agents can generate 70 Wikipedias of text per month, and yet nobody knows how to make sense of it. Warehouses query numeric columns, not multi-turn conversations. Dashboards show averages while model failures hide in message content. My hypothesis: making sense of AI data is a data engineering problem, not an AI modeling problem. We need new tools that enable customers to store, explore and curate AI data while scaling to trillions of messages. I’ll demo live: a browser-native stack that reads Parquet and Iceberg from object storage, no backend. Range requests fetch only bytes needed; client-side decoding via hyparquet and Icebird, our open-source Iceberg reader. Navigate table snapshots, scroll millions of LLM rows, surface failures with LLM-as-a-judge and curate data — all in the browser.

title: AI Mesh – The Age of the AI Products
abstract: This session explores the evolution from Data Products to AI Products, introducing "Agents" as scalable, composable building blocks for the enterprise. We will discuss how to apply product thinking to AI—ensuring agents are discoverable, connectable, and trusted within the Unity Catalog. The talk details the "Agents Maturity Model," guiding you from L0 (Observe) to L3 (Act) automation, and outlines a robust architecture where agents serve as domain experts. Finally, we will demonstrate a real-world energy use case, showing how to build and orchestrate reusable agents to analyze wind park data using Databricks Genie, significantly accelerating time-to-market.

title: AI Search: High Quality Retrieval Made Easy
abstract: Measuring and tuning performance and retrieval quality for Search bars, recommender systems, entity resolution traditionally required quarters of tuning, a team of domain experts, and ongoing maintenance that kept engineers away from building the actual application. Databricks AI Search makes it simple to build a state-of-the-art retrieval system, with quality bespoke to your application. In this talk we’ll show you how easy it is to deploy a production grade Search with the latest advances in hybrid (keyword-plus-semantic) search, reranking, domain-tuned models, evaluate retrieval quality for your corpus, and build feedback loops that continuously improve your retrieval quality. You'll see what's shipped, what's next, and walk away with a production-ready stack and a working playbook for measuring and improving retrieval quality

title: AI Will Go Wrong and the Blueprint to Get It Right
abstract: Most AI failures aren't technology problems — they're people, process, and architecture problems. In this hands-on session, you'll witness a live AI trainwreck: an agent operating without guardrails, governance, or the right organizational design. Then, in a real-time post-mortem, we will collectively dissect what broke and why. You'll map the missing middle layer: the intersection of roles, accountability structures, and platform architecture. And you'll work alongside peers to design practical fixes. The session closes with an exercise where attendees act as domain experts to train an AI Judge capable of scaling oversight across enterprise deployments. Expect minimal slides, maximum doing, and a concrete blueprint you can apply within 30 days. This session is built for executives who are tired of theoretical AI frameworks and want proven patterns that make AI projects safer, faster, and genuinely business-ready.

title: AI_DIAGNOSE: Automating Spark Job Debugging With LLM Agents
abstract: Debugging distributed Spark jobs is notoriously difficult, often requiring hours of sifting through massive logs to find root causes. We introduce AI_DIAGNOSE, a new Spark SQL procedure in Databricks Runtime that automates this process using large language models (LLMs). This session explores the architecture of AI_DIAGNOSE, detailing how we implemented a ReAct-style agent within the Spark engine. We will demonstrate how the agent autonomously gathers context, retrieves distributed logs, and analyzes job failures. We'll cover technical challenges like managing LLM context windows with large logs, ensuring structured actionable outputs, and leveraging Databricks Model Serving for secure inference. Join us to learn how AI_DIAGNOSE works under the hood to drastically reduce Mean Time To Resolution (MTTR) for data pipelines.

title: AiChemy: How MCP-Powered Agents Cut Drug Discovery Research from Weeks to Minutes
abstract: Drug discovery demands sifting through millions of compounds, thousands of papers, and dozens of databases—a process that costs the industry an average of $2.6B and over 10 years per approved drug. Researchers spend days cross-referencing OpenTargets for genetic evidence, PubChem for chemical properties, and PubMed for supporting literature. What if agents could do it in minutes?Meet AiChemy, a multi-agent assistant that combines external MCP servers like OpenTargets, PubChem, and PubMed with your own chemical libraries on Databricks. Add Agent Skills to find druggable targets, drug candidates and their chemical properties and safety profiles, complete with supporting evidence.You can build your own multi-agent assistant in just 5 minutes using our no-code Agent Bricks. Plus, Databricks assets like Genie, Vector Search, and Functions are automatically turned into MCP servers for seamless integration. Stop scrolling through endless articles and databases—let your agents do it for you!

title: An Intro to Building and Scaling Agentic Apps
abstract: Agents have promised a lot lately, but most people just have a job they want done and don't want to spend time on endless science experiments. Teams stall on integration, struggle with scale, and wrestle with how to deliver agents to users safely and reliably inside a real application. This intro session shows how to build and scale agentic apps end-to-end on Databricks. You'll see how Agent Bricks lets you create managed, production-ready agents; how Databricks Apps delivers them to users with governance and observability built in; and how Lakebase powers the transactional backend so your app can act — not just answer. You'll walk away with a clear blueprint for turning your first agent into a production app your whole company can use, and the confidence to move from prototype to scaled deployment without rebuilding your stack.

title: Apache Iceberg™ Interoperability: First-Class Open Support in Databricks Delta Sharing
abstract: Open data sharing across platform boundaries is now a reality. As organizations move toward multi-engine environments, collaborating across different catalogs and ecosystems is a strategic necessity. With the launch of first-class Iceberg support in Databricks Delta Sharing, you can maintain a single governance layer while supporting a diverse, multi-platform data estate. Key Highlights: First-Class Iceberg Support: Share Delta tables as native Iceberg tables via the Iceberg REST Catalog API for zero-copy sharing to Snowflake, Trino, and Spark. Bi-Directional Interoperability: Bring ""foreign"" Iceberg tables from AWS Glue or Snowflake into Unity Catalog and share them to any recipient. Unified Governance: Share fine-grained Views via secretless authentication, even to non-Databricks platforms. Open Standards, No Lock-In: Shift from closed sharing models to a transparent protocol that supports multiple clouds, formats, and platforms simultaneously.

title: Apache Spark™ Connect: The Path to Modern, AI-Ready Spark
abstract: Spark Connect is more than a new client interface for Apache Spark™ — it is the foundation for a modern, AI-ready, and production-friendly Spark experience. As AI assistants generate more Spark code, the defaults they learn will shape how the next generation of data applications is built — that makes Spark Connect a strategic shift, not just a technical one. In this session, we will share our vision for making Spark Connect the default way developers build with Spark. We will discuss how DataFrame-first guidance, better AI-generated code compatibility, and machine-readable API discovery can make Connect the easiest path for developers. We will also cover the work needed to build production trust, including closing migration gaps, improving observability, and increasing ecosystem compatibility. Attendees will leave with a clear view of why Spark Connect matters now and what it will take to make it the standard interface for modern Spark applications.

title: AppKit: The Official Full-Stack SDK for Databricks Apps
abstract: AppKit--the official TypeScript SDK for Databricks Apps--handles the toughest parts of building apps--so you don't have to. In this technical session, the creators of AppKit walk through how its plugin architecture (Analytics, Genie, Lakebase, Files) gives you production-ready capabilities out of the box: auto-generated TypeScript types for safe SQL, built-in caching, telemetry, retry logic, and OBO execution — all pre-wired so you can focus on your app logic, not your infrastructure. Every API is also designed to be discoverable by LLMs, making AppKit a natural fit for AI-assisted development. Whether you're starting from databricks apps init or extending an existing app, leave with a clear picture of how AppKit makes Databricks-native development fast, structured, and AI-friendly.

title: Applying Software Development Principles to a Data-Driven World: Automating SDP from Dev to Prod
abstract: Are you a data architect struggling to bring rigor and best practices to your data operations? This session highlights how the Intermountain Health Data Teams transformed their data platform by overcoming cultural resistance and technical gaps to fully automate production-grade data pipeline deployments. By combining Databricks Asset Bundles, GitHub Actions, and Spark Declarative Pipelines, they built a reliable CI/CD workflow supporting nearly all workloads. Parameterized deployments manage dev and prod seamlessly, while a trunk based Git strategy avoids the complexity of multi branch models. The impact: over 90% improvement in deployment reliability, fewer hotfixes, and 20% faster processing. And because transformation depends on people, we’ll share how Intermountain guided teams away from GUI only ETL habits, building trust, clarity, and excitement for this modern, maintainable approach.

title: Architecting Agentic Security: Scaling Threat Detection with LLM and Lake house Architecture
abstract: When new threat intelligence lands, attackers are already moving. Adobe’s security team needed more than automation, so we built an agentic security platform that ingests data, orchestrates hunts, and surfaces detections with minimal human intervention. Using reasoning, agents analyze threats, validate attack paths, and execute fleet sweeps, reducing threat detection timelines from days to minutes. In this talk, we’ll walk through how we built this system on a lakehouse architecture. Databricks Workflows orchestrate parallel hunt campaigns across various security logs, autonomously triggering jobs and aggregating results. You’ll learn how we designed for agentic behavior, including multi-source ingestion into a single pipeline, workflow orchestration logic that decides when and what to hunt, and production patterns that keep the system reliable at scale. We’ll share architecture and code so you can adapt these agentic security patterns in your own environment.

abstract: This session is not a generic “AI is the future” talk. It is a practical, experience‑based guide to taking Databricks AI/BI Genie from a promising pilot to a trusted, production‑grade capability. Dashboards answer “what,” but not “why” or “what if.” Here is where Genie comes in. We’ll walk through our journey at Atlassian from pilot to production—designing Genie spaces on curated tables and metrics, building an evaluation framework for accuracy and coverage, and integrating Genie into our everyday tools and Rovo AI agent. We will touch upon how Databricks and Atlassian partnered to bring the power of Genie to our Rovo Marketplace and built the ability to route a user question to the right Genie space. title: Automating Document Work with Long-Horizon AI Agents
abstract: ~90% of enterprise data is unstructured, and a lot of that lives in the form of documents - PDFs, pptx, docx, etc. - powering a majority of enterprise knowledge work.AI agents have the potential to simultaneously better make sense of docs and also automate human workflows over them. Existing document AI use cases have either been long-running but constrained (e.g. a batch invoice processing through RPA), or non-deterministic but short-horizon (e.g. ChatGPT deep research over a collection of existing files). Going forward there's a huge opportunity to build long-running agents that can understand, reason over, and edit documents at scale.In this session, we'll walk through core advances in document OCR and agent orchestration that have given rise to initial use cases around doc extraction workflows and general-purpose chatbots (and share real-world customer use cases). We will then articulate some of the remaining gaps needed to achieve "long-running" document work automation.

title: Automating Phishing Triage With Agentic AI and Knowledge Graph Memory on Databricks
abstract: Phishing attacks remain a persistent threat, exploiting human trust through sophisticated impersonation. In this session, we present a Databricks-based compound agentic system using knowledge graphs, multiple agents, and MLflow to automate triage of reported phishing emails at scale, reducing analyst workload and accelerating threat response. We walk through scalable pipelines built on Spark Structured Streaming and Delta Lake, then describe how our knowledge graph provides long-term memory, storing historical emails to enable reasoning across campaigns. We demonstrate agentic orchestration with LangGraph where specialized agents use tools to analyze headers, sender reputation, body content, URLs, and behaviors before producing triage decisions with reasoning traces. abstract: As enterprises evolve from isolated AI assistants to domain-specific multi-agent systems, scaling innovation without overloading central teams becomes critical. title: Behind the Curtain: How We Do Eval in Genie
abstract: Evaluating AI systems is notoriously challenging—especially when correctness isn’t binary. title: Benchmarks Don't Lie: Inside Lakebase Performance Engineering
abstract: Get an inside look at how the Lakebase engineering team designs benchmarks that reflect real-world workload patterns rather than synthetic best-case scenarios, and how we isolate variables across the storage, compute, and network layers to understand where time is actually spent. title: Best Practices for Disaster Recovery and Resilience on Databricks
abstract: When a region goes down, every minute counts. But building disaster recovery for a lakehouse is often complex, requiring coordination across data, metadata, and workspace assets. In this session, we’ll share best practices for designing resilient data and AI platforms on Databricks. Learn how to think about recovery objectives, including RPO and RTO, and how to architect for cross-region availability across your data, governance layer, and production workloads. We’ll walk through common patterns for replication, failover, and recovery, along with tradeoffs between cost, complexity, and performance. You’ll also see how to reduce operational overhead, avoid brittle DIY approaches, and ensure applications can recover quickly when disruptions occur. Whether you’re supporting mission-critical analytics or production AI systems, walk away with practical guidance to design, test, and operate disaster recovery with confidence.

title: Beyond Frontier Models: Building Closed-Loop LLM Systems That Learn from Outcomes
abstract: Frontier models are powerful generalists, but the future of LLM applications will be won by systems that are specialized, measurable and continuously improving. He covers how live business outcomes become training signals, how smaller models can become faster, cheaper, and more reliable than general-purpose APIs, and why the next generation of LLM applications will be closed-loop, governed, and outcome-driven from day one.

title: Beyond Medallion: Architecting Disney’s DATOS for Complex, Real-Time Data Streams With Databricks
abstract: Disney’s Medallion architecture laid a strong foundation for enterprise data governance, but emerging needs—ranging from personalized user experiences to real-time financial insights—required a richer, near real-time view across domains such as subscriptions, billing and payments. DATOS addresses this by serving as a contextual aggregation and abstraction layer built on the Databricks Lakehouse Platform. Using Structured Streaming and Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines, DATOS ingests diverse sources like Kafka, Kinesis, and data lakes while absorbing upstream schema and delivery variability to provide stable, reusable data products. Liquid Clustering enhances performance on high‑volume tables, and Unity Catalog ensures unified governance and security. This session explores how DATOS reduces operational overhead, decouples producers and consumers, accelerates onboarding, and delivers a context-aware source of truth that powers real-time analytics, Unity Dashboards, and advanced AI/ML workloads.

title: Beyond Monitoring: Lakeflow Observability for Operational Health
abstract: It is 3 AM. A dashboard is stale, an SLA slipped, and everyone is guessing which job, pipeline, or dependency broke first. That is when surface-level monitoring stops being useful. You need observability that shows the health of your workflows and helps you find the cause fast. In this session, we will show how Lakeflow Observability helps data engineering teams move from reactive monitoring to real operational health. You will see how to monitor runs, tasks, dependencies, alerts, and health metrics across jobs and pipelines, and how Databricks system tables provide the historical depth needed for root-cause analysis, performance analysis, cost tracking, and reliability reporting at scale. We will also cover practical patterns for tracking streaming backlog, freshness, SLA risk, and failure trends, and show how Genie Code can help teams troubleshoot faster using natural language. Your 3 AM self will thank you.

title: Beyond Tables: How Musinsa Built a Self-Optimizing Semantic Layer on Databricks
abstract: Musinsa, South Korea's #1 fashion platform ($3.4B GMV, 8,000+ brands, 10M+ users, 13 countries), faced an architecture trilemma where every pipeline forced trade-offs between productivity, latency and cost. The root cause was not technology but a mental model: "build a table before you analyze." This caused "Organizational Amnesia": marts preserved results but lost the logic. We built a TVF-based semantic layer on Databricks SQL, shifting from "which table to query" to "what logic to compose." Four time-standardized TVFs, demand-driven caching (CTVF) on Delta Lake, and three AI agents (AI/BI Genie, MCP) enable self-optimizing analytics managed via Unity Catalog. Results: 75% fewer managed assets (1,000 to 250), 98% faster analysis (7 days to 2 hours), 3.6x self-service increase (15% to 55%). Attendees leave with a trilemma framework and concrete TVF patterns. Includes a live SQL demo.

title: Beyond the Dashboard: Designing Premium, AI-Powered Operations Apps on Databricks
abstract: Connected systems generate massive operational telemetry, yet most teams still consume it through generic dashboards that can bury insight behind filters and grids. Turning raw signal into decisive action across hundreds of assets is as much a product and design challenge as a data one. This session shows how to deliver branded, business-facing operations experiences on Databricks using Apps, Lakebase, Model Serving and Genie as a single substrate for data, AI and product. We follow an operations lead through a custom app built around an aircraft fleet: a top-level overview, deeper insight views with recommended actions and an AI chat that answers natural-language questions on the same governed tables. The talk focuses on patterns you can reuse: shaping noisy telemetry into decision-ready gold tables, designing apps that feel like products rather than dashboards and orchestrating multiple AI agents.

We will hear from Edmunds on how they built an agentic digital workforce powered by Claude on Databricks. We'll deep-dive into how a "hunting party" of specialized agents autonomously writes code, opens merge requests, and audits 101 legacy schemas in one afternoon (vs. two weeks manually). Attendees will learn how 40+ composable skills yield exponential capability, how a self-improving flywheel slashed prototype-to-production lead times by 50% and how tasks that once cost $640 in human effort now run for $25 in agentic compute.

title: Beyond the Tech Stack: Architecting a Data-First Culture at Scale
abstract: A modern data platform without data-ready people is a stranded asset. Yanolja, Korea's leading travel-tech unicorn, learned that scaling AI-driven innovation required building a talent strategy as sophisticated as its technical architecture. When Yanolja partnered with Databricks, the breakthrough was not technology deployment but C-suite commitment to train more than 1,000 employees out of a workforce of roughly 2,000. That scale of organizational investment created a cultural shift that changed how leadership, engineering, and business teams collaborated around data. In this session, data engineering leader Youngho Song, and Head of Data Sooyoung Lee share the "assess-and-architect" methodology they used to identify skill gaps, the enterprise-wide data capability framework that created a shared language across the organization, and the measurable platform ROI that followed. For CHROs, CTOs, and CDOs who understand that the bottleneck to AI maturity is human, not technical—this session is the strategic playbook you need.

title: Beyond the Trace: adidas’ Agent Digital Twin for Governance, Cost and ROI
abstract: Your agent answered but can you prove why, what it cost, and what breaks when a tool or prompt changes? AI spend is forecast near $1.5T in 2025 and GenAI at $644B, yet Gartner predicts >40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end-2027 as costs rise and controls lag. At adidas (200+ serving endpoints, 300+ data and AI products, 6k+ registered models, 600k+ pipeline runs), we go beyond per-run traces to an agent digital twin: A lakehouse control plane mapping agent → tool → prompt → retrieval → model call → post-processing, then rolling up risk, quality and unit economics across a fleet. You’ll see a Databricks pattern with MLflow Tracing, Unity Catalog + system tables for audit evidence and DBU/cost signals, plus eval/optimization loops with governance guardrails. Key highlights: Digital-twin control plane for fleets Per-hop unit economics + cost leak forensics Continuous audit evidence by design ROI attribution by agent behavior

title: BI for AI: Transforming OTel Agent Telemetry into Enterprise Analytics
abstract: You’ve instrumented your GenAI application, captured your MLflow traces using OpenTelemetry standards and stored them in Unity Catalog. Now what? Too often, observability stops at ingestion, treating traces like passive, isolated logs instead of valuable corporate data. This session looks past the initial setup to show the analytical power unlocked when agent telemetry lives inside a governed lakehouse. By merging your trace tables with existing enterprise data, you can move past micro-debugging and start running true business intelligence on your artificial intelligence. Key takeaways: Cross-domain data ingestion (join MLflow trace tables with Zendesk/Salesforce data to correlate agent performance with ticket volume/CSAT) SQL-driven agent analytics (isolate systemic tool failures, latency bottlenecks, infinite loops across thousands of runs) Data-driven evaluation loops (harvest production logs for targeted LLM eval and fine-tuning)

title: BI Locked Semantic Models are Dead! Open Semantics Just Entered the Chat
abstract: The biggest blocker in fully adopting Unity Catalog (UC) isn’t data access; it’s the business logic that never makes it there. KPIs, measures, and dimensions live inside proprietary semantic models, hand-crafted by analysts over years. In an AI-era open semantics are crucial to go the next mile beyond static and manual data analytics, but rebuilding them manually is expensive, fragile, and doesn’t scale. We bring this vision of a scalable, automated & governed solution to life using our open-source agentic framework, Kasal. In this demo, we feature Coca-Cola HBC, a pioneer in big data processing & innovation, with whom we leveraged Kasal for one of their most complex Power BI reports to automatically generate over 25+ UC Metric Views, encompassing over 200 measures from a single semantic model and powering a fully optimized Genie Space on top of it. This real-world example shows how Kasal accelerates migrations and enables next-level AI-driven insights to generate real business value, as demonstrated through their IDOR (Insights Discovery On Report) initiative.

title: Bionic Supply Chain: Architecting a Unified Agentic Framework for Risk & Cost Recovery
abstract: The modern supply chain is fractured, stuck in a “visibility vacuum” of cost asymmetry and a “triage trap” where material and production planners miss critical risks and purchasing managers miss cost targets due to cognitive overload. To bridge this gap, we present a unified vision for the AI-enabled supply chain ecosystem, moving beyond disparate tools to a cohesive intelligent platform. We introduce an agentic architecture built entirely on the lakehouse, utilizing Databricks Apps and Unity Catalog to serve distinct personas. For purchasing managers, we deploy NOVAA, an engine using MLflow to benchmark “should-costs” and Mosaic AI to arrest margin leakage and generate negotiation playbooks. Simultaneously, SONAR, our supply planners’ control tower, empowers them by aggregating SAP/TMS data into a unified truth. Here, a hierarchical agentic workflow, powered by Agent Bricks, bridges classical ML with GenAI to predict disruptions and orchestrate sub-agents for autonomous resolution.

title: Blue Origin — Using Data to Build a Road to Space
abstract: At Blue Origin, Databricks is the central data lakehouse for design, manufacturing, and launch operations. Scaling to thousands of pipelines without scaling headcount required rethinking how we manage data in the first place. We will share how we use AI and automation to build pipelines and tables with no human intervention required and how we automated data quality and metadata management to make our data AI ready. This enables federated data teams across the company to use trustworthy data and AI to build a road to space! We will walk through a multi-agent system built on this foundation to manage satellite telemetry. An orchestrator queries a knowledge graph of prior episodes and a vector store of resolution procedures, then routes tasks to specialist agents for anomaly classification, forecasting, resolution, and command safety validation. Each execution is captured, clustered, and distilled back into procedural memory, so the system improves from its own operational history.

title: BP Cut Cloud Spend by 43% and Speed Critical Jobs From Days to ~8 Hours With Databricks SQL
abstract: BP is a 117-year-old global energy company spanning upstream exploration and production, refining, trading, retail, and growing low-carbon businesses. Its data estate evolved across classic enterprise warehouse patterns and cloud stacks split by business unit—upstream on Azure and retail on AWS. Hadoop-era systems became too slow at scale, and Redshift-based serving was costly and hard to right-size. BP standardized on Databricks SQL as its warehouse and BI serving layer across clouds, using Unity Catalog and Delta Sharing to reuse governed data without copying it. The team reduced cloud cost 43% and accelerated key processing from days to ~8 hours, while powering Power BI and other tools through Databricks SQL Serverless warehouses.

title: Branching the Database: What Engineering Teams Can Finally Do When the Database Forks in One Second
abstract: Every other layer of your stack has been cheap to fork, fail, and restart for years. Code branches. Containers spin up and down. Infrastructure templates. But the database stayed expensive — and the workarounds we built around it became permanent fixtures: • Mocks for every repository. • Shared staging environments with six developers stepping on each other. • Production bugs that nobody can safely reproduce, because the data lives in production. • Migrations tested for the first time in a maintenance window, on a Friday afternoon, with prayer. These weren't best practices. They were rational responses to a constraint everyone accepted: databases were too expensive to fork, so we developed against fiction. Databricks Lakebase changes the economics. A full production database branch in roughly a second, costs cents, and is governed natively in Unity Catalog — making this category of capability viable in regulated environments, not just startups. In this session, we’ll share: how integration tests can exercise production feature branches, and how destructive QA can become something teams can run without asking for permission. We draw on a real, state-heavy application running on Lakebase and current client work.

• Production bugs that nobody can safely reproduce, because the data lives in production.
• Migrations tested for the first time in a maintenance window, on a Friday afternoon, with prayer.

 

These weren't best practices. They were rational responses to a constraint everyone accepted: databases were too expensive to fork, so we developed against fiction.

 

Databricks Lakebase changes the economics. A full production database branch in roughly a second, costs cents, and is governed natively in Unity Catalog — making this category of capability viable in regulated environments, not just startups.

 

In this session, we’ll share: how integration tests can exercise production feature branches, and how destructive QA can become something teams can run without asking for permission. We draw on a real, state-heavy application running on Lakebase and current client work.

title: Breaking Down Data Silos: Mastercard’s Path to Comprehensive, Privacy‑Safe Marketing Intelligence
abstract: In today’s rapidly evolving marketing landscape, global and multi market teams in companies like Mastercard face unprecedented complexity - fragmented Martech tools, siloed data, proliferating channels, and stricter privacy regulations. The results are shallow insights, weaker personalization, and difficulty measuring ROI across channels. A unified data platform built on a governed, scalable data lake addresses these challenges by integrating global data into a single source of truth, enabling identity resolution, advanced segmentation, real time activation, and consistent full funnel insights. We will explore how Mastercard is building a CDP in Databricks with marketing data sources powered by Unity Catalog. Using Data Vault modeling within the CDP allows data to be onboarded easily and enables teams to ingest data quickly. Finally, we will cover how Unity Catalog enables governance, ensuring each team has access to only the data they need, while sensitive attributes remain protected.

title: Bringing Agents to Data: How Workday Architects Governed Agentic AI with Iceberg and Unity Catalog
abstract: Traditional “data-to-compute” models create latency and fragmented governance that hinder Agentic AI. To solve this, Workday and Databricks advocate “bringing agents to data” via the Databricks Lakehouse. By operating on data in situ, autonomous agents maintain real-time consistency without the risks of replication. This architecture enables reliable multi-agent coordination at scale while ensuring unified data integrity and reduced operational costs across the enterprise. The technical core uses Apache Iceberg for ACID transactions and snapshot isolation, providing a stable foundation for agent reasoning. Databricks Unity Catalog adds a unified governance layer, enforcing fine-grained security, lineage, and auditability. This production-grade approach significantly cuts query latency and storage expenses, allowing organizations to scale from single-agent pilots to hundreds of coordinated agents across multiple departments like Customer Experience, RevOps and Analytics.

title: Build and Deploy Databricks Projects Using Automation Bundles and Agents
abstract: Modern data engineering teams need more than deployment automation. They need projects that are source-controlled, governed, and reviewable, so both humans and AI agents can safely build, deploy, and operate them at scale. Declarative Automation Bundles (DABs) provide that foundation. By expressing your entire Databricks project as source code, DABs not only enable scalable processes for human developers, but provide the exact structured interface AI agents need to interact with and manage your workflows. In this session, we will show how to use DABs in practice, including best practices and the latest authoring workflows across Genie Code, local IDEs, and the Workspace UI. We will also introduce Deployment History, a new service to track exactly who deployed what, when, and with what result. Building on this foundation, we will share a first look at our Genie Code powered product that monitors jobs, pipelines, tables, and other data assets for failures and optimization opportunities. It explains the root cause, proposes a fix, and validates it in a sandboxed environment. Today, data engineers spend 50%+ of their time maintaining data assets. As agentic tools make code generation faster and more broadly available, removing that operational bottleneck is more urgent than ever.

title: Build Better & Faster on Databricks with the AI Dev Kit
abstract: AI-assisted development tools have transformed how software is built, yet lack native integration with enterprise data platforms. The AI Dev Kit is an open-source framework enabling AI code-generation services—Claude, Cursor, Gemini, and others—to build and deploy production workloads directly on Databricks. It provides platform-aware tooling allowing AI assistants to generate Databricks-native code adhering to best practices across pipelines, jobs, and Unity Catalog. Critically, it enables non-technical analysts to build robust Databricks workflows through natural language, dramatically lowering the barrier to entry. Since launch in January 2025, the project surpassed 100 GitHub stars in one week with accelerating organic adoption. This session covers architecture, real-world use cases, and implications of AI-assisted development for the Databricks ecosystem.

title: Build Fresh Data View for Agents
abstract: When you have a large enterprise monorepo or corpus with 1% changing every day, how do you build a data pipeline that effectively surfaces fresh insights to your coding agents continuously? Agents run ~50x faster than humans and create massive unstructured data. You cannot fit the entire thing into the agent; it requires building a view over a large unstructured corpus. CocoIndex is a context engine for agents: a new computing paradigm over evolving unstructured assets and multi-stage processing. You declare the state of your target as a function of the source; the engine keeps it in sync with minimal reprocessing, across time horizons, at scale. Demo: building context for coding agents on 100GB+ monorepos, ~1% changing daily.

title: Building “Vehicle 360” at Daimler Truck & Bus — How We Find Needles in a 30,000 Parameter Haystack
abstract: Daimler Truck & Bus built “Vehicle 360” to break down organizational silos on a global scale and create one trusted, up‑to‑date view of each vehicle. We combine configuration and production records, sales and aftersales processes, over‑the‑air updates and more than 300 GB of daily vehicle log files to maintain this view across more than 1,000,000 vehicles — each with 30,000+ parameters. On an open lakehouse architecture, Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines keep data fresh and organized, while Unity Catalog provides unified governance and easy sharing. It gives teams one place to see a vehicle’s current state, drill into recent parameter changes, find vehicles with specific characteristics, orchestrate dynamic over‑the‑air updates, and diagnose issues faster. Beyond day‑one wins, this foundation also enables proactive anomaly detection, AI‑driven support and our journey to a software‑defined vehicle.

title: Building a Data Telescope to Study the Vast Expanse of Social Media
abstract: Researchers studying extremism and misinformation need massive social media datasets but face infrastructure and budget constraints. Traditional solutions offer dashboard access to pre-aggregated data, limiting flexibility. Princeton’s Accelerator gives researchers direct Databricks workspace access with pre-built Typical Activity Datasets, enabling custom queries and analysis. We built a multi-tenant data and AI-powered platform serving R1 institutions. Our medallion architecture ingests data via Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines: Bronze captures raw data, Silver applies filtering/text enrichments, and researchers can query via semantic search powered by MLOps. Leveraging Databricks Asset Bundles, REST APIs, and Unity Catalog, we built solutions for cross-workspace monitoring. Users who spent months building scrapers start work in days, querying 100+ languages and discovering content patterns while learning valuable skills. This talk shares our architecture for democratizing data infrastructure with engineering rigor.

abstract: Energy is arguably the most critical industry on earth, and yet the complexity of the processes and the implications of getting it wrong have been barriers to AI adoption, until now. The session will also unpack how Databricks provides the enterprise-ready backbone for Orbital, supporting rapid data ingestion, creation, indexing, model training and more

title: Building a Production: Scale Dimensional Data Mart With Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines and AUTO CDC
abstract: At 84.51˚, we replaced legacy ETL processing in our retail sales data mart with Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines to simplify development while improving reliability at scale. In this session, we’ll walk through how a low-code, declarative approach enables dimensional modeling for both slowly changing dimensions and high-volume fact data. You’ll see how to use AUTO CDC to handle data updates across batch and streaming pipelines, supporting continuously arriving sales transactions alongside rapidly changing product, store and customer attributes. Our ETL crunches approximately 8 million sales transactions and over 80 million purchased items per day in support of our 84.51˚ Stratum platform. Attendees will leave with practical guidance for designing and operating dimensional data marts using Spark Declarative Pipelines, including patterns for CDC, schema evolution, and hybrid batch/streaming workloads that can be applied immediately in production environments.

title: Building Agent-Ready Data: Best Practices for Intelligent Document Processing at Scale
abstract: Roughly 80% of the context that powers your business—invoices, contracts, call transcripts, support tickets—lives in messy, unstructured data and documents. Turning that into a structured data layer is one of the biggest opportunities in your organization: it's what lets you build accurate and reliable agents and analytics on your enterprise's full context. However, when building these massive scale pipelines, going from prototype to production is harder than it looks. Accuracy, cost, and throughput stop being independent dials and become a three-way tradeoff you have to design around. In this session, we'll share the framework and the playbook for winning that tradeoff. We'll show you how to compose AI Functions—Databricks' research-backed, task-specific building blocks for intelligent document processing—into production-ready agentic workflows. You'll learn how to choose the right function for each task, iterate on quality effectively, and tune for cost and throughput at scale. Along the way, we'll demo new features across AI Functions that push what's possible. You'll walk away with a concrete decision framework for building large-scale agentic workflows over unstructured data, plus the best practices to get them into production.

abstract: This hands-on course introduces how to build single-agent, multi-agent, and multi-model systems on Agent Bricks, including key components, architectures, and use cases. You'll learn how to create agent tools using Unity Catalog functions to extend agent capabilities. You'll begin by using Genie to build agents that can interact with structured data, before extending these concepts to create a second agent designed for working with unstructured data and external resources. title: Building Agentic Apps on the Databricks Platform: Architecture, Considerations, and Key Patterns
abstract: Agentic applications are fundamentally different from traditional software: they don't just retrieve data, they reason over it, take actions, and update state in response to the world around them. That makes the database layer a critical design decision, not an afterthought. When agents need to read fresh operational data, write back results, and coordinate across concurrent tasks, the infrastructure underneath determines what's actually possible. This session covers what makes agentic apps so powerful, what can go wrong without the right foundation, and how the Databricks Platform addresses the core requirements. title: Building Agents on Databricks in 90 Minutes: Orchestrating Knowledge, Data, and Reasoning
abstract: Most enterprise AI questions don't fit neatly into one box. "Why did my bill go up?" lives in structured tables. "How do I turn off my hot spot?" lives in product docs and support tickets. Real assistants need both — and the orchestration to know when to use which.In this hands-on lab, you'll build a complete multi-agent customer support system for a fictional telco using Agent Bricks — no deep ML expertise required. You'll stand up a Knowledge Assistant over vector-indexed FAQs and historical tickets, query structured billing and customer data through a Genie space, and wire them together under a Supervisor Agent that intelligently routes every question to the right specialist. Along the way, you'll learn how Unity Catalog governance, vector search, and natural-language instructions combine to turn fragmented data into a single, unified, production-ready assistant — in under 90 minutes.

title: Building AI That Matters: Powering Global Healthcare at The Virtue Foundation
abstract: Ever wonder how The Virtue Foundation connects medical resources with underserved regions? As the first collaboration under Databricks for Good, the foundation partnered with us to build an AI-powered platform improving medical outcomes across 73 countries. This talk breaks down the production Lakehouse architecture behind the system that continuously curates healthcare data to match volunteers with communities in need. What we’ll cover: LLM extraction at scale: Processing 5M+ web pages with OpenAI models via bespoke multimodal pipelines running natively on Spark, reducing cost while improving precision. Data engineering on Spark: Running skewed, multi-terabyte workloads using Spark for parallelism, Photon for performance at scale, and production-grade orchestration. Making data trustworthy: Unifying millions of healthcare facilities through entity resolution. A candid, systems-level look at what it takes to move LLM-powered data extraction from proof of concept to global impact.

title: Building an AI Database for Agentic GTM Operations
abstract: Rippling leverages Databricks to power agentic GTM operations across RevOps, PLG, marketing, sales and account management. Built on Apache Iceberg™-compatible tables and Lakeflow, we ingest and unify large-scale market intelligence data, perform ML-based entity resolution across heterogeneous sources, and apply LLM-driven summarization and classification to generate structured outputs. These enriched profiles power a 360° GTM portal that enables personalized outreach and engagement at scale. Using Databricks AI/BI, we conduct deep performance analysis across campaigns, segments, messaging, and personalization dimensions—closing the loop between intelligence generation and revenue outcomes. We'll dive deep into how Rippling combines scalable data pipelines, interoperable Iceberg storage, AI/BI analytics, evaluation frameworks and generative AI on Databricks to move from fragmented GTM workflows to measurable, agentic operations that drive revenue impact.

title: Building an Explainable AI Research Agent With Databricks Genie
abstract: Forecasting sales at more than 7,000 retail stores generates frequent inquiries into forecast drivers, and traditional methods like driver dashboards or SHAP fail to give field leaders clear narratives. Data scientists were spending days writing ad‑hoc SQL to answer basic “why” questions. In partnership with Databricks, we built an AI/BI Genie-powered Research Agent that delivers fast, plain‑language forecast explanations using governed data. The agent joins core datasets, computes variances and accuracy metrics, correlates key drivers and links every answer to underlying SQL, cutting analysis time from days to minutes and revealing model biases. This session covers how we used Unity Catalog as the semantic backbone and encoded business rules in the Genie Knowledge Store so the agent reasons like a retail analyst. We’ll demo the agent with Deep Research and share key lessons and a repeatable blueprint for operationalizing Genie.

title: Building and Scaling a Multi-Agent App Platform
abstract: How we designed, scaled and shipped a multi‑agent AI app platform for Skuld — built 100% natively on Databricks — and the unified App, AI and data patterns that made it possible. Maritime insurance claims depend on shifting legal facts, mixed‑format case files and strict audit requirements, and standard chunking plus top‑k filtering lost provenance and broke under load. At Skuld, we built a multi‑agent app on Databricks: Lakeflow Jobs runs parsing and enrichment pipelines, Model Serving powers synchronous agent calls, Databricks Apps handles secure user workflows and Unity Catalog governs access end-to-end. The talk dives into our evidence‑first retrieval pattern, where documents become source‑linked fact cards, conflicting facts stay visible for review and agents return exact citations instead of opaque answers. Attendees leave with a hosting decision framework and benchmark data on parsing throughput, queues, token cost, rate limits and latency.

title: Building Autonomous, Always-On Agentic Systems on Databricks
abstract: Agentic commerce could drive up to $1T in retail revenue by 2030, but the real opportunity spans every industry. Most agentic systems today are still reactive, relying on chat prompts. True transformation requires always-on, long-running agents that monitor data, reason through exceptions, and act autonomously.In this session, we’ll walk through how to build asynchronous, event-driven agentic systems on Databricks using a supply chain example. Learn how to move beyond chatbots to resilient, system-to-system workflows by orchestrating Structured Streaming, Model Serving, Lakebase, and Agent Bricks.Key takeaways:• A scalable design pattern for long-running, event-driven agents• Always-on anomaly detection with streaming + ML• Stateful task queuing and high-concurrency routing with Lakebase• Multi-step agent reasoning with tools and safe execution• Evaluation and human-in-the-loop escalation for edge cases

title: Building Better Apps: Architecture Best Practices and Common Patterns on Databricks Apps
abstract: Building a data-driven application is easy; building one that is secure, performant, and scalable is where most teams struggle. This session provides a definitive field guide to the architectural patterns used by the most successful builders on the Databricks App platform. We will break down the ""how-to"" for the most in-demand app categories: Internal Tools, AI Copilots, Agentic Workflows, and Customer-Facing Products. For each pattern, we will dive into the technical specifics that matter most: Connectivity & State: Best practices for integrating with Databricks SQL and Lakebase. Identity & Auth: Implementing On-Behalf-Of (OBO) tokens and service principal delegation to ensure data privacy. Agentic Design: Orchestrating LLMs and tool-calling within a full-stack environment. Performance: Strategies for caching and low-latency UI responses. Join us to learn how to avoid common pitfalls and leverage standardized blueprints to ship better apps.

Designed for data engineers new to Spark Declarative Pipelines, the course provides a comprehensive overview of core components such as incremental data processing, streaming tables, materialized views, and temporary views, highlighting their specific purposes and differences. title: Building End-to-End ML Systems With Genie Code
abstract: Coding agents are transforming how data science teams build and operate machine learning systems. In this session, we'll explore how teams use Genie Code across the ML lifecycle—across EDA, feature engineering, model development, evaluation, deployment, and monitoring. We'll also provide an inside look at how Genie Code was built and optimized for ML workflows. Genie Code understands your data through Unity Catalog and leverages metadata, business semantics, governance policies, and lineage to provide context-aware assistance. Deep integration across the Databricks ML stack enables teams to move faster and work with greater confidence. We'll then look ahead at how Genie Code is evolving from a coding assistant into an agent that can help deploy, serve, and operate ML systems in production. You'll also learn how to customize Genie Code for your ML team through skills and instructions, as well as other tips and tricks to get the most out of Genie Code. Attendees will leave with practical examples of how coding agents are reshaping machine learning and actionable guidance for applying these capabilities to their own ML projects.

title: Building Enterprise Applications with Databricks Apps
abstract: This hands-on course introduces Databricks Apps, a new feature that empowers developers to build and deploy secure data and AI applications directly on the Databricks platform. It is primarily designed for data scientists, data engineers, and developers who need to create custom applications that make data insights accessible to non-technical users within their organizations. The course begins with an overview of the main components of Databricks Apps, followed by the deployment of a simple app using available templates. Next, you will learn how to build and deploy a data-driven application that integrates with other platform features. The course then covers how to set up an IDE for Databricks Apps, and how to edit and deploy an app using an IDE. It concludes with how to implement security and best practices for an enterprise app. Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026.
