description_raw:
This hands-on course introduces Databricks Apps, a new feature that empowers developers to build and deploy secure data and AI applications directly on the Databricks platform. It is primarily designed for data scientists, data engineers, and developers who need to create custom applications that make data insights accessible to non-technical users within their organizations.

 

The course begins with an overview of the main components of Databricks Apps, followed by the deployment of a simple app using available templates. Next, you will learn how to build and deploy a data-driven application that integrates with other platform features. The course then covers how to set up an IDE for Databricks Apps, and how to edit and deploy an app using an IDE. It concludes with how to implement security and best practices for an enterprise app.

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. 

Prerequisites

  • Familiarity with core Databricks components, including workspaces, clusters, SQL warehouses, Unity Catalog, Jobs, and Model Serving

speakers.name: David LeBlanc
speakers.bio: Dave has been a Brickster for the past five years, combining a background in software development with his work as a Curriculum Developer, where he designs and delivers hands-on training across Databricks Apps, governance, platform administration, and AI. As the owner of the Databricks Apps learning pathway, he focuses on helping practitioners build secure, production-ready data and AI applications. His experience also includes implementing and supporting the infrastructure that powers Databricks training environments, giving him a practical perspective on application architecture, governance, and the operational realities of running platforms at scale.

title: Building Enterprise-Scale Agentic Claims Automation and AI Observability With Databricks
abstract: As enterprises move from GenAI experimentation to production, the hardest problems are no longer models or agent frameworks—they are enterprise‑scale orchestration and observability. At Suncorp, we have deployed 16 production‑grade agentic AI solutions that are now converging into an enterprise claims automation capability. This session shares the reference architectures and engineering patterns behind this journey, focusing on two pillars: agentic orchestration, where Databricks supports low‑latency, governed workflows and shared agent memory using Delta Lake, Vector Search, Agent Bricks, and Lakebase, and AI observability at scale, where we use MLflow evaluation, OpenTelemetry, Databricks Apps, and AI/BI Dashboards to trace agent behaviour, decisions, quality and risk. Attendees will leave with practical patterns for building orchestrated, observable agentic AI in a regulated enterprise.

title: Building ETL Pipelines with SQL
abstract: This hands-on course is designed for data professionals who want to explore the data warehousing capabilities of Databricks. Assuming no prior knowledge of Databricks, it provides an introduction to leveraging Databricks as a modern cloud-based data warehousing solution. Learners will explore how use the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform to ingest, transform, govern, and analyze data efficiently. Learners will also explore Genie, an innovative Databricks feature that simplifies data exploration through natural language queries. By the end of this course, participants will be equipped with the foundational skills to implement and optimize a data warehouse using Databricks. Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. Prerequisites Basic SQL proficiency and understanding of data querying concepts General knowledge of data warehousing concepts, including tables, schemas, and ETL/ELT processes Some experience with BI or data visualization tools (recommended but not required)

title: Building Higher Quality Genie Agents (fka Genie spaces): How to Ensure Accuracy and Trust
abstract: High-quality Genie Agents (formerly known as Genie Spaces) are built on a foundation of clear metadata, curated semantics, and continuous iteration. New capabilities make it faster than ever to bootstrap and develop Genie Agents. In this session, we'll show how to design, refine, and scale Genie Agents that consistently deliver accurate, trusted results. Topics include: Using Unity Catalog Business Semantics (Metric Views) improve accuracy and consistency from the start Leveraging Genie Code and knowledge mining to automate space setup How to define metadata and context in the Genie knowledge store How to use evaluation and Benchmarks to measure accuracy and guide improvements Best practices for monitoring and optimizing Genie Agents at scale

title: Building Intelligent Data Discovery with Unity Catalog: Domains and Discover
abstract: As data estates scale across teams and workspaces, governance and discovery must operate at the account level, not just within individual projects. In this session, we’ll explore how Discover Page, Domains, and recommendations in Unity Catalog work together to scale data governance and discovery across the enterprise. You’ll learn how Domains provide a business-aligned governance layer, how Discover Page curates trusted data and insights across the account, and how recommendations leverage metadata, lineage, and usage signals to surface the right data at the right time. We’ll share real customer patterns and practical guidance for building a governed, intelligent discovery experience that grows with your organization.

title: Building Permission-Aware AI for Enterprise Content with LakeFlow Connect
abstract: In this session, we’ll explore how to build scalable, permission-aware AI applications by ingesting files and metadata from Google Drive and SharePoint into Databricks.We’ll examine how LakeFlow Connect ingests structured files (Excel, JSON), semi-structured data, and unstructured documents (PDF, DOCX, and more) from enterprise content systems, while capturing rich metadata and preserving file-level permissions for secure downstream use. You’ll learn how to process change feeds, handle deletes, manage schema evolution, and synchronize access controls, ensuring that AI systems respect enterprise security boundaries without sacrificing performance or scalability. We’ll then showcase how this ingestion foundation powers high-impact GenAI applications, including knowledge assistants and enterprise search with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), transforming distributed enterprise content into governed, AI-ready intelligence that delivers trusted answers and actionable insights.

title: Building Production-Grade SQL ETL on the Lakehouse
abstract: ETL pipelines are often the most brittle part of the analytics stack — spread across tools, written in multiple languages, and hard to operate at scale. This session shows how teams build production-grade SQL ETL on Databricks Lakehouse using a unified, SQL-first approach. We’ll cover how to ingest, transform, and manage data using declarative pipelines, apply governance and quality controls consistently, author and optimize with AI, and deliver reliable datasets directly to analytics and downstream workloads. The focus is on simplifying architecture, reducing operational overhead, and enabling faster iteration without sacrificing correctness or scale.

title: Building Production-Ready Agents with a Self-Evolving Test Suite
abstract: Building agents is challenging. Most teams iterate on agent quality by vibe-checking. Try a question, fix what looks wrong, ship. It works at first and breaks down fast. Each fix can revive an old bug. Coding agents make this worse by rewriting the agent in seconds while verification stays manual.This session introduces a new best practice. With one MLflow command, your coding agent turns into a rigorous builder that grows a test suite from inside the vibe-check loop. Every piece of feedback on a bad answer becomes an automated test. Every coding-agent fix runs against the accumulated suite, scored and recorded in MLflow. By the time your agent is ready to ship, you have a real test suite that grew alongside the build.We walk through this on stage end to end. We start with a prototype agent that has no tracing and no eval, and we end with a production-ready agent backed by a test suite that grew alongside the build.

title: Building Query Expert MCP: Using RAG to Build an Analytics Agent That Goes Beyond Text-to-SQL
abstract: LLMs are fast and confident SQL writers that can unlock self-serve analytics across your business. But actionable insights require more than SQL syntax—they demand business context, domain expertise and nuances that live outside your schema docs. In this talk, we'll deep-dive into how Block built Query Expert MCP, a scalable AI agent that captures and distributes institutional data knowledge using Databricks. You'll learn how we: Automated documentation at scale—using query_ai sub-agents to generate standardized table documentation across 11,000+ tables Captured SQL nuances—Databricks sub-agents categorize and label domain-specific query patterns across 1M sample queries Human in the loop—Databricks Apps allow users to directly edit, remove or upload context to the agent’s memory Enabled intelligent retrieval—Databricks Vector Search indexes for RAG-powered query generation that scales to a 12,000 person org, while supporting domain-specific scoping for teams' use cases

title: Building RAG Agents with Agent Bricks
abstract: This hands-on course teaches you how to build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) agents on Databricks using Agent Bricks’ tooling—including Vector Search, AI Playground, and the Foundation Model APIs. First, you'll begin with prompt engineering and the fundamentals of retrieval and augmented generation. Next, you'll learn how to ingest, process, and prepare documents for use in a retrieval pipeline. Then you'll explore embedding vectors, vector database design, and how to use Vector Search in a Databricks environment. Finally, you will build a retrieval agent end-to-end and trace its behavior using MLflow Tracing for observability and debugging. Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. Prerequisites Familiarity with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, including Unity Catalog Intermediate Python programming experience Basic SQL proficiency for querying and creating functions Familiarity with Generative AI fundamentals, including large language models (LLMs) and prompt engineering Basic knowledge of MLflow

title: Building Reliable Conversational Agents with Genie
abstract: This course teaches you how to design, build, and maintain a Databricks Genie Space, a natural language interface that enables business users to ask questions about governed data and receive SQL-backed answers without writing code. You will learn how Genie fits into the Databricks AI/BI product family and how it translates natural language into reliable SQL queries. The course focuses on what it takes to create a Genie Space that delivers accurate, consistent, and trustworthy results. You will follow a complete end-to-end workflow, from understanding source data and defining benchmarks to configuring and refining a Genie Space using the full set of Knowledge Store curation tools. These include metadata, synonyms, prompt matching, SQL logic, example queries, and text instructions. You will also learn how to share Genie Spaces through Databricks One, understand how Unity Catalog governance is automatically enforced, and use monitoring and user feedback to continuously improve quality over time. By the end of the course, you will be able to create and manage a production-ready Genie Space that delivers governed, self-service conversational analytics at scale. Prerequisites General familiarity with the Databricks workspace - You can navigate the workspace UI, attach compute resources, and run notebooks. Familiarity with Unity Catalog concepts - You understand catalogs, schemas, and tables in Unity Catalog. Prior experience with permissions, tags, or column masks is helpful but not required. Intermediate SQL proficiency - You can read and write SQL queries including SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, and aggregate functions. Access to a Databricks workspace with the Databricks SQL entitlement and CAN USE permission on a serverless SQL warehouse.Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026.

title: Building Search for Agents with Lakebase
abstract: Traditional search breaks under the bursty, concurrent demands of multi-step agents. In this session, learn how to build agent-native search on Postgres that extends pgvector with advanced indexing and first-class BM25, with vector and full-text indexes living right alongside your operational data. The payoff: no brittle app-level joins, just single-statement SQL that fuses vector rankings with structured filters. Watch it scale to zero when idle, burst to billion-vector scale with no performance hit, and branch instantly for sandboxing and A/B testing, all without rebuilding a single index. Then get a first look at what we are building to make Lakebase the foundation for the next generation of AI agents.

title: Building Secure AI-Powered Analytics Experiences Across Organizational Boundaries
abstract: Data sharing between organizations has come a long way — but the next wave is about much more than moving files or granting table access. It's about delivering rich, intelligent experiences to partners, customers, and collaborators while keeping sensitive information protected on both sides. In this talk, we explore how the collaboration landscape is evolving: smarter defaults, stronger privacy guarantees, and AI-powered capabilities that make shared data more useful without increasing risk. You'll hear about the engineering principles behind building privacy-safe collaboration features at scale — balancing openness with control, and convenience with governance. title: Building the Commercial Lakehouse: AI-Driven, Open and Interoperable
abstract: AstraZeneca modernized its Commercial data estate, transitioning from legacy EMR to a high-performance global commercial lakehouse. At the core lies Unity Catalog (UC), established as the unified governance layer. We demonstrate how UC enables a true open architecture, orchestrating seamless federation for legacy Glue workloads and utilizing Iceberg REST integration to provide zero-copy access for iceberg clients e.g., Snowflake. The transformation was powered by a multi-agent AI migration system, utilizing LLMs and testing agents to automate the conversion of 250+ pipelines into a rigorous Medallion architecture. Key components include Databricks Asset Bundles for versioned CI/CD, Liquid Clustering for storage optimization. Processing complex external data sources (Claims, CRM, Digital), this platform delivered 50% cost savings. This session covers the multi-agent migration architecture, UC-centric interoperability design patterns and lessons from modernizing commercial data at scale.

title: Building the Foundation for AI: McKinsey’s Transformation from Legacy to Lakehouse
abstract: As enterprises race to operationalize AI at scale, legacy data warehouses have become a critical bottleneck. In this session, Databricks and McKinsey share proven, real-world best practices for modernizing data platforms to unlock analytics, GenAI and agentic workloads with speed, governance and cost efficiency. Drawing from large scale transformations including McKinsey’s Nebula platform, we outline a pragmatic modernization blueprint that balances risk, payback period and business impact. Attendees will learn how to migrate from brittle legacy architectures to an open lakehouse and federated data mesh, reduce total cost of ownership by up to 40%, accelerate time to insight and enable secure self-service analytics and AI across the enterprise. This talk delivers concrete lessons for executives and practitioners navigating modernization in the AI era.

title: Building With Community Connectors: Custom Data Sources, Managed Reliability
abstract: Are you tired of building fragile, costly API scripts for niche data sources that lack enterprise-grade features like lineage, retries and unified governance? Community Connectors are built on the foundational power of Lakeflow Connect and bridge the gap between "DIY" and “fully managed." These new AI-powered, open-source templates help you build, manage and host your own ingestion paths while inheriting many of the robust, built-in features of the Databricks Platform. In this lightning talk, we’ll explore: Built-in tooling: Use out-of-the-box observability, SCD Type 2 handling, automatic retries and more Flexible customization: Use open-source templates to meet requirements that go beyond standard managed connectors Unified governance: Centrally manage credentials, pipelines, data and lineage via Unity Catalog Join us to get started and learn how they offer the flexibility of a DIY approach with the scale and reliability of a managed Databricks service.

title: Building Your Open Security Lakehouse: Ingest, Normalize, and Model Security Data at Scale
abstract: Many organizations are experimenting with “security data lakes,” but struggle to move from DIY projects to an operational architecture the SOC can live in every day. This session walks through Lakewatch’s reference architecture for an open security lakehouse — how to onboard and unify diverse security, IT, and business telemetry on open storage, normalize it to OCSF, and organize it into bronze, silver, and gold tables optimized for SecOps. We’ll cover ingestion patterns for common data sources, Medallion modeling for security analytics, governance with Unity Catalog, index and search strategies, and how to safely bring in multimodal data like emails and documents. You’ll leave with an opinionated architecture to evaluate or design your own security lakehouse, plus guidance on when to augment versus replace existing SIEM tooling.

title: Built on Databricks: How CMSPI Scaled Payments Routing and Optimization Using Lakebase and DBSQL
abstract: CMSPI built a Databricks-native analytics app that automates payments optimization at enterprise scale — replacing spreadsheets with a governed platform that processes billions of transactions and delivers measurable time and cost savings for global merchants. Lakebase powers real-time scenario configuration, while Delta tables and SQL warehouses enable interactive analytics. Databricks Workflows orchestrate a mathematical solver (PROM) that evaluates billions of routing combinations and returns results in 30–40 minutes — eliminating 30+ hours of manual work per initial analysis and uncovering ~10% incremental savings opportunities. This session shares CMSPI’s path to productization: access control with Entra ID groups, MLOps for approval-rate prediction models and external monetization via Delta Sharing to non-Databricks consumers. The architecture demonstrates the “built on Databricks” pattern for secure, governed apps — with plans to expand collaboration using Databricks Clean Rooms.

title: Buliding ETL Pipelines with SQL
abstract: This hands-on course teaches you how to build production-ready ETL pipelines using pure SQL on the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. You'll learn the declarative building blocks — Streaming Tables, Materialized Views, and AUTO CDC — that replace complex procedural ingestion and transformation logic with concise, incremental, and fully managed pipeline definitions. Following a realistic retail dataset through the medallion architecture, you'll incrementally ingest files with Auto Loader, build pre-computed Silver-to-Gold transformations with incremental refresh, manage SCD Type 1 and Type 2 dimensions with AUTO CDC, and orchestrate the full pipeline using Lakeflow Jobs with SQL File tasks and DAG-based workflows. Prerequisites Navigating the Databricks workspace — sidebar, Catalog Explorer, and SQL Editor Unity Catalog basics — catalogs, schemas, tables, and volumes Intermediate SQL — SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, CAST, COALESCE, CREATE TABLE, and INSERT Data warehousing concepts — fact tables, dimension tables, star schemas, and the medallion architecture Basic understanding of ETL — Extract, Transform, Load workflows and why incremental processing matters Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026.

title: Bulk Metadata Generation To Bring Genie to Life
abstract: Genie benefits significantly from the presence of column metadata. In this talk we will describe the various components that feed into a high-quality Genie space and review some code you can use to populate the base Unity Catalog column metadata in bulk. The code makes use of customizable prompts and optional data sampling to produce high-quality metadata across entire schemas or even catalogs.

title: Cache Smarter, Not Harder: Building a Semantic Cache Gateway with Lakebase and MLflow
abstract: As LLM applications move into production, redundant calls quietly drive up latency, cost, and complexity. Traditional caching falls short — exact string matches miss the majority of real-world queries where users ask the same question in different ways.In this session, we introduce semantic caching: a smarter approach that retrieves responses based on intent, not syntax. You'll learn how to build a production-ready semantic cache gateway using Lakebase and MLflow to capture paraphrased and context-aware queries. We'll walk through why exact-match caching breaks down at scale, how to design a low-latency caching layer with a FastAPI gateway on Databricks Apps, and how to incorporate conversational context for multi-turn accuracy — plus the observability and governance patterns that make it production-safe.Walk away with a deployable architecture and proven patterns to cut LLM costs by up to 80% while improving response speed and reliability.

title: Cascading Failures in Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Evaluating multi-agent systems requires a fundamental shift in perspective: we are no longer just testing model outputs, but the integrity of the coordination layer. Instead of just getting one bad response, we get a complex palette of hidden — and not-so-hidden — issues like poisoned shared memory, sub-optimal decision patterns and distributed hallucinations. In this session, we’ll cover how to identify these glitches with MLflow observability, how to move from passive monitoring to active intervention, and which Databricks components can actually prevent the chaos from happening in the first place. The goal of this talk isn't to give you a recipe for every possible disaster, but to broaden your thinking in a world where agents are becoming more autonomous — and significantly more creative with their mistakes.

title: Centene: The Gifts of the MAGI: Delivering Secure, Repeatable, and Explainable AI
abstract: For enterprises in regulated industries, scaling agentic AI requires more than policy—it demands runtime governance. Centene, in partnership with Databricks and Slalom, built MAGI (Machine Agentic Governed Intelligence), a production framework that delivers three essential gifts: Security that enforces compliance and protects PHI by default, Explainability via immutable audit trails for every AI decision, and Repeatability through a governed "paved road" for consistent AI development. We'll demonstrate how MAGI's composable architecture uses automated evaluation, quality gates, centralized monitoring, and feedback loops to accelerate safe AI adoption at scale. This approach has given Centene the consistency and confidence to grow its AI portfolio across the enterprise. Leave with practical patterns for building your own runtime governance for agentic AI on Databricks.

title: Classic to Serverless: An Agentic Migration Playbook for Python and Scala
abstract: Moving real workloads from classic to serverless compute can mean dozens of small changes: Spark configs that no longer apply, init scripts that need rethinking, Scala and JAR jobs, and pipelines tied to specific runtime versions. Doing this by hand across hundreds of Jobs and Notebooks does not scale. This session is a hands-on practitioner's guide to migrating Notebooks, Jobs, and Pipelines to serverless, with a focus on the new agentic tooling that automates most of the work. We walk through concrete examples covering Python and Scala/JAR workloads, show how the migration agent inspects code, classifies incompatibilities, and proposes fixes, and demonstrate how to validate the result before promoting the change. Attendees leave with a repeatable migration playbook, a clear view of what is fully automated today versus where a human stays in the loop, and a sense of which workloads are ready to move now.

title: Clean, Correct Change Data Capture with Spark Declarative Pipelines
abstract: Learn how to construct clean, correct, cost-conscious CDC pipelines that conquer chaotic change, column creep and complicated SCD calculations. Today, implementing CDC typically means writing complex, expensive merge logic. Handling straightforward cases is manageable — but complexity escalates quickly when you introduce out-of-order data, duplicates, schema evolution and slowly changing dimensions. What works in development often breaks under real production conditions. Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP) addresses this with Auto CDC, a declarative API that abstracts away merge orchestration and correctness guarantees. Instead of implementing imperative patterns, you declare intent — such as applying SCD Type 2 — and SDP executes it with built-in consistency, incremental processing and resilience. In this session, we’ll walk through the Auto CDC API, examine how it automates complex merge operations and show how declarative CDC improves reliability across batch and streaming workloads.

title: Closing the Agent Quality Loop Through Observability in Production
abstract: You built an agent. It passed dev testing and shipped. But production is a different world, and now the real work begins: proving it stays high quality and making it better with every release. This session walks the agent quality loop end to end on Databricks with MLFlow, from the seat of the AI Ops engineer supporting a production agent. We start with tracing and observability: real-time trace logging into Unity Catalog, out-of-the-box LLM judges, and a review app for SME labeling. We turn that human feedback into trustworthy, scalable evaluation by aligning LLM judges to users' corrections. We surface problems through automated issue detection that opens trackable bugs, then feed production traffic into larger, more targeted evaluation sets as a CI gate, and ship repeatably with Declarative Automation Bundles. In the end, we are left with an Agent flywheel that de-risks the upcoming releases and discovers problems in existing ones. Through this session, we demonstrate this whole loop live on a real composite agent.

title: Coding with AI Agents to Supercharge Your Spark UDFs with GPU-Acceleration
abstract: NVIDIA cuDF enables GPU-accelerated query execution for Apache Spark workloads. However, a common performance bottleneck for vectorized query engines are User-Defined Functions (UDFs). Since UDFs contain opaque custom code, the engine must fall back to row-at-a-time execution. We present a new set of agents skills in Project Aether to convert Spark UDFs into GPU-compatible implementations: either native SQL expressions or GPU UDFs invoking cuDF or CUDA primitives. The agent reasons through tasks in an end-to-end workflow: 1) generating CPU-behavior tests, 2) producing a GPU implementation, 3) running benchmarks, and 4) profiling and optimizing performance, with correctness verified through iterative feedback loops. By transforming UDFs to run on GPUs, agents enable full query acceleration for the cuDF plugin, RAPIDS Accelerator for Apache Spark, unlocking significant 20x+ UDF speedups. In this session we will go into the practical learnings from building an AI agent for Spark.

title: Comprehensive Data Warehouse Migrations With Lakebridge
abstract: Lakebridge is Databricks' free, AI-powered solution for migrating legacy data warehouses to the Lakehouse. Migrating from a legacy warehouse means confronting decades-old code, converting proprietary dialects, and reconciling bespoke differences between source and target systems. With Lakebridge, AI agents handle that automatically. We'll show how Lakebridge uses Genie Code to accelerate the migration lifecycle: Assessment: analyze legacy code automatically to surface complexity, dependencies, and risk before work begins Conversion: Use agents to convert proprietary dialects into open ANSI SQL, automatically validating syntax and semantic intent Data Migration: Use LakeFlow Connect to replicate data from a wide range of sources, either as a one-time snapshot or incremental change capture Reconciliation: easily identify discrepancies between source and target systems With Lakebridge, migrations are faster to scope, easier to deliver, and no longer dependent on expensive manual workflows.

Hear from brands already shipping Lakebase-powered apps, and leave with a repeatable framework for turning lakehouse intelligence into the tools your frontline teams actually use.

title: Cost Management for Serverless Compute: Notebooks, Jobs, and Pipelines
abstract: Serverless compute removes infrastructure overhead, but platform teams still need to govern who can use it and how much each workload can spend. This session covers the cost-control model now for serverless Notebooks, Jobs, and Lakeflow Pipelines, current features, recent developments, and the roadmap ahead.We walk through the new primitives: entitlements that grant or revoke serverless access per user, group, or service principal, and per-workload rate limits that cap the spend rate of an individual Job or Pipeline. Attendees leave with a concrete migration path from cluster policies to serverless cost controls.

title: Creating Better Travel Experiences for All — Confronting Airline Pricing Pressures From Legacy Tools
abstract: easyJet carried nearly 90 million passengers last year, flying more than 1,200 routes, with a fleet of 300+ planes. Even as one of Europe’s leading low-cost airlines, the company faced mounting pressure to modernize, as traveler expectations necessitate seamless booking, flexible changes and personalized offers. Across Europe, high costs, thin margins and digital-first competitors only raised the stakes for all airlines. With core systems still tied to a decade-old desktop app and one of the region’s largest SQL Server databases, easyJet struggled with frequent engineering bottlenecks, fragmented workflows and more. Moving to the Databricks Platform helped the airline consolidate their commercial tools into a single hub and cut deployment timelines from up to nine months to three — a pace shift that put innovation back on track for easyJet.

title: Cross-Cloud Delta Sharing: Eliminate Egress cost with Delta Sharing Global Distribution
abstract: Cross-cloud and cross-region data sharing introduces egress costs that grow with recipient query volume, creating a scaling challenge for large-scale data providers. This session covers best practices for architecting cost-efficient Delta Sharing deployments across clouds and regions, and introduces a new Databricks capability designed to change how providers manage cross-cloud/region delivery at scale.

title: Customer Zero: How Databricks' Own Finance Team Runs on Databricks
abstract: The most credible proof of a platform's power is how the company that built it uses it to run its own business. Databricks' Office of the CFO has gone all-in on the Databricks platform to unify transactional data from ERP, CRM, HRIS, and planning systems into a single, governed source of financial truth, eliminating the 'which number is right?' debate that costs enterprises countless hours in every close cycle. In this fast-paced, demo-forward lightning talk, you'll see how Genie and AI/BI enable natural language financial analytics and forecasting, how Unity Catalog ensures SOX compliance and audit readiness, and how RowZero enables seamless data ingestion from spreadsheets into governed pipelines without disrupting the workflows finance teams already use. If your CFO or finance team is still living in spreadsheets, this talk demonstrates what it looks like when finance becomes a first-class data organization. Expect less theory, more demo.

title: Customer Zero: How Retool Scaled 1 Million Databases on Databricks Lakebase
abstract: Learn how Retool, an enterprise AppGen platform for building intelligent applications and agents, became an early adopter of Databricks Lakebase, creating over 1 million serverless Postgres databases to power its operational foundation. title: Cybersecurity Forum | Sponsored by: Deloitte
abstract: In the AI era, security is fundamentally a data problem. As cyberattacks shift from human-operated to machine-scale autonomous agents, traditional security architectures have hit a breaking point, forced into a "fidelity trade-off" between spiraling costs and dangerous visibility gaps. Join us for the Cybersecurity Industry Forum to discover how Databricks is disrupting the legacy SIEM market with Lakewatch, the industry’s first open, agentic SIEM built on the security lakehouse. This 90-minute session explores how to “fight fire with fire” by deploying swarms of defensive AI agents to meet machine-speed attackers. We will dive into the architectural shift required to unify security, IT, and business data into a single, governed environment, eliminating the “ingestion tax” and enabling petabyte-scale detection and response at a fraction of the cost of legacy providers. Hear from security innovators and Lakewatch design partners who are moving beyond experimental AI to operationalize agentic security at scale. Learn how to leverage open formats (OCSF) and “Detection-as-Code” to build a proactive, high-velocity SOC that identifies threats in minutes, not days.

abstract: Nonprofits are tackling some of society’s most urgent challenges, but many are constrained by limited budgets, fragmented data, and limited technical capacity. In this session, we will share how Databricks for Good helps mission-driven organizations overcome these barriers through nonprofit pricing, technical enablement, and hands-on support from Databricks experts. Attendees will learn how nonprofits can use the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform to unify data, strengthen analytics foundations, explore responsible AI, and turn information into insights that support better decisions and greater mission impact. Attendees will leave with a practical playbook for how nonprofits can get started with Databricks and accelerate meaningful, measurable social impact.

title: Data Governance at Scale
abstract: This hands-on course equips learners with hands-on expertise to implement robust, enterprise-scale data governance in Databricks using Unity Catalog. Implement access control at scale with ABAC, enable comprehensive observability and auditing, monitor and assure data quality, visualize and manage complete data and model lineage, and effectively track usage, costs, and data quality across your platform. Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. Prerequisites Familiarity with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, including workspaces, notebooks, and basic cloud concepts Intermediate SQL experience, including creating and managing tables, views, and functions, and granting/revoking privileges Working knowledge of data governance concepts, including access control, security policies, and fine-grained techniques such as row-level filters and column masking Understanding of Unity Catalog's object model (metastore, catalogs, schemas, tables, volumes, functions, models) and basic data lineage principles Basic awareness of metadata management and data discovery practices

title: Data Governance at Scale with ABAC at Atlassian
abstract: Atlassian’s internal data platform is the backbone for analytics, product insights and business decisions across the company. Managing data access policies at this scale is complex. In this talk, we’ll share how Atlassian embeds robust data governance policies, balancing agility with compliance, and innovation with security. Learn how we handle access management, data classification, and policy enforcement across diverse teams and tools. A key part of our approach is leveraging Databricks Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) to manage and abstract complex business policies. ABAC enables us to flexibly enforce fine-grained access controls (FGAC) using data tagging along with tag-driven policies, adapting quickly to changing requirements while keeping implementation logic abstracted from users. Join us for insights into the challenges, lessons learned, and solutions that keep our data platform secure and well-governed.

title: Data Intelligence for SaaS Threat Hunting: How Obsidian uses Databricks at scale
abstract: Security teams are overwhelmed by fragmented SaaS logs, identity signals, and investigation workflows spread across tools. Obsidian Security unifies SaaS security telemetry across cloud apps and identity providers to detect real-world threats like account takeover, suspicious OAuth activity, and insider risk.In this session, Damien Miller-McAndrews (Threat Researcher, Obsidian Security) shares how Obsidian leverages the Databricks Lakehouse to accelerate threat investigations using anonymized, high-volume security telemetry stored in a unified Databricks data lake. He investigates how attackers combine SaaS abuse, identity compromise, and social engineering into fast-moving breaches, and develops detection strategies to help teams respond faster to account takeovers, OAuth abuse, and anomalous access across enterprise SaaS environments. He brings a practitioner’s perspective to threat hunting and regularly shares research and practical insights to help security and IT teams better protect their organizations.

title: Data Interoperability with Unity Catalog
abstract: This hands-on course explores how to achieve seamless data interoperability between systems using Databricks Unity Catalog as a unified governance layer, using both Delta and Iceberg open table formats. Participants will learn to implement, manage and optimize a data environment where tables can be accessed by both Delta and Iceberg clients, enabling cross platform analytics and eliminating data silos. title: Data Privacy at Databricks
abstract: Handling PII and sensitive data is a top priority, especially for the platform storing the world’s data. We will show how we use Unity Catalog’s fine-grained access controls, dynamic masking and attribute-based access control (ABAC) to enforce GDPR and CCPA compliance internally. See how we ensure data utility for our engineers without ever compromising on privacy.

title: Databricks Apps: A Magic Wand for Driving Data Quality Adoption and Observability
abstract: Most data quality tools don’t fail because the checks are wrong. They fail because users don’t understand how to use them.In this talk, we’ll share how we rebuilt our internal data quality platform using Databricks Apps and Databricks Workflows table triggers to prioritize usability and holistic visibility. We moved away from a config-file-driven model owned by a small group of platform engineers toward a user-centric approach that empowers teams to create, test and manage their own data quality rules. With a Databricks App as the central interface, users can define and test rules, inspect production run history, and track data quality trends across the tables and teams they own. Combined with table-triggered workflows, checks run automatically as data changes without added operational complexity.This session covers our architecture, key design decisions, and lessons learned, and shows how Databricks Apps can turn data infrastructure into a user-friendly platform.

title: Databricks FinOps Genie — Cost Observability Meets Optimization Insights
abstract: We will showcase Databricks FinOps Genie, a cost observability and optimization capability that combines a Databricks‑native FinOps dashboard, Genie space and FinOps agent, proven at scale across 1,000+ workspaces in a large bank. Learn how to turn Databricks usage and billing data into a lightweight, reusable cost intelligence layer that surfaces key drivers of spend, anomalies and optimization opportunities through a single dashboard. See how a Genie space lets users “talk” to their FinOps data in natural language and receive detailed explanations and recommendations. Take home patterns for using a FinOps agent and recommendation model to right‑size clusters, address anomalous workloads and enable teams on Databricks FinOps best practices, so you can apply the same approach in your own estate.

title: Databricks on Databricks: Automating Service Reliability at Scale
abstract: Rapid product delivery makes service reliability a core engineering challenge. This talk shows how we use Databricks on Databricks to build production systems that automate reliability detection and investigation for user-facing services.I’ll cover 2 systems. KPI Miss Auto-Investigator automates KPI regression analysis by detecting dips, ranking error contributors, computing customer blast radius, and syncing annotations across team and global dashboards. Built with Databricks Jobs and ETL pipelines with inter-job dependencies, it cuts on-call investigation time by 67%.User Error Anomaly Detection is a Databricks-based system for logging, detection, and monitoring. User error logs are ingested via Zerobus into Delta tables, analyzed by Jobs using Asset Bundles, and monitored through SQL Alerts and AI/BI dashboards. The system detects incidents up to 3 hours before customer reports, reducing discovery time by 95% and customer impact by 90%, with 95% recall and 98% precision.

title: Decathlon’s Race to Unified Governance: Securing Interoperability at Scale
abstract: Decathlon, operating in 70+ countries, aims to make wellbeing accessible through sport. Scaling to thousands of tables strained our legacy metadata management (AWS Glue). Moving to Unity Catalog (UC) unified governance for 2,000+ users but created a key challenge: How to centralize governance within the Databricks Lakehouse while maintaining interoperability with external engines? This session details Decathlon’s migration from AWS Glue to Unity Catalog, focusing on how we ensured "openness" so that external engines—EMR, Athena, Polars, DuckDB—remain compatible and performant under UC. We will share the framework used to automate the transition of thousands of tables and present metrics on improved metadata rendering speeds and streamlined platform administration.

title: Deep Dive Into Streaming and Batch ETLs With Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines
abstract: Let's deep dive into the new declarative ETL pipeline framework in Apache Spark™, Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP). Let's peel it off to learn how SDP's high-level Python and SQL abstractions translate into lower-level Spark SQL and Spark Structured Streaming queries. During the talk, you will learn how SDP automatically resolves complex dependencies and builds optimized Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) for both batch and streaming workloads. We will walk through the internal state management and orchestration logic that allows SDP to handle retries and incremental processing out of the box, replacing thousands of lines of imperative "glue code." You will leave with a clear mental model of the engine's architecture, the pros and cons of SDP, and be ready to debug and optimize your pipelines. You'll understand where and how to use it (alongside your existing ETL pipelines).

title: Deep Dive Into Streaming on Databricks
abstract: A factory detects an equipment anomaly and needs the alert in seconds. A financial platform needs to process a transaction, enrich it with account history, and flag it for fraud—all before the customer closes the app. These workloads both involve streaming data, but they have very different requirements under the hood. This session introduces the two core streaming capabilities on Databricks, Real-Time Mode and Zerobus Ingest, and how to match them to your workload. Real-Time Mode on Apache Spark™ Structured Streaming is for when data needs to be acted upon, not just stored. With sub-second, event-driven computation and expressive stateful processing via TransformWithState, it's the right choice for operational workloads where latency directly affects business outcomes: live betting platforms, ad attribution pipelines, fraud detection, and real-time personalization. Zerobus Ingest is a Kafka-free ingestion capability that lets applications and devices write event data directly into Delta Lake, no message broker, no compute overhead, governed delivery out of the box. It's designed to move data fast and at scale. It does not process or transform data in flight, and for ingestion-heavy workloads, that's exactly the right tradeoff. We'll contrast both tools, walk through a workload decision framework, and show you when to use each, and how to chain them together for end-to-end real-time data flow on Databricks.

title: Delta + Iceberg, Better Together
abstract: For years, Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg co-evolved as parallel standards. That era is ending. This session goes deep on the technical “how” of this convergence. We first walk through Apache Iceberg v4’s adaptive metadata tree: what is changing in the redesign and how the new structure enables single-file commits to significantly accelerate performance. We then cover how Delta Lake 5.0 adopts the Iceberg v4 metadata tree as its native content metadata. This produces a single on-disk structure that both Delta and Iceberg clients read and write directly. No translation layers, no conversion overhead. Just one format.

title: Delta Kernel <> Catalog-Managed Tables
abstract: With the introduction of Catalog-Managed Tables, Delta Lake has unlocked unified governance, enforceable constraints, and a path towards multi-table updates.As a result, Delta connectors must adapt to properly load, read, and write Delta Tables, as the Catalog is now the authoritative broker of commits, not the filesystem.In this talk, learn how we designed Catalog Managed Tables support in Delta Kernel—the one right Delta abstraction to rule them all. We’ve built a unified catalog-agnostic API against which connectors can develop, enabled deep and powerful engine integrations for DuckDB, Delta-Spark, and Delta-Flink, all while keeping the complexity of catalog support out of Kernel.

title: Delta Sharing SecureConnect: Simplify Network Configuration for External Data Collaboration
abstract: As Delta Sharing deployments scale to more recipients, managing per-recipient IP allowlists and allowing direct storage access becomes a significant operational burden. It can also be a blocker for data providers that want to keep their storage hidden behind firewalls. This session covers how Delta Sharing SecureConnect addresses this problem by introducing a Databricks-managed network intermediary that proxies storage access on behalf of recipients. Providers perform a one-time network configuration regardless of the number of recipients. SecureConnect then handles routing across AWS, Azure, and GCP without requiring storage to be exposed to the public internet. We'll cover the architecture, cloud-specific configuration patterns, and how SecureConnect offers private and simple data sharing at scale.

Delta Sharing provides the industry’s most widely adopted open protocol for the secure, real-time exchange of the datasets and AI assets required for modern innovation. We’ll dive deep into: Fueling AI With Openness: How to share live data, volumes and AI models with any recipient—regardless of their platform—to accelerate model training and deployment. title: Deploying and Monitoring Agents on Databricks
abstract: This hands-on course guides you through deploying and monitoring agentic AI systems in the Databricks environment. You will start by learning how to deploy agents in batch mode using AI Functions and integrate them into data pipelines. Next, you'll explore real-time deployment using Model Serving, including deploying agents as REST endpoints and managing autoscaling, versioning, and governance via Mosaic AI Model Serving. You'll then turn to observability and monitoring, using MLflow tracing and scoring functions to capture metrics, analyze requests and responses, and detect anomalies in production. Finally, you'll learn best practices for deploying agents with built-in trace collection, inference logging, and feedback loops to support ongoing evaluation and robustness. Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. Prerequisites Familiarity with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, including Unity Catalog and Delta Lake Intermediate Python programming experience Familiarity with Generative AI fundamentals, including LLMs, RAG architectures, and prompt engineering Familiarity with Databricks Asset Bundles (DABs) Basic SQL proficiency, including use of functions like ai_query Basic understanding of MLOps/LLMOps principles and software deployment concepts, including CI/CD pipelines, REST APIs, and YAML configuration

title: Designing Agentic Systems Reliable Enough for Production
abstract: Most agents don't fail in production because the model is bad. They fail because the system around the model has no guardrails, no structure, and no way to see what's happening. In this session I'll make the case that reliability is an engineering problem, not a prompting one. I'll walk through the harness every production agent needs: control flow, a real plan, execute, observe, and replan design, and observability you can act on. I'll back it with production failures we've all seen and a benchmark where the same model went from 20% to 60%+ just by changing the system. You'll leave with a pre-deploy checklist: the blocks to include, and the ones most teams forget.

title: Designing beautiful, effective dashboards: Best practices for visual story telling in AI/BI
abstract: A great dashboard isn’t just fast and accurate. It’s intuitive, engaging, and easy to act on. Yet many fall short, cluttered with too many visuals, unclear layouts, and designs that don’t translate across devices.AI/BI Dashboards make it easier to build polished, interactive experiences, but strong design still depends on thoughtful choices around layout, hierarchy, and usability. title: Designing Data Models and Architectures
abstract: This practitioner-focused course is a deep dive into designing data models within the Databricks Lakehouse. The course explores three leading data warehousing approaches — Inmon's Corporate Information Factory, Kimball's dimensional modeling, and Data Vault 2.0 — and shows how each maps to the medallion architecture. Participants will also learn how to extend these foundations to modern use cases such as data products for scalable, governed data sharing across domains. title: Designing for Agents: A New Playbook for AI-Native Product Experiences
abstract: For 30 years, we’ve designed software around a human who needed to be in the driver’s seat — navigating menus, configuring pipelines, running queries. That human is leaving the driver’s seat.In this session, we explore what happens to product design when AI agents become the primary users of your platform. We’ll look at real workflows being disrupted across industries — from legal to design to data engineering — and introduce the Levels of AI Autonomy framework (L0–L5), a practical tool for aligning product and engineering teams on how much the AI should do versus the human.You’ll leave with a concrete playbook for deciding when to build a UI, when to get out of the agent’s way, and how to design the trust and control surfaces that make agentic experiences actually work.

title: Detecting and Reducing Manipulative AI Outputs With Interpretable Governance Signals
abstract: Large language models are increasingly embedded in data platforms and decision workflows, yet they can generate manipulative and propagandistic content at scale, often without obvious policy violations. In this talk, I present a production-oriented approach to detecting and mitigating manipulation in generative AI systems using interpretable, data-driven signals. Drawing on real-world pipelines I’ve built, I show how manipulative techniques can be operationalized as measurable indicators within AI evaluation workflows. I demonstrate how these signals can be used to monitor model behavior, compare outputs across model versions, and guide alignment strategies that significantly reduce harmful generation while preserving utility. This session focuses on how to integrate responsible AI checks into data pipelines, how to reason about governance beyond binary safety flags, and how interpretable metrics enable more trustworthy AI systems at scale.

title: Diagnosing Performance Bottlenecks in Databricks Lakehouse
abstract: In complex analytics environments, performance issues are rarely isolated — and surface-level tuning often misses the real bottleneck. This deep dive session presents an advanced framework for diagnosing performance problems in Databricks Lakehouse, grounded in how the engine executes queries at scale. We’ll walk through how to distinguish query-level inefficiencies from data layout issues, concurrency pressure, and system-level constraints, and how to interpret execution plans and runtime signals to identify the true root cause. Attendees will leave with a repeatable diagnostic approach they can apply to large, multi-tenant production workloads and examples of using AI to assist in finding and resolving your performance bottlenecks.

title: Ditch the Message Bus with Zerobus Ingest
abstract: Streaming is evolving—quickly. Modern architectures are eliminating infrastructure sprawl in favor of a direct-to-lakehouse model, eliminating the need for intermediate message buses and the expense of maintaining them. Zerobus Ingest allows you to push data directly to the lakehouse with near real-time writes, high throughput, and support for thousands of concurrent clients. In this demo-packed session, we’ll cover: How Zerobus works and how to build production-ready pipelines—without the heavy ownership costs of DIY infrastructure. The latest supported interfaces (e.g., REST, OTel, and Kafka-compatible APIs), as well as new features designed for massive scale (e.g., liquid clustering, JSON variant type support, etc.). See how global innovators like Joby Aviation and Toyota Motor Corporation have embraced this shift to streamline their real-time architectures. Join us and discover a direct ingestion framework to simplify your stack and accelerate your impact.

title: Doubling Medical Safety: Fine-Tuning Open LLMs for Women's Health Without Human Labels
abstract: Enterprises building LLM features in healthcare hit the same wall: satisfying dozens of safety rules simultaneously—crisis escalation, treatment boundaries, referral language—while real user data is off-limits and expert labeling is prohibitively expensive. We'll show how Flo Health broke through using RFT-inspired synthetic fine-tuning, transforming Llama 3.3 70B into a healthcare-compliant assistant for women's health that doubled safety compliance versus our previous iteration. The key insight: instead of investing expert time in labeling, we redirected it into designing LLM judges that scale. Our system uses 60 LLM judges—52 for medical safety, 8 for usefulness—with priority-weighted reward aggregation where P1 safety rules dominate over P2 quality rules. You'll learn patterns for multi-judge evaluation systems, reward aggregation strategies for binary constraints, and why simpler approaches beat complex alternatives. For anyone building AI where "mostly safe" isn't good enough.

title: Dr. Jekyll and Mr. H-AI-de: Using MLflow and AI Judges to measure model alignment and safety
abstract: Emergent misalignment sent shockwaves through the AI community in 2025. We discovered that a model fine-tuned on narrow tasks could suddenly pivot from a "helpful tool" into a "rogue actor." In early 2026, Nature warned that mistrained models "quickly go off the rails," making AI safety a non-negotiable for enterprise innovation. To build with confidence, we must move beyond blind trust toward empirical control.In this 20-minute lightning talk, we will demystify the process of assessing model integrity. We'll walk through the practical steps to:- Build custom judges designed to detect latent misalignment and goal-drift.- Deploy judges in MLflow to automate the evaluation of frontier open-source models.- Benchmark against emerging standards like HarmBench to quantify operational risk.Learn how to stay in control and inherently understand the internal "compass" of your models. The last thing your enterprise needs is an assistant that turns into a monster the moment you look away.

title: Duct Tape to Databricks: 3 Years of Brickbot at Data & AI Summit
abstract: Brickbot started as a simple chatbot hacked together for DAIS 2024. DuckDB in memory, parquet files in git and a prayer that Heroku wouldn't go down. At DAIS 2025 we improved it with tool calling and direct integration with RainFocus, but it was still mostly cobbled together. Now, for DAIS 2026, we've rebuilt it entirely on Databricks with no custom infrastructure, using Agent Bricks, Vector Search, Databricks Apps, Lakebase, UC Functions as MCP tools and Lakeflow. This talk traces that journey, the lessons learned shipping an AI app to 30,000 conference attendees, and how the Databricks' platform evolved alongside it.

title: Effective document management and retrieval for generative AI
abstract: Building production RAG systems requires far more than embedding documents. This 90-minute deep dive covers the complete technical pipeline: document structuring principles, semantic vs. fixed-size chunking tradeoffs, contextual and multi-modal embeddings, and advanced retrieval optimization, accompanied by practical implementation on Databricks. We'll demonstrate a real-world Databricks RAG pipeline covering pre-processing at scale, embedding optimization and advanced retrieval techniques—including re-ranking, contextual filtering and real-time quality evaluation. Beyond retrieval, we showcase how Agent Bricks transforms RAG systems into autonomous, agentic applications capable of multi-step reasoning and complex tasks. The session also explores emerging trends—vision-space retrieval, contextual clustering and real-time quality assurance—critical for production systems where accuracy directly impacts outcomes.

title: Embracing Serverless SQL at Riot Games
abstract: At Riot Games, we found that embracing serverless compute—rather than limiting it—allowed us to scale more effectively while improving performance, governance and user experience. In this session, we’ll share Riot’s shift from a cost-first mindset to an enablement-driven approach using Databricks SQL Serverless, with Unity Catalog as a key enabler. Consistent governance, lineage and usage visibility gave us the confidence to adopt serverless while maintaining transparency and accountability. We’ll explore how serverless SQL warehouses support diverse analytics and reporting needs through strong performance, simplified user experiences and elastic, on-demand cost efficiency. We’ll also discuss how serverless compute streamlined the data engineering lifecycle by reducing infrastructure management. Finally, we’ll cover Riot’s broader adoption of serverless for jobs and general workloads, the resulting operational and cost benefits, and how we manage costs in a serverless-first model.

title: Emotional Congruence at Scale: Using Databricks AI to Align Ads and Content
abstract: TV advertisers know context matters, but most contextual signals stop at coarse attributes like genre or keywords. What about emotion? What we watch shapes how we feel—and how we feel influences how we engage with brands. At NBCUniversal, we built an Emotional Congruence engine to quantify whether alignment between these emotional signals drives intent and conversion—and how to scale it using Databricks. Using foundation models served on Databricks, we extract and summarize unstructured signals from content and ads, tagging each with a standardized emotional taxonomy across themes, tones and personal values. Governed end-to-end with MLflow 3.0, the system is orchestrated for rigorous testing and deployment. Testing shows emotional alignment drives measurable lift—often in the double digits. As a result, it is now embedded within NBCUniversal’s broader contextual advertising offering.

title: Empowering Non-Technical Users in Pharma With Dashboards and Chatbots Working Together in Databricks
abstract: The presentation shows how Databricks enables non‑technical users in pharma to gain scientific insights by uniting dashboards, chatbots, documents and data. The foundation is data and documents from source systems organized in Unity Catalog and a semantic layer of schemas, tables with definitions, metrics views with business logics, keys linking datasets, SQL functions, Genie and Agent Bricks. Clinical study data is complex, with interpretation depending on context often described in documents. We use a dashboard for context, with visuals and filters conveying the overarching story, while Genie and Agent Bricks offer insights via natural-language questions. Traditional dashboards excel at data storytelling but lack flexibility and tends to grow into overwhelming complexity, by adding context-aware chatbots we address these challenges. Insights can also be embedded into platforms like Teams and SharePoint, ensuring easy access, while having data and calculations centrally governed.

title: Enabling a Low-Latency Data Mesh at Warner Music Group Using Lakebase, Iceberg and Unity Catalog
abstract: Today’s enterprises face daunting challenges when creating impact with data, from fundamental trust issues to dynamically evolving AI use cases. Legacy systems with technical debt impede business value even as users expect trustworthy, low-latency insights for both natural language queries and classic insights. Furthermore, pipelines are often distributed across different engines. This environment demands a flexible approach to drive impact that brings cohesion to an often-messy data environment. This session describes how WMG Tech leveraged Databricks to develop a declarative data platform that realizes a compositional data mesh designed to tackle this challenge. This architecture includes: Iceberg as an engine agnostic data layer for access to diverse sources Unity Catalog for compositional access to data products Lakebase for native low latency analytical APIs Together, this platform enables an array of data products that serve AI queries and WMG's applications.

title: Enabling Evolutionary Database Development with Database Branching
abstract: This talk builds on the foundations of Evolutionary Database Design, applying the framework of Values, Principles, Methods, Practices, and Tools to a revolutionary capability: database branching.In 1999, Thoughtworks pioneered evolutionary design out of necessity, leading to modern standards like migrations and tools such as Flyway and Liquibase. However, despite improvements in testing and automation, teams still lacked the ability to branch databases as easily as code.Lakebase changes this. Its copy-on-write technology creates a full-fidelity, governance-aware production clone in roughly one second, regardless of size, with zero initial storage.Kevin and Pramod will demonstrate how database branching transforms workflows:* Self-Sufficiency: Enabling teams to be more productive and autonomous.* Collaboration: Shifting the DBA from a "gatekeeper" to a design contributor.* Innovation: Empowering teams to run unlimited experiments to find optimal solutions.

The AI-Powered Practice will bring powerful AI assistants to automate the entire medical practice including clinical, billing, front-office & patient engagement. Discover how ModMed, through purposeful collaboration with Databricks, is leading the charge in vertical AI in transforming healthcare operations, reducing provider burnout and elevating the human connection in medicine with visionary, cutting-edge AI.

title: Enterprise AI at Scale: Serving Google Gemini on Databricks for Production Workloads
abstract: Foundation models are moving beyond chatbots and copilots into the core of enterprise data pipelines — enriching records, classifying documents, resolving entities, and powering agentic workflows at massive scale. This session shows how Google Gemini and Databricks are partnering to make this real for production enterprises today. Google Cloud shows how Gemini is available as a first-party model on Databricks, served natively via ai_query() and Model Serving — with built-in governance via AI Gateway, including cost controls, rate limits, usage tracking, and Unity Catalog logging. HG Insights then brings this to life with a production use case: a multi-stage AI pipeline processing 7 billion records where rules and custom BERT models handle the predictable cases, and Gemini acts as an agentic enrichment layer — autonomously reasoning over incomplete company profiles and resolving missing attributes across hundreds of millions of inference calls. Orchestrated by Lakeflow and monitored via AI/BI dashboards, this pipeline directly generates the revenue-critical datasets HG Insights delivers to Fortune 500 customers. Whether you're enriching CRM data, building document classification pipelines, or deploying agentic data quality workflows, this session gives you the architecture patterns and lessons learned to run Gemini on Databricks at enterprise scale.

title: Enterprise Observability with ZeroBus and OTEL at Scale with Databricks
abstract: OpenTelemetry has become the industry standard for collecting traces, metrics, and logs from modern distributed systems. However, operating observability platforms at enterprise scale often requires proprietary tools and fragmented data pipelines. In this session, we present an end-to-end architecture for enterprise observability using OpenTelemetry and ZeroBus with Databricks as the analytics and visualization backbone. We will show how OpenTelemetry telemetry streams can be ingested through ZeroBus and stored in Delta Lake, enabling scalable processing and long-term retention of traces, metrics, and logs. We will demonstrate how to build a custom Databricks App to visualize flame graphs, explore distributed traces, and correlate metrics and logs in a unified interface - delivering capabilities similar to proprietary platforms but powered by the Lakehouse.
description_raw:
OpenTelemetry has become the industry standard for collecting traces, metrics, and logs from modern distributed systems. However, operating observability platforms at enterprise scale often requires proprietary tools and fragmented data pipelines.

 

In this session, we present an end-to-end architecture for enterprise observability using OpenTelemetry and ZeroBus with Databricks as the analytics and visualization backbone. We will show how OpenTelemetry telemetry streams can be ingested through ZeroBus and stored in Delta Lake, enabling scalable processing and long-term retention of traces, metrics, and logs.

 

We will demonstrate how to build a custom Databricks App to visualize flame graphs, explore distributed traces, and correlate metrics and logs in a unified interface - delivering capabilities similar to proprietary platforms but powered by the Lakehouse.

title: Enterprise Resiliency Strategies with Lakebase
abstract: Building enterprise applications on Lakebase means meeting the security, compliance, and availability requirements your organization demands. This session covers the full range of enterprise-grade resiliency capabilities in Lakebase: customer-managed encryption keys, high availability, point-in-time recovery, and strategies for disaster recovery. You'll learn how to architect for resilience from the start, what the tradeoffs look like between different recovery approaches, and how these capabilities integrate with Databricks' broader compliance and network security controls. Whether your requirements are driven by regulatory mandates, business continuity planning, or both, you'll leave with a clear framework for running Lakebase in production with the governance, auditability, and data protection your enterprise requires.

title: Evolution of the Databricks Commercial Motion: Building Scalable Intelligence on Databricks

In this session, we share our journey using Databricks to bridge the gap between technical complexity and operational reality.We detail our journey: We start by centralizing fragmented sources via Unity Catalog, surfacing descriptive trends via AiBi dashboards. We then move from descriptive to prescriptive insights, using Lakeflow orchestration to automate generation and understand causal effects. Then, we evolve from static insights to dynamic optimization, exemplified by a contract scoring system that helps sellers structure deals, built on MLflow and integrated with Salesforce. Finally, we explores how Databricks' AI products amplify the values of the previous stages.Attendees will learn to unify Databricks’ core capabilities, transitioning from high-level vision to a functional reality where AI and human strategy are woven together.

title: Evolving Apache Spark Structured Streaming in Open Source: A Year in Review and the Road Ahead!
abstract: Apache Spark Structured Streaming has quickly become the foundational open-source technology for powering mission-critical streaming ingestion and ETL pipelines worldwide. The Spark 4.1 release introduces powerful updates, most notably a new Real-Time Mode that enables operational pipelines to process data with latencies in milliseconds, all within the Spark ecosystem. Stateful transformations have been significantly bolstered through TransformWithState and stream-stream join enhancements, offering broader coverage and higher performance. Furthermore, robust improvements—such as revamped locking and integrity verification—provide improved stability for stateful queries. Looking ahead to Spark 4.2, the roadmap includes state repartitioning, query evolution, hybrid sources, and other enhancements, further establishing Spark as the gold standard for all streaming workloads. Join us to explore these recent advancements and the exciting future of open-source Structured Streaming!

title: FanDuel Presents: Operating Databricks at Scale
abstract: As organizations adopt Databricks as their central lakehouse, the challenge shifts from implementation to operating the platform reliably, securely, and cost-effectively at scale. This session presents a platform engineering operating model built on a Govern, Build, Deploy, Optimize lifecycle that enables diverse teams while embedding governance and performance controls.These initiatives demonstrate the lifecycle in action at FanDuel:• Govern – Terraforming Databricks provisions workspaces, Unity Catalog, compute, and access as code, delivering consistent and auditable environments.• Build – Standardized PySpark frameworks accelerate migrations and ensure architectural consistency through reusable ingestion and transformation patterns.• Deploy – The Project Stargate Framework uses Databricks Asset Bundles and CI/CD for controlled, traceable promotion to production.• Optimize – Cost visibility and performance efficiency through segmentation and data-driven optimization.

title: Faster Queries in Local Laptop Mode for Apache Spark™
abstract: Apache Spark™ is optimized for distributed large-scale processing, but this architecture introduces significant overhead for small, local datasets — often making sub-100 MB queries take several seconds. In this talk, we present a suite of optimizations that dramatically improve Spark’s local-mode performance across three fronts: smarter query compilation and task scheduling that eliminates unnecessary shuffles, an Arrow-based df.cache implementation that cuts cache load and query times in half and a novel shuffle-free execution mode using Java virtual threads for lightweight in-process data transfer. We will walk through the design, benchmarks and engineering trade-offs of each approach, and show how together they position Apache Spark as a practical gateway engine from laptop-scale exploration to petabyte-scale production.

title: Faster, Leaner, and Easier to Debug: PySpark UDFs in 2026
abstract: PySpark has long provided one of the most powerful and flexible ways to bring Python logic to large-scale distributed data processing. In this talk, we focus on two major advances in the PySpark UDF ecosystem: performance optimizations and improved debuggability. First, we introduce Arrow-based execution for Python, including Native Arrow UDFs and Arrow UDTFs, which operate directly on columnar Arrow data without Pandas conversion overhead. This design reduces memory usage, improves support for complex types, and delivers faster execution compared to earlier Python UDF approaches. Second, we present new debuggability enhancements for Python running inside Spark tasks, including built-in faulthandler integration for clearer crash diagnostics and improved profiling support to better understand CPU and memory behavior of UDFs. Together, these improvements make PySpark UDFs not only faster and more scalable, but also significantly easier to diagnose and optimize in production environments.

title: Feature and ML Platform Powered by Databricks
abstract: This presentation offers a comprehensive exploration of the Feature & Machine Learning Platform, focusing on its architectural design, essential components and seamless integration with Databricks. The platform harnesses Databricks for advanced feature engineering, structured streaming, declarative pipeline orchestration and end-to-end model training and serving, supporting both scheduled and event-driven workflows for maximum flexibility. Key technologies highlighted include the DBX Feature Engineering SDK, Apache Spark Structured Streaming and Databricks Lakeflow jobs, all of which contribute to scalable, efficient data processing. Online feature computation is facilitated through the DBX Unity Catalog with Python UDFs, while Databricks Online Feature Stores powered by Lakebase enable real-time use cases. For batch feature consumption outside Databricks, managed Delta UniForm and Iceberg read-only feature tables provide robust solutions.

title: Feeding the World with Unified Data: Syngenta's Data Mesh Strategy for Global Agricultural Intelligence
abstract: Agriculture generates some of the most complex and consequential data on the planet — from laboratory research and satellite imagery to factory sensors and farmers' mobile applications. The challenge is not capturing that data. It is unifying it across organizational silos into intelligence that can drive decisions in real time at global scale. Syngenta, one of the world's premier agricultural technology companies, is tackling this challenge using data mesh principles and Databricks, creating a foundation where disparate data — physical and digital, structured and unstructured — becomes connected, trustworthy insight. In this session, CDO Thomas Jung shows how breaking silos and democratizing data access is enabling proactive decisions that lift crop yields, strengthen agricultural resilience, and support global food security. For CDOs managing complex multi-domain, multi-geography data estates in regulated industries, Syngenta's approach to enterprise data governance at agricultural scale offers a model that translates across sectors.

title: Financial Services Industry Forum
abstract: Financial intelligence beats general intelligence. Trading books reprice in milliseconds, fraud patterns shift with every payment rail, and supervisors in your backyard are already asking how your models work, not if you use them. Generic AI can summarize the noise; it cannot safely move capital or satisfy regulators. Financial intelligence — built on unified, governed, and secure data — can. At the Financial Services Forum, leaders from retail and community banks, asset managers, insurers and advisory firms will share how they are unifying data, deploying domain‑trained models and running agentic AI with firm governance controls. The result: AI decisions that are fast, explainable, audit‑ready and built on the unified intelligence only your data can provide.

title: Flipping the Switch to Serverless: How McAfee Modernized Its Infrastructure and Halved Compute Costs
abstract: At McAfee, we empowered 1,000+ end users and transformed our data platform — migrating over a third of production workloads to Databricks Serverless and unifying governance with Unity Catalog. Serverless compute put self-service analytics directly in users' hands, driving a 34% jump in monthly active users, a 30%+ lift in job efficiency, and $400K+ in projected annual savings — all delivered by a lean platform team. Our phased, data-driven migration playbook made adoption safe and reversible, using decision dashboards and clear revert-to-classic paths. To date, we've hit 65% infrastructure modernization — 90% of warehouses and 40% of jobs on Serverless. title: Forecasting at Databricks: One Framework Behind Consumption and Infra Cost
abstract: Consumption forecasting and infrastructure cost forecasting at Databricks share three challenges: trust and stakeholder adoption, model accuracy under hierarchy and outliers, and data signal quality. We addressed them on a unified Databricks-native stack. For trust and adoption: a self-serve human-in-the-loop Databricks App lets infra cost owners review recommended forecasts and inject inorganic shifts the model won’t see, while AI/BI dashboards and Genie Agents let users self-serve insights, and decomposition keeps consumption forecasts explainable. For model accuracy: Unified Forecasting Framework, the backend behind AI_Forecast() function scheduled on Lakeflow Jobs validates model selection across the hierarchies. For data and signal quality: Unity Catalog, Metric Views, and Lakeflow form the governed data backbone for cost forecasting and the feature-selection substrate for consumption. Attendees leave with Databricks-native patterns for forecasts domain owners self-serve and leadership defends.
