title: How We Built Agent Mode for Genie
abstract: Agentic analytics promises to go beyond answering questions enabling AI to investigate, reason, and synthesize insights across complex data. But building systems that do this reliably is far from simple.Genie Agent Mode introduces a new approach to conversational analytics, where AI can explore multiple hypotheses, interact with data iteratively, and generate structured explanations. Under the hood, this requires careful orchestration of planning, validation, and context management to ensure results are both accurate and trustworthy.In this session, we’ll go behind the scenes to explore how Genie Agent Mode works and what it takes to make agentic analytics production-ready:- How Genie Agent Mode plans and executes multi-step analytical workflows- How the system maintains context and evaluates intermediate results- How accuracy and reliability are enforced through validation and safeguards- Key lessons learned building agentic systems for real-world data use cases

title: Human-in-the-Loop Compliance at Global Scale: Databricks Apps + Lakebase Casework + SME Labeling
abstract: In this session, we share a practical pattern we call “PolicyOps” on Databricks: converting long policy documents into cited, versioned, queryable policy units, then operationalizing a human‑in‑the‑loop workflow that captures domain SME judgment as structured labels. We’ll show how to parse and structure large policy PDFs into clause-level records (including page-aware citations), how to extract decision criteria into queryable tables, and how to connect policy interpretation to real operational review.We’ll then demonstrate an SME review queue built with Databricks Apps — designed for high-signal feedback (not just thumbs up/down) — with Lakebase used to manage case workflow state (assignment, status, reviewer actions, approvals). The result is a scalable workflow that keeps humans in control of edge cases while systematically converting implicit SME knowledge into reusable labels and corrections that improve quality over time.

title: Implementing Data Governance with Unity Catalog
abstract: This hands-on course provides a comprehensive foundation for managing governed data environments using Unity Catalog. It is designed for data engineers, platform administrators, and analytics engineers responsible for organizing, securing, and operationalizing data at scale across modern Lakehouse architectures.The course begins with an overview of Unity Catalog’s role within a cloud deployment, including how it integrates with account-level architecture and administrative responsibilities. You will explore how metastores are created and configured, how workspaces are attached, and how governance boundaries are established across environments. Through guided exercises, you will learn how data is logically and physically organized, including the use of object storage, managed and external locations, and secure access patterns for underlying storage systems.As the course progresses, you will design and implement effective data organization strategies using catalogs and schemas, translating business structures such as business units, regions, and environments into scalable naming conventions and governance models. You will apply fine-grained access control using Unity Catalog’s permission model, including ownership, management privileges, and inherited access patterns, enabling secure, least-privilege data access across teams.The course also introduces foundational interoperability concepts through Lakehouse Federation, enabling access to external data systems while maintaining centralized governance. You will explore how to bring existing data into Unity Catalog, configure secure access to external locations, and manage permissions consistently across internal and external data sources.The course concludes with practical implementation workflows, where you will create and manage catalogs, schemas, and permissions using both the UI and SQL interfaces. You will troubleshoot common configuration challenges, apply governance best practices, and establish patterns for isolating development, testing, and production environments.By the end of the course, you will be able to design, implement, and manage a secure, well-organized data governance framework using Unity Catalog, ensuring scalable access control, clear data ownership, and consistent data organization across your Lakehouse.

title: Inside Adobe’s Near Real-Time Cloud Spend Monitoring System
abstract: Cloud costs are rising faster than budgets, yet teams often discover expensive operations only after the spend has occurred. We moved from reactive cost reporting to proactive, near real-time monitoring—reducing SQL warehouse costs by 51% and Serverless compute by 14% in less than 30 days. This talk covers how we built a production-grade monitoring system managing millions in annual Databricks spend across petabyte-scale data, 94,000+ jobs, and millions of compute hours, with 15-minute monitoring cycles and zero infrastructure cost. The key challenge was attribution: Databricks assigns SQL warehouse costs to warehouse creators, not query executors, obscuring who drives spend. We solved this by combining Databricks system tables—`billing.usage`, `query.history`, and `compute.warehouse_events`—to enable query-level cost attribution without added compute. Attendees will learn the architecture, implementation patterns and reusable strategies to build proactive cost monitoring at any scale.

title: Inside Nav-AI: Accenture's No-Code Agent Factory, Powered by Databricks Apps and Lakebase
abstract: Accenture's Nav-AI lets business users build and deploy AI agents through a visual interface — no deep technical expertise required. Every customer deployment used to be a bespoke engineering project: weeks of custom work per cloud, fragile ingestion, and no foundation for agents to improve over time.In this session, Accenture shows how Nav-AI was rebuilt on Databricks to become a true product — using Databricks Apps for one-click multi-cloud deployment, the medallion architecture for reliable customer data ingestion, Model Serving for the agent runtime, and Lakebase for persistent state and self-improvement. Expect live demos from real deployments and a concrete blueprint for turning agents from a science project into a repeatable platform.

title: Inside our Lakeflow Journey at SEGA: Scaling Streaming Analytics Across Titles
abstract: At SEGA Europe, we process billions of game telemetry events daily to power real-time analytics for live ops, player experience optimisation, and business intelligence. We have rebuilt our streaming platform on Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines, moving from fragile, manually managed jobs to a resilient, self-healing lakehouse architecture. This approach was battle-tested during the launch of Football Manager 2026, where scale and reliability were critical. This session shares our production journey with Lakeflow—the wins, lessons, and unexpected challenges of operating at gaming scale. We’ll cover our migration from legacy streaming infrastructure, achieving sub-minute latency, and handling evolving event schemas. Topics include stream fan-out from Kinesis to Bronze, schema evolution, late and out-of-order events, data quality checks, performance tuning, and cost control. We’ll also share quantified results from FM26 and practical patterns for teams evaluating Lakeflow at scale.

title: Insights at Scale With Agentic AI: How AI Ready Data is Transforming Commercial Life Sciences
abstract: Pharma leaders face pressure to accelerate commercialization and improve launch performance, yet many commercial analytics teams are held back by fragmented data, brittle dashboards and heavy manual insight generation. At the same time, generative AI is rapidly advancing from copilots to fully-agentic systems, creating new opportunities and risks in regulated environments. In this session, Merck and ZS show how Merck is deploying Agentic AI using Databricks AI/BI Genie and Agent Bricks to build domain aware data agents on trusted, governed data products. These agents automate high-friction workflows across marketing, field effectiveness and brand performance, cutting time to insight by over 50% and enabling faster, more consistent decisions. We will share Merck’s blueprint for building context-rich data products, embedding business semantics and orchestrating agent workflows that integrate with existing BI—offering a practical, scalable architecture for Agentic AI in pharma.

title: Integrating Lakebase Databases into Intelligent Applications
abstract: This hands-on course teaches Databricks application developers how to use Lakebase as the operational database for intelligent, data-driven applications on Databricks. Learners explore how Lakebase enables applications powered by analytics, BI, and AI. Through guided exercises, the course covers Lakebase core concepts and architecture, provisioning and managing database instances, connecting from Databricks SQL, notebooks, and external clients, and applying best practices for connection management, permissions, and environment configuration. By the end of the course, developers will be able to confidently integrate Lakebase into production-ready data and AI applications, safely manage database resources, and unlock unified analytics and AI on live operational data. Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. title: Intelligent Document Processing with Lakeflow: Transforming Unstructured Data for Agents and Analytics
abstract: A huge portion of the data that runs your business doesn't live in clean tables — it lives in millions of documents: invoices, contracts, forms, and filings. This is some of the richest context your enterprise has, and today's agents finally have a shot at unlocking it. But there's a catch: agents can't actually read your documents. On our OfficeQA benchmark, even frontier agents score below 50% on real enterprise document tasks because they struggle to read them. Close that gap, and every agent, dashboard, and decision downstream gets sharper. In this session, we'll show how Document Intelligence on Databricks turns unstructured documents into accurate, governed insights that power more accurate agents and analytics. We'll walk through how to build intelligent document processing pipelines with Lakeflow and AI Functions purpose-built for document understanding — taking your documents from raw PDF to rich answers in Genie. Walk away knowing how to turn your document corpus into the data layer that powers smarter, faster, and more trustworthy agents and analytics.

title: Introducing Indexes for the Lakehouse
abstract: Substring searches that take hours. Point lookups that scan terabytes. Pattern-matching queries that force you to maintain a separate tools alongside your lakehouse. These are problems that traditional databases solved decades ago — and that the lakehouse is now solving too. In this session, we'll introduce two new indexing capabilities coming to Databricks: Full-Text Search indexes for fast substring, regex, and IP-address matching with up to 20x query speedup; Standard (Secondary) indexes for needle-in-a-haystack point lookups with 30-60x speedup on non-clustered columns; We'll cover how each index type works under the hood, when to use which, and how they complement Liquid Clustering and data skipping. Then we'll show a live demo — creating indexes on real tables, running queries that previously took minutes in under seconds. If you're running log analytics, SIEM workloads, UUID lookups, or any query pattern where you're scanning far more data than you need to — this session is for you.
description_raw:
Substring searches that take hours. Point lookups that scan terabytes. Pattern-matching queries that force you to maintain a separate tools alongside your lakehouse. These are problems that traditional databases solved decades ago — and that the lakehouse is now solving too.

 

In this session, we'll introduce two new indexing capabilities coming to Databricks:

  • Full-Text Search indexes for fast substring, regex, and IP-address matching with up to 20x query speedup; 
  • Standard (Secondary) indexes for needle-in-a-haystack point lookups with 30-60x speedup on non-clustered columns; 

 

We'll cover how each index type works under the hood, when to use which, and how they complement Liquid Clustering and data skipping. Then we'll show a live demo — creating indexes on real tables, running queries that previously took minutes in under seconds.

 

If you're running log analytics, SIEM workloads, UUID lookups, or any query pattern where you're scanning far more data than you need to — this session is for you.

title: Introducing Lakewatch
abstract: Cyberattacks are no longer just human-operated. AI-driven threats now move at machine speed, exploiting gaps across systems while your SOC is still triaging yesterday's alerts. Traditional SIEMs weren’t built for this reality: they force painful trade-offs between data volume, retention and cost, leaving security teams flying blind with only a fraction of their telemetry in view. In this session, we’ll take you inside Lakewatch, Databricks’ open, agentic SIEM built for machine-speed defense. We’ll start with the “why”: what motivated us to build something fundamentally different. Then we’ll demo how Lakewatch unifies 100% of your security, IT and business telemetry in one governed environment using open formats and Unity Catalog, with no costly duplication and no vendor lock-in. You’ll see how embedded AI agents powered by Genie Code automate threat detection and response at machine speed, and we’ll close with an exclusive peek at the roadmap and what’s coming next. Whether you’re evaluating your current SIEM, dealing with runaway data costs or looking to modernize your SOC on your existing Databricks investment, this session is your practical starting point. Key takeaways: Why traditional SIEMs structurally fail against AI-driven threats How Lakewatch unifies all your telemetry with open formats and Unity Catalog How Genie agents automate detection, hunting, and response A first look at the Lakewatch roadmap and what’s coming next

title: Introduction to Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines: Reliable Data Pipelines Made Easy
abstract: Building data pipelines often means hand-writing complex data engineering patterns like incremental processing, CDC/SCD handling, and backfills in every job. Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP) are the next evolution in how transformations are written in Spark by default. You declare the data you want to produce, and the platform applies proven execution semantics for you. Built on an open, declarative standard for Spark pipelines, SDP helps teams move faster on hard problems while scaling production best practices consistently. In this session, you’ll see how SDP: Provides a necessary foundation for agentic data pipeline development Reduces the amount of custom logic required for incremental and CDC workloads Makes batch and streaming pipelines easier to build, debug, and evolve over time Standardizes reliability and correctness across pipelines as they scale We’ll walk through concrete examples that show how declarative pipelines simplify otherwise complex data engineering patterns.

title: Keeping AI safe in healthcare - evaluation strategies for production ready agentic systems
abstract: Healthcare organizations struggle with siloed data from claims, hospital records, physician notes, and lab results and now with the latest agentic frameworks on top of Databricks, we are able to unify these data sources and provide access to insights that can vastly improve patient care. However, deploying AI agents in healthcare requires rigorous evaluation that goes beyond traditional accuracy metrics to ensure clinical safety and compliance. In this breakout session, attendees will learn how to implement continuous evaluation workflows that track agent performance across critical dimensions specific to healthcare. We will demonstrate how to leverage MLflow 3 to build a comprehensive evaluation pipeline for a multi agent AI system that includes-SQL-based validation rules for data integrity-Structured UAT protocols with clinical stakeholders-LLM-as-Judge evaluation for scalable output assessment-Human-in-the-loop feedback alignment -Automated production monitoring mechanisms

title: Lakeflow Designer: No-code ETL— Authored With AI, Built for Production
abstract: As demand for data grows, central data teams can’t build every transformation themselves. But traditional “self-service” ETL tools often introduce new problems: logic leaves governed platforms, pipelines live in parallel runtimes, and productionization requires costly rewrites by data engineering teams. Lakeflow Designer addresses this gap by giving analysts a no-code, AI-first way to do data prep on the same Lakeflow execution model used by data engineering teams. Instead of introducing a parallel toolchain, Designer produces governed, production-grade transformations that fit directly into existing data engineering workflows. In this session, you’ll see how Lakeflow Designer: Enables analysts to do data prep without moving data outside Databricks Preserves centralized governance, quality, and lineage through Unity Catalog Lets data engineers scale pipeline development by directly operationalizing designer-authored logic— without rebuilding, translating, or refactoring

title: Lakeflow Jobs: Modern Orchestration for the Data Platform
abstract: Modern data platforms need more than a scheduler. They need orchestration that understands data, integrates with the platform, and scales with both engineering and AI workloads. Join this session to see how Lakeflow Jobs helps teams orchestrate pipelines, notebooks, dbt projects, SQL, and external components, natively on the Databricks Platform. We will show how Lakeflow Jobs goes beyond basic scheduling with data-aware orchestration that understands the assets and systems it is coordinating. You will see how teams can trigger workflows based on data changes, build modular workflows in Python, orchestrate external systems alongside Databricks workloads, and use Declarative Automation Bundles (DABs) for a more reliable CI/CD path. We will also cover how Serverless Jobs and observability features such as lineage and system tables help teams reduce operational overhead and better understand what is happening across their workflows. Finally, we will preview how agentic authoring and diagnostics can speed up building, troubleshooting, and improving production jobs, and how you can embed agents directly into your workflows. Whether you are modernizing from legacy schedulers or building new workloads on the lakehouse, this session will share practical patterns, product direction, and live demos for modern orchestration on Databricks.

title: LakeFoundry: The Databricks-Native Delivery Platform for Spec-Driven Autonomous Software Building
abstract: Most enterprises don't struggle to write code — they struggle to consistently deliver production-grade Databricks solutions that are clearly scoped, governed, and built to last. LakeFoundry is Slalom's autonomous, agent-driven delivery platform that transforms ideas, tickets, chats, and draft requirements into a repeatable, auditable path from concept to production — entirely within Databricks.At its core, LakeFoundry operates across three planes: a Control Plane that enforces structured specification and stakeholder alignment before a single line of code is written; an Execution Plane where autonomous subagents generate, verify, and deploy production-grade code with Unity Catalog governance, policy-as-code guardrails, and replayable LLM audit trails; and a Continuous Improvement Plane where an embedded Improvement Agent analyzes MLflow traces, detects performance drift, and proposes human-reviewed PRs — keeping systems from decaying post-launch.LakeFoundry integrates natively with Slack, Jira, Teams, GitHub, and CLI — meeting teams where work already happens — while eliminating the ambiguity, context rot, and governance gaps that cause autonomous development to fail at enterprise scale.The result: spec clarity before execution, test-driven autonomous generation, and governance embedded by design — not bolted on after. For Databricks customers, LakeFoundry provides a native path to operationalize agentic software delivery on the same trusted platform that already governs their data, workloads, and environments.

LakeFoundry is Slalom's autonomous, agent-driven delivery platform that transforms ideas, tickets, chats, and draft requirements into a repeatable, auditable path from concept to production — entirely within Databricks.At its core, LakeFoundry operates across three planes: a Control Plane that enforces structured specification and stakeholder alignment before a single line of code is written; an Execution Plane where autonomous subagents generate, verify, and deploy production-grade code with Unity Catalog governance, policy-as-code guardrails, and replayable LLM audit trails; and a Continuous Improvement Plane where an embedded Improvement Agent analyzes MLflow traces, detects performance drift, and proposes human-reviewed PRs — keeping systems from decaying post-launch.LakeFoundry integrates natively with Slack, Jira, Teams, GitHub, and CLI — meeting teams where work already happens — while eliminating the ambiguity, context rot, and governance gaps that cause autonomous development to fail at enterprise scale.The result: spec clarity before execution, test-driven autonomous generation, and governance embedded by design — not bolted on after. For Databricks customers, LakeFoundry provides a native path to operationalize agentic software delivery on the same trusted platform that already governs their data, workloads, and environments.

title: Language-Agnostic UDF Protocol for Spark
abstract: User-defined functions (UDFs) are a fundamental extension mechanism in Spark, enabling users to express logic that goes beyond built-in operators. However, the current UDF execution model is not enough for the multi-language architecture in Spark Connect. Existing implementations are tightly coupled to specific runtimes (e.g., PySpark), rely on ad-hoc communication protocols, and embed language-specific logic into planning and execution.This proposal aims to introduce a language-agnostic UDF execution model for Spark. It is built around three core ideas: (1) planning UDFs based on execution shape rather than programming language, (2) a structured execution IPC protocol and (3) a declarative worker specification to decouple the Spark engine from language runtimes.To provide a clean and extensible foundation for IPC-based UDF execution across languages, this proposal aims to standardize multi-language support and establish a sustainable direction for the UDF ecosystem.

abstract: Johns Hopkins is undergoing a major cloud transformation, moving from a legacy SQL Server EDW to a modern, scalable data and analytics platform. In this session, the JHHP and CitiusTech team will share best practices for designing and implementing an enterprise‑grade Databricks platform on AWS GovCloud—critical for supporting Johns Hopkins’ partnerships with the armed forces and Tricare. The session highlights architectural principles for building a modular, ingestion‑ready platform that unifies diverse data sources, along with results such as reducing workload runtimes from 22+ hours to 2–3 hours for full loads and under an hour for incremental runs. Presenters will also cover lessons learned in optimizing pipelines, using a Brickbuilder‑certified metadata ingestion framework, and enabling a strong data‑quality engine. Attendees will leave with practical guidance for large‑scale cloud modernization in regulated environments while creating reusable, enterprise‑wide data assets.

title: Latest innovations in Genie Code: The Future of Agentic Data Work
abstract: AI coding assistants have changed how developers write code, but most stop at suggestions. Genie Code is an autonomous AI agent designed specifically for data teams. It plans and executes full workflows, and it monitors your production systems in the background, triaging and fixing pipeline failures before your team even notices. We'll cover: - What’s new in Genie Code - How it builds and maintains production data and AI workflows end to end, from pipeline creation to model serving observability - How Unity Catalog integration gives Genie Code the enterprise context, governance, and accuracy that general-purpose agents lack - Best practices for working with Genie Code as an autonomous partner, including Agent Skills and persistent memory

title: Learn How We Secure and Govern Lakewatch on the Databricks Trusted Lakehouse
abstract: Security data is among the most sensitive in the enterprise, yet many SIEM deployments lack consistent, fine-grained governance. Learn how Lakewatch leverages Unity Catalog to provide centralized governance across your entire security ecosystem. We will dive deep into the Lakewatch RBAC model, demonstrating how to manage Principals (Users, Groups, and Service Principals) across protected resources like Datasources, Detection Rules, and Notables. You’ll learn how to implement Lakewatch’s unique inherited permission model — where cases automatically inherit context from parent resources — to streamline investigations while maintaining strict "need-to-know" access. Takeaways include: implementing table, row, and column-level security for telemetry; defining Viewer, Creator, and Manager scopes at Workspace and Resource levels; practical patterns for SOC, cloud, and data teams to collaborate safely; sharing data with partners via Delta Sharing without compromising auditability or lineage.

title: Less Infrastructure, Higher Impact: Nationwide’s Serverless Transformation with Databricks
abstract: Simplifying infrastructure accelerates data work and drives outcomes. The future of analytics isn’t about managing clusters; it’s about empowering users with seamless, scalable compute. In this session, Nationwide and Databricks share a real-world journey from server-managed infrastructure to Databricks Serverless, covering all-purpose compute, jobs compute, and SQL warehouses. We show how serverless simplified operations, sped up development cycles, reduced cost variability, and improved the user experience. We highlight the biggest wins, explore key design decisions that shaped success, and close with practical best practices to help your organization confidently accelerate its move to serverless.

title: Let AI Work on Your Database: Safe AI-Driven Development with Database Branches
abstract: AI coding agents have drastically improved the way we work in so many areas of software development, but because LLMs are inherently non-deterministic, many developers are still hesitant to let AI agents touch their databases because of the risk of destructive actions. In this talk, we’ll show how to safely leverage AI in real workflows using Lakebase’s branching capabilities. With the tools and strategies we’ll discuss, you will be able to create isolated code and data environments that enable AI coding agents to build in parallel, experiment safely, and iterate faster, without risking production data. By the end of this talk, attendees will walk away with practical patterns to integrate AI into their development workflows with confidence.

title: Let Your Agent Pilot Your Fleet: Business Insights From 35,000 Feet
abstract: We run a data platform at Thales IFE that tracks how millions of passengers interact with in-flight entertainment at 35,000 feet. While the data was widely available, business teams still depended on analysts to answer questions or build yet another dashboard. This session shows how we made an AI assistant the primary interface for business and operational insight using Databricks Apps and how it was integrated with existing business systems and portals. We walk through a real scenario: A business user opens a Databricks App, interacts with the AI agent and explores passenger usage & system performance data. The same agent can also be embedded into existing business applications, bringing consistent data access directly into daily workflows. The talk focuses on outcomes and lessons learned: What Databricks simplified, where challenges appeared and what it takes to move AI agents from experiment to production for our business users.

title: lululemon: How We Modernized Our Audience Segmentation and Where It's Taking Us With Agentic AI
abstract: At lululemon, our CRM Audience Data Science team operates PAVE—an ML platform scoring millions of guest profiles for personalized marketing across email, push, web and paid media. With growth came pain: data scientists managing deployments instead of building models, no path to production, and marketing waiting weeks for new segments. The bottleneck was never the model. We came to DAIS 2025 with these problems and left with a plan: DABS, Unity Catalog, and MLflow 3.0 as the foundation for a live system. Key areas we will cover: DABS: parameterized pipelines that any team member can deploy in one command Multi-stream architecture where each new model type inherits the same pipeline pattern Unity Catalog migration seeding an enterprise feature store now scaling beyond PAVE MLflow 3.0 for unified tracking, registry and model promotion across all streams Agentic AI roadmap: next best action for marketing partners and generative model monitoring

title: Magnite's Journey of Interoperability on a Petabyte of Iceberg Data
abstract: For Magnite's business, they have a need to handle the ingest of 900TB of data every 10 days, while offering subsets of that data to many different customers (internal and external). Join this session to learn how Magnite successfully accomplished this while centralizing their data access via Unity Catalog while improving performance and handling many different engines (including Apache Spark, DuckDB, and Snowflake). We'll discuss the different approaches required, best practices followed, and rough edges encountered along the way. This lively presentation will be beneficial to anyone looking to separate compute and storage in their data domain at any scale.

title: Making Agents Work: How the Ecosystem Unlocks Enterprise Value
abstract: Most enterprises struggle to move AI from experimentation to enterprise-grade deployments because agents lack a grounded, real-world understanding of how their business actually runs. Without this "operational reality," AI agents remain unreliable at scale, creating a trust gap that prevents true autonomous execution and measurable efficiency. Together, Celonis and Databricks provide the foundation to transform operations and make them AI-first from the ground up. We provide AI agents with the business logic needed to reason about the past and predict the future, bridging the gap between raw data and autonomous action.Join us to learn how ARM is industrializing AI, moving beyond isolated pilots to an environment where people, agents, and systems work together with unprecedented accuracy. By connecting business processes, ARM is orchestrating global operations with measurable productivity gains and a clear path to long-term ROI.

title: Managing Data at Exabyte Scale for AI Model Training
abstract: More and more enterprises are post-training AI models to be custom tailored to their domain and users. Success in model training depends critically on establishing the right data flywheel to improve iteration speed. From exploration to curation, from feature engineering to training, current data infrastructure solutions are insufficient to support the full iteration loop. Model development teams wrestle with a hodgepodge of single-purpose tools, copying data across systems for different workflow steps. This is a key reason why so many enterprise AI model training efforts are delayed or fail. In this talk, we’ll cover how LanceDB solves this by managing all of your multimodal training data in a unified table and streamlining the entire exploration to GPU-loading path. Through customer case studies, we’ll outline this new architecture, practical recipes for success and how it all fits into your existing enterprise data architecture.

Hear directly from industry innovators who are already leading the transformation and leave with actionable frameworks for deploying Industrial AI at scale.

title: MCP Security Deep Dive: How Databricks Secures Tool Access for Enterprise Users
abstract: As agents connect to external tools and systems, security becomes a first-order concern. Every interaction — from authentication to tool invocation — must be governed, permissioned, and fully auditable. One leaked credential or broken audit trail can break production trust overnight.In this deep dive, we'll show how to secure MCP-based integrations in production on Databricks. You'll learn how to implement authentication and authorization, manage fine-grained access to tools, and ensure every agent action is traceable end-to-end. We'll also share how Databricks applies these patterns internally — using Unity Catalog connections to securely grant MCP access to thousands of users — along with the key risks, design tradeoffs, and best practices.You'll walk away with a production-ready blueprint for protecting data and systems as agents start taking real actions on behalf of your users.

Drivers demand a seamless, personalized experience, while OEMs demand data sovereignty and low-latency interventions. Real-Time Nervous System: Vehicle telemetry (Engine Temp, TPMS) streams directly into Unity Catalog via Zerobus, enabling near real-time anomaly detection.2. Infinite Memory & Context: How Bricksy utilizes Vector Search and Lakebase to instantly recall car manuals, service history, and long-term driver preferences.3. AI That Comes to Your Data: How manufacturers can deploy proprietary tools and functions directly on the Lakehouse, ensuring sensitive telemetry never leaves their governance boundary.

title: Merchandising Intelligence That Merchants Trust: Albertsons' Structure-First AI for Smarter Promotions
abstract: Retail promotion decisions involve billions of dollars and millions of interdependencies — yet most AI systems produce recommendations that merchants cannot explain, validate, or trust. Albertsons built a different kind of merchandising intelligence. Using 70 billion rows of transaction data processed on the Databricks Lakehouse, they modeled item and promotion relationships as reusable graph structures — what they call Promo Molecules — that explicitly surface demand shifts including substitution effects, halo effects, and cannibalization. These structures are not black boxes. They expose deterministic, merchant-validated signals that can be audited and acted on with confidence. Foundation models then reason probabilistically to answer natural-language what-if questions, enabling merchant-trusted promotion decisions at scale without manual overrides. In this session, Karthik Iyer explains the structure-first AI architecture behind Albertsons' merchandising intelligence platform, the business outcomes it is driving, and why explainability — not just accuracy — is the key to unlocking AI adoption in retail. This is a session for CMOs, CDOs, and retail executives who are done compromising between AI capability and business trust.

title: Metric Views—What They Are, How They Work, and How to Model Them
abstract: Databricks has always had a strong foundation for data engineering, but one thing has been missing: a semantic layer that lives inside the platform. Metric Views finally change that. With Metric Views, measures and models are defined directly in Unity Catalog and reachable from Databricks Notebooks, Databricks SQL editor, AI/BI Dashboards, and AI/BI Genie. Data engineers and analysts are finally working from the same definitions, no more translating DAX back into SQL to understand what a number means. In this session we will walk through what Metric Views are and what the setup looks like in practice. Then we will look at the modeling decisions, whether to build small specialized views or broader shared ones, how those choices affect reuse and consistency, and how they affect what Genie returns and how dashboards behave. New to metric views or already using them, you will leave with a clearer picture of how to approach them.

title: MGM Enterprise Data Hub: Accelerating Data Delivery With DABS CI/CD Approach
abstract: MGM Resorts is unifying our data estate, leveraging Unity Catalog for centralized governance, access control and cross‑environment consistency across gaming, hospitality and partner ecosystems. We updated our framework with DABS reducing delivery time for gold tables by 67%, enabling automated deployment and validation in under 5 min, cutting deployment code by 75%. We: Enabled isolation and targeted lifecycle management via a multi-bundle architecture with shared utilities in a common wheel Improved reliability with a GitHub Actions pipeline for sequential DEV → UAT → PROD deployments, with consistent governance across environments using Unity Catalog Freed engineers to focus on business logic through centralized configuration, SCD handling, and Apache Spark™ lifecycle management Key takeaways: CI/CD best practices using standardized databricks.yml Higher reliability and faster delivery through a bundle-based pattern Metrics and lessons to drive low-risk, predictable releases across the org
description_raw:
MGM Resorts is unifying our data estate, leveraging Unity Catalog for centralized governance, access control and cross‑environment consistency across gaming, hospitality and partner ecosystems. We updated our framework with DABS reducing delivery time for gold tables by 67%, enabling automated deployment and validation in under 5 min, cutting deployment code by 75%.

 

We:

  • Enabled isolation and targeted lifecycle management via a multi-bundle architecture with shared utilities in a common wheel
  • Improved reliability with a GitHub Actions pipeline for sequential DEV → UAT → PROD deployments, with consistent governance across environments using Unity Catalog
  • Freed engineers to focus on business logic through centralized configuration, SCD handling, and Apache Spark™ lifecycle management

 

Key takeaways:

  • CI/CD best practices using standardized databricks.yml
  • Higher reliability and faster delivery through a bundle-based pattern
  • Metrics and lessons to drive low-risk, predictable releases across the org

title: Migrate to Lakeflow Jobs: Modernizing Data Orchestration on Databricks
abstract: Still running orchestration outside Databricks? That often means more tools to manage, less context about your data, and more overhead connecting pipelines, schedules, and dependencies across systems. Join this session to learn how to migrate to Lakeflow Jobs, Databricks’ native orchestrator for data and AI workloads. We will cover practical migration patterns, the tooling available to accelerate the move, and the tips, techniques, and best practices that help teams reduce risk and avoid common pitfalls. You will learn: Why teams are consolidating orchestration onto Databricks How common migration patterns from legacy orchestrators map to Lakeflow Jobs What tooling, tips, and techniques can speed up migration and simplify rollout The best practices that help teams move faster with less operational overhead What real customer migrations look like in practice, including key challenges, tradeoffs, and outcomes

title: Migrating from SQL Server and Synapse to Azure Databricks
abstract: Learn proven best practices to modernize from SQL Server and Azure Synapse to the Databricks Lakehouse. The session will include Lakebridge's AI‑assisted migration to analyze and convert legacy SQL (T‑SQL DDL/DML, views, stored procedures) and Synapse scripts into Databricks Lakehouse and Spark‑based workloads. Adopt unified governance and privilege mapping in Unity Catalog, and follow a phased cutover: begin with Lakehouse Federation for read‑through access to SQL Server and Synapse, add CDC‑based replication, and run side‑by‑side reconciliation and query validation before switching over. Optionally leverage Lakeflow Connect for managed SQL Server ingestion under Unity Catalog governance. Finally, serve high‑performance BI at scale with SQL Serverless to deliver fast, reliable dashboards in Power BI and beyond. Learn how to de‑risk migrations, improve price/performance, and accelerate delivery.

title: Migrating to Serverless: The Databricks Journey

title: Millisecond Pricing: High-Velocity Feature Serving on the Lakebase
abstract: Fragmented architectures kill pricing precision. Real-time systems require millisecond latency across millions of features without training-serving skew. title: Mission-Critical Inference: Powering High-Scale AI in Production
abstract: You've shipped your model. Now it needs to serve millions of requests a day without blinking — at the right latency, the right cost, and with zero downtime. The architecture that handled your prototype won't cut it in production, and most teams learn that the hard way.This session walks through the architecture, tuning knobs, and operational patterns that let Databricks Custom Model Serving handle the world's most demanding inference workloads. You'll see how GPU autoscaling matches capacity to traffic, how request batching drives down cost per call, how traffic splitting enables safe rollouts, and how built-in observability lets you catch regressions before users do.Bring your hardest production challenges — you'll leave with concrete patterns for running high-scale AI inference reliably, and the playbook to keep it fast, governed, and cost-efficient as demand grows.

title: Mo’ Agents Mo’ Problems: How We Simplified Lakehouse Threat Hunting as a Service at Scale
abstract: Security teams face an impossible ratio of millions of events, thousands of alerts, and a handful of analysts. Most hunt reactively or not at all. We built a threat hunting platform on Databricks that flips this equation. Our architecture spans the full stack: Lakeflow DLT normalizes 20+ sources into OCSF, billions of events are governed in Unity Catalog, and detection pipelines form the foundation for specialized AI agents that hunt autonomously. These agents generate hypotheses, investigate the lakehouse, enrich IOCs via MCP tools, and produce findings without prompting. The critical constraint: agents never see raw telemetry. They query pre-aggregated views, keeping billion-row datasets out of the LLM context while preserving investigative depth. You'll learn how we architected safe agent-to-lakehouse communication, orchestration patterns for autonomous hunt cycles, and detection at scale, while hearing about our service delivery at petabyte scale.

title: Modern Data Modeling at Scale: Advanced Patterns
abstract: Unlock the truth behind data modeling in Databricks. This session will tackle the top 10 myths surrounding relational and dimensional data modeling. Attendees will gain a clear understanding of what Databricks Lakehouse truly supports today, including how to leverage primary and foreign keys, identity columns for surrogate keys, column-level data quality constraints and much more. This session will talk through the lens of medallion architecture, explaining how to implement data models across Bronze, Silver and Gold tables. Whether you’re migrating from a legacy warehouse or building new analytics solutions, you’ll leave equipped to fully leverage Databricks’ capabilities, and design scalable, high-performance data models for enterprise analytics.

title: Modernization Without Illusions: Migrating a Barclays Business-Critical Equities Data Warehouse to Databricks
abstract: Transitioning a mission-critical data platform is rarely straightforward—especially when the legacy system already works and the environment is tightly regulated. This session shares real-world lessons from moving a high-stakes post-trade data platform to a cloud-native Databricks architecture, focusing on the trade-offs that determine whether teams merely migrate or truly land well. We explore how decisions around design, execution, and platform-native patterns shape performance, cost and business SLAs from day one—and why treating migration and modernization as a binary choice often leads to poor outcomes. Through concrete examples, we highlight how principle-driven interventions turned initially underperforming designs into stable, scalable solutions, offering a candid look at the realities of transitioning critical data platforms without sacrificing predictability or value.

title: Modernizing Clinical Data Integration at Novo Nordisk With Lakebase and the Databricks Lakehouse
abstract: Novo Nordisk transformed how vendor-sourced and vendor-facing clinical trial data is ingested, operationalized and exposed by building an API layer on the Databricks lakehouse powered by Lakebase. By replacing fragmented, self-hosted Postgres silos with Lakebase, a Postgres engine integrated with the lakehouse, we now make data available 30x faster than with legacy self-hosted Postgres. This session walks through the end-to-end architecture and migration. We’ll talk about why Lakebase was chosen—horizontal scale and simplified operations—and how these capabilities reduce friction and speed onboarding. We’ll further expand on the blueprints we employed for Lakebase development, including governance and deployment patterns that can be adopted across an organization, and elaborate on the lessons learned along the way. Attendees will learn how we modernized ingestion of structured and unstructured data to achieve consistent, auditable data in a regulated environment.

title: Modernizing Investment Analytics Through Data Driven Architecture
abstract: Transforming a 30-year-old monolithic analytics platform is as much about mindset as it is about technology. Our legacy, batch-based system—with its rigid relational model and high maintenance costs—could no longer keep up with growing data, client demands, or innovation needs. In this session, we share how we reimagined investment analytics with a cloud-native architecture modern ingestion and ETL pipelines using Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP), dimensional modeling, and a modern OLAP engine. We’ll highlight key design decisions, migration patterns, and how we preserved trusted reporting while improving data quality, transparency, and self-service. Attendees will learn practical strategies to de-risk modernization, accelerate delivery, and unlock new analytical capabilities without disrupting mission-critical operations.

title: Move Fast, Stay Secure: Enterprise AI Agent Security in Practice
abstract: Agentic AI is moving from POCs to mission-critical workloads- and the attack surface is expanding fast. As LLM-driven agents reason, plan, and act across enterprise data and tools, a new class of risk emerges: the "Lethal Trifecta," where sensitive data access, untrusted inputs, and external actions converge to make prompt injection attacks exploitable end-to-end. Karol Piekarski (Experian) and Nishith Sinha (Databricks) present the Databricks Agentic AI Security Framework (DASF v3), drawing on both Databricks' own AI infrastructure which handles millions of daily queries, and patterns from Fortune 100 deployments. The session walks through how the Databricks platform breaks the Lethal Trifecta at each layer: constraining what agents can access, hardening how they process inputs, and limiting what a compromised agent can actually do. Finally, see how the Databricks Security team built, open-sourced, and actively uses BlackIce, a containerized AI red teaming toolkit, to shift security from a point-in-time exercise to continuous, automated validation. Leave with a practical framework for moving fast on AI without compromising governance or security.

title: Multi-Tenant Architecture at Scale: Fewer Workspaces, Less Admin, No Silos
abstract: As analytics and AI workloads grow, most enterprises scale by adding more Databricks workspaces and infrastructure. Over time, this leads to admin overhead, duplicated standards, slow onboarding, and analytics, ML and GenAI teams operating in silos. In this session, we share our lessons learned at Procter & Gamble, one of the largest Databricks workspace deployments. We show how we reversed that pattern by designing a multi-tenant Databricks architecture built to adapt to constant change and scale with minimal admin effort. Databricks is a multi-tenant platform — this session shows how to maximize it at enterprise scale. Using a “hub-and-spoke” approach, we consolidated workspaces while preserving team autonomy and execution speed. Attendees will learn how to: Design a multi-tenant architecture that scales without increasing admin overhead Consolidate workspaces while maintaining team ownership Run analytics and AI workloads on a shared platform without creating silos

title: Native Streaming-to-Lakehouse Governance with Unity Catalog
abstract: Real-time data powers modern AI and analytics yet governing high-velocity streaming data in the lakehouse remains a challenge. In this session, StreamNative and Databricks showcase a native integration that brings governance to streaming pipelines through Databricks Unity Catalog without sacrificing performance or simplicity. We introduce catalog-based commits, a new approach where streaming data written in Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg formats is registered and governed in Unity Catalog at commit time. This eliminates post-processing, manual metadata synchronization and governance gaps, while enabling consistent access control, lineage and auditing across streaming and batch workloads. Attendees will learn how this integration reduces operational complexity, accelerates AI and real-time analytics and delivers a seamless path from event streams to governed, AI-ready lakehouse tables.

This eliminates post-processing, manual metadata synchronization and governance gaps, while enabling consistent access control, lineage and auditing across streaming and batch workloads.

 

Attendees will learn how this integration reduces operational complexity, accelerates AI and real-time analytics and delivers a seamless path from event streams to governed, AI-ready lakehouse tables.

title: Navigating the Realities of AI Policy: The 2026 Data + AI Policy Intelligence Brief
abstract: Artificial Intelligence and how to regulate it is top of mind for companies, governments, and policymakers everywhere. Today, industry faces a “Deregulation Paradox”: While the current US Government takes executive action to dismantle AI rules, states are doubling down on their own policies and enforcement. In 2025, U.S. legislators introduced over 1200 AI-related bills, threatening a regulatory patchwork that is colliding with a federal push for preemption. To separate the signal from noise, join leading experts for a deep dive into the the policy and politics surrounding AI and data regulation at the federal, state, and international levels in the year ahead. Moderator: Alan Davidson, Databricks Head of Government Affairs

title: Near Real-Time Media Analytics with Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines
abstract: In digital-first media, analytics latency directly drives editorial, revenue and audience decisions. For global publishers, sub-second insight into content performance shapes how teams react to breaking news, tentpole events and monetisation windows. This session shares how Condé Nast — a global media company with 115+ years of publishing history — is re-architecting media analytics on Databricks, moving from a fragmented, high-latency stack to a near real-time lakehouse powered by Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines and Lakebase. Our legacy stack delivered analytics with a 15–30 minute delay across InfluxDB, Qlik and rigid third-party tools — costing us revenue yield on trending stories, delayed subscription conversions, duplicated business logic and blind spots between top-of-funnel content and downstream drivers like commerce and MAI. The new architecture ingests directly from web collectors into Databricks. Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines unify streaming and batch, run on-the-fly aggregations and enforce consistent business logic at scale. Lakebase powers low-latency operational serving, while the lakehouse remains the system of record. The result: end-to-end latency under 10 seconds, third-party black-box vendors phased out, and a single unified view across audience, subscription, affiliate and ad data. We will also explore extending this with the Databricks Genie API to bring LLM-powered text-to-query into real-time media workflows.

title: Nimble Semantic Web Search on Databricks
abstract: Nimble brings semantic web search into Databricks by turning high-volume web search and real time crawling into task-specific web indexes. Instead of giving agents raw pages from a generic index, Nimble organizes web data into entities, fields, relationships, freshness, and source context before reasoning begins. Deployed with Databricks Lakebase and aligned with Unity AI Gateway, Nimble lets enterprises consume live web intelligence directly inside their governed lakehouse environment. This enables AI applications that combine internal data with fresh external web context, securely and at scale. We will show how a Fortune 500 company deploys a task-specific agent with Nimble’s specialized web search, delivering more accurate web intelligence with lower token cost and enterprise-scale reliability.

Learn how Atlassian achieved: 80% ingestion cost reduction moving to file notification loader Scheduled jobs running queries in seconds from minutes Day‑long searches accelerated from minutes to seconds with Z‑ORDER and OPTIMIZE We’ll cover PySpark patterns, and collaboration spaces, reusable libraries and notebooks that make IR handoffs repeatable. title: O(n*m) Architecture in Open Source. What Could Possibly Go Wrong?
abstract: There's a quiet crisis going on in open source right now — whenever an open table format wants to build a new feature or integration, there's an exponentially more amount of work to do to incorporate it. A project that's increasingly harder to contribute to is the death of innovation. Kernel sets out to solve this problem by rewriting the source of truth. When other projects adopt Kernel, they no longer need to do any additional development for new features — they just appear. Join us for a deep dive into how we turned this project on its head, to solve not just these problems, but future problems we anticipate in open source. What started out as a contribution to Delta, could change the way that open table formats fundamentally integrate everywhere. Join Robert Pack, open-source contributor for Delta, Iceberg, Arrow and all round Rust enthusiast, and Holly Smith, tech communicator, who bullied Robert into this talk.

title: OLTP on the Object Store: Reimagining Postgres with the Lakebase Architecture
abstract: Traditional databases force architects into a familiar set of tradeoffs: scale compute and you pay for storage you don't need, add read replicas for analytical queries and you introduce replication lag, separate your OLTP and OLAP systems and you're managing data movement and consistency across boundaries. These aren't bugs in the design; they're consequences of tightly coupled storage and compute. Lakebase decouples storage from compute and runs Postgres natively on object storage. In this session, you'll learn what that architecture looks like, why it changes the tradeoff calculus, and what it makes possible: analytical queries running directly on operational data without read replicas, compute that scales to zero when idle, and transactional workloads sitting alongside lakehouse analytics on the same underlying data. We'll map the architecture to concrete use cases, including real-time applications and AI workloads that need fresh operational data, and hybrid workloads that previously required two separate systems. You'll leave with a clear mental model of how Lakebase works and where it fits in your stack.

abstract: Fonterra is on a journey to replace thousands of traditional reports with AI‑driven, self‑service analytics powered by Databricks AI/BI and Genie. Today, the platform supports more than 1,300 data products and over 25 Genie Spaces, driving strong adoption and measurable business impact across the organization. In this session, we’ll share how the Ingredients and Trading team transitioned from a fragmented landscape of on‑premises systems, tools, and databases to a unified Databricks platform. This shift has enabled a move from static, report‑based consumption to governed, natural language access to data—making insights faster, simpler, and more accessible. We’ll walk through the transformation journey, highlight immediate wins across Ingredients and Trading as well as the wider Fonterra business, and outline what’s next. This includes how AI/BI Dashboards and Genie spaces are becoming the new standard and how Databricks applications are featuring on the roadmap. title: One Stack for Retail AI: From Transactional Planning to Agentic Intelligence on Databricks
abstract: Retail AI platforms are no longer just analytics or ML systems — they must power real-time planning, massive-scale AI and intelligent decisioning on a single foundation. In this session, we share how our retail AI SaaS product is built entirely on Databricks’ unified platform. What we do uniquely on Databricks: We run classic AI (forecasting, optimization) and GenAI + agentic workflows together in a single Databricks stack, eliminating fragmentation between ML pipelines, planning logic and intelligent decision automation. Our hyperlocal forecasting USP (unique model per SKU–Store via ensemble selection) is possible only because Databricks enables massive distributed ML at low cost, scaling to millions of combinations without infrastructure sprawl. Hierarchical forecasting across store > city > region > national levels, combined with genetic optimization for inventory and replenishment, runs at production scale using Apache Spark™’s distributed compute and optimized execution engine.

title: One Year. One Lakehouse. What It Really Takes to Modernize Enterprise Data
abstract: Dr. Michael Y. Uohara, Chief Data & Analytics Officer at Hospital for Special Surgery, is leading an enterprise transformation focused on redefining how data is structured, governed, and activated across the organization. As the nation’s leading orthopedic hospital, HSS launched an 18-month initiative to implement a modern Lakehouse architecture capable of supporting enterprise-scale analytics, intelligent applications, and decision-making. A former surgeon turned data executive, Dr. Uohara brings a unique perspective to enterprise data strategy. Rather than building around isolated reporting needs, his team adopted a long-term architectural approach centered on full-system ingestion, reusable data assets, and shared enterprise standards. The result is a scalable environment designed to support both rapid delivery and increasingly sophisticated analytical capabilities across all data domains. In this session, Dr. Uohara will discuss the vision behind the organization’s Lakehouse strategy, the principles that shaped its execution, and the cultural shifts required to sustain transformation at scale. He will share lessons learned around empowering teams with autonomy, establishing clear engineering practices, and creating an operating model that balances speed, flexibility, and governance without sacrificing trust or consistency. Attendees will leave with practical insights on building a modern data organization – one that enables faster decision-making, accelerates development of comprehensive applications, and creates the foundation for long-term enterprise innovation.

Attendees will leave with practical insights on building a modern data organization – one that enables faster decision-making, accelerates development of comprehensive applications, and creates the foundation for long-term enterprise innovation.

title: Open for Business: Building the Open Lakehouse for the Agentic Age with Unity Catalog Open Source and Open Sharing
abstract: You can build a serious data-and-AI platform almost entirely from open source today. We'll grow one alongside a business — open storage and Delta, **Unity Catalog OSS**, multi-engine access on the same managed tables via the new **UC Delta APIs**, MLflow, lineage. The Open Lakehouse is real — and it already governs data well: credential vending, server-side planning, trusted compute. What those patterns share is an assumption — every request comes from a human you can hold accountable — and agents open a gap in it, reading what they're allowed to then acting in ways no one authorized, while the catalog that governed the read never sees the act. We'll show today's open governance patterns, where agents and cross-org sharing strain them, and why closing the gap — including with the new **OpenSharing** protocol — means extending governance to the platform, in the open. Context is the new data.

title: Open Streaming Meets Governed Lakehouse: Running Apache Flink With Unity Catalog–Managed Delta Tables
abstract: As organizations adopt open streaming engines like Apache Flink alongside centralized governance platforms, interoperability becomes critical. This talk explores how the Flink Delta Connector bridges Flink’s real-time processing model with Delta Lake tables managed by Unity Catalog. We’ll explain how the connector preserves Delta’s ACID guarantees, integrates with UC-managed metadata, and respects centralized governance when writes originate from external Flink clusters. Through architectural deep dives and practical examples, we show how teams can build end-to-end streaming pipelines that combine Flink’s scalability with Databricks’ unified governance and lakehouse architecture.

title: Open Table Formats for Dummies
abstract: With the enormous amount of discussion about open storage formats between nerds and even not-nerds, it can be hard to keep track of who’s doing what and how this actually makes any impact on day to day data projects. Let's take a closer look at the three big projects in this space; Delta, Hudi and Iceberg. They’re all trying to solve for similar data problems and have tackled the various challenges in different ways. This talk with start with the very basics of how we got here, what the history is before diving deep into the underlying tech, their roadmaps, and their impacts on the data landscape as a whole.

Attendees will leave with practical lessons on where enterprise AI creates value: choosing focused use cases, embedding AI into existing tools, building trust through measurement, and redesigning work so AI takes the first pass while people focus on judgment, escalation, and action.

title: Operating Databricks at Enterprise Scale: 60–70% MTTR Reduction Through SQL & AI Functions
abstract: As Databricks scales enterprise-wide, IT Operations teams face mounting challenges: controlling analytics costs, maintaining reliability and supporting business-critical workloads. A global semiconductor manufacturer leveraged Databricks SQL and AI functions to transform operations at scale—turning cost control and incident response into repeatable, automated workflows. Databricks SQL and AI functions create an autonomous optimization engine, Unity Catalog ensures enterprise governance and production-safe validation guarantees zero SLA risk. Databricks SQL provides the analytical foundation, enabling deep workload analysis through query metadata, execution plans and table statistics. AI functions layer intelligent reasoning on top, automatically generating optimized SQL, reconstructing data lineage and validating code transformations—all within the platform. These are leveraged to address five key problems and the operations team could save a significant time and achieve cost savings.

title: Operating Scalable AI for Games: From LLM Intelligence to Real-Time ML Systems
abstract: Cheating in live games does more than break the rules. It damages fairness, player trust, and the health of the service itself. In this session, KRAFTON shares how we built scalable AI systems for PUBG anti-cheat by connecting two signals: what players say outside the game and what suspicious players do inside it. We first show how noisy community feedback across languages, slang, and sarcasm can be turned into a clear operational signal using Vector Search, LLM validation, and LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation. Then we move inside the game and share how a lean engineering team evolved an ESP cheat detection system from research code into near-real-time ML pipeline on Databricks. Along the way, we discuss the practical tradeoffs behind latency, cost reduction, feature consistency, serving stability, and scale-out architecture.

title: Optimize Lakehouse Cost and Performance With Intelligent Storage and Liquid Clustering
abstract: Optimizing cost and performance in the lakehouse starts with how your data is stored and organized. In this session, we’ll show how Intelligent Storage and Liquid Clustering work together to automatically optimize data layout for your workloads. You’ll get a quick refresher on Liquid Clustering, then dive into what’s new, including Automatic Liquid Clustering on Unity Catalog managed tables, adaptive layouts that handle evolving query patterns, and metadata-driven optimizations that reduce unnecessary data scans. More importantly, we’ll cover best practices for when and how to rely on automation versus manual tuning. Learn how to choose the right table types, avoid common pitfalls, and take advantage of co-clustered joins and layout-aware optimizations to accelerate queries at scale. Whether you’re managing terabytes or petabytes, walk away with practical guidance to reduce costs and improve performance without constant intervention.

title: Petabytes in Plain Sight: Extending Databricks to the On-Prem Data You Already Have
abstract: Every enterprise building a lakehouse hits the same wall: the most valuable data lives on-premises. You can mask it. Tokenize it. Replicate a fraction. But data bound by HIPAA, GDPR, or sovereignty mandates cannot leave at all. Either way, Databricks never sees the full picture.Until now.MinIO and Databricks have solved this by embedding open sharing protocols directly into the data foundation. When your data foundation natively speaks open sharing protocols, data movement becomes unnecessary. Databricks queries on-prem tables directly, in place with full governance retained by the data owner.MinIO CTO Ugur Tigli shows how customer demand drove MinIO and Databricks to run analytics on full-fidelity production data on-prem through open protocols like Delta Sharing and the Apache Iceberg™ REST API. He covers what happens to your security posture when pipelines disappear, what it means when you unlock petabytes to become first-class Databricks assets.

title: Phar Lakehouse: The Evolution of Our Data Market
abstract: As organizations migrate to the lakehouse architecture, they often struggle with the fragmented management of physical storage, authentication, and logical governance layers. This session introduces "Phar Lakehouse," a robust data product designed to standardize and automate the deployment of Databricks Unity Catalog across complex enterprise environments. We will explore how the Phar Data Platform team leveraged infrastructure as code (Terraform) to transform disjointed infrastructure tasks into a unified “black box” process. By providing a standardized storage foundation based on the Medallion Architecture, Phar Lakehouse enables squads to deploy tailored schemas—including specialized Utilities and PII-secure layers—without manual overhead.

In this session, NAB shares how it implemented Databricks Genie as a first‑class engineering capability, from early prototypes to bank‑wide adoption. We will walk through the key decisions and patterns that made Genie genuinely useful for technical teams: how it integrates with existing SDLC and data workflows, how NAB approached onboarding and change management, and examples of high-value use cases and how their benefits were measured. title: Pipeline to Production in Minutes: How a Leading P&C Insurer Achieved End-to-End DevOps on Databricks
abstract: P&C insurance data platforms must deliver analytics rapidly while meeting stringent governance and regulatory requirements. Although Databricks is widely adopted as the analytics backbone, many P&C organizations continue to struggle with inconsistent deployments, manual promotions and fragmented DevOps practices. This lightning talk demonstrates how a P&C organization implemented true end-to-end DevOps on Databricks using Asset Bundles, Databricks Apps and GitHub Actions. Learn how a Git-driven, declarative deployment model uses Asset Bundles to package notebooks, workflows and DLT pipelines with environment-aware configuration, enabling consistent promotion across multiple environments, while GitHub Actions orchestrates CI/CD pipelines for validation, automated deployment and auditability. The session highlights how Databricks Apps are integrated into the same pipeline to operationalize analytics use cases as secure, production-ready data product governed by Unity Catalog.

title: Pitch Data to Player Insights: How the Cleveland Guardians Use AI and Real-Time Analytics at Scale
abstract: The Cleveland Guardians run a real-time data and AI platform that ingests live game feeds, scores every pitch with neural network models, and delivers AI-powered scouting insights to analysts through natural language tools.Behind the scenes, this system supports high-stakes, in-game decisions. Built on Databricks, it combines streaming ingestion, ETL pipelines, model serving, and live dashboards. The challenge was not just building it, but deploying it across dev, QA, and production without slowing innovation.In this session, we will share how we standardized and scaled the platform using Databricks Asset Bundles. By consolidating assets into a version-controlled monorepo, we created a unified deployment framework for modular jobs, shared clusters, coordinated builds, and post-deployment orchestration.You will leave with a practical blueprint for operationalizing a modern data and generative AI platform, plus candid lessons on what worked and what we would refine.

title: Prada Group Serves High-Quality Business Metrics with Lakebase
abstract: Prada Group's advanced analytics and KPI calculations had evolved across multiple disconnected systems, each serving different teams and use cases. This fragmentation made it difficult to maintain consistent definitions, reuse existing logic, and deliver a single trusted view of performance across the business. As data volumes and reporting demands increased, the organization needed a way to reliably manage and compute thousands of KPIs across regions, product categories, and time periods while still providing fast, decision-ready insights. To address this, Prada Group implemented a unified analytics architecture supported by Lakebase as its central data foundation. Lakebase consolidated previously siloed data into a single governed and scalable environment, enabling high-volume storage, efficient querying, and low-latency KPI computation. On top of this foundation, a standardized KPI model and microservices-based APIs provided consistent, easily accessible analytics across departments and systems, transforming fragmented reporting into a trusted, enterprise-wide capability for data-driven decision making.

title: Predictable Migrations: Scaling Lakebase Adoption With Provider-Agnostic Readiness Tools
abstract: Successful migration from managed OLTP services to Lakebase depends on one factor: identifying architectural nuances before the transition begins. Instead of a “move-and-fix” approach, teams need a rigorous, automated way to audit environments and quantify technical debt. This session introduces a unified readiness assessment framework designed to evaluate any managed OLTP workload for Lakebase compatibility. We will explore how an automated engine interrogates database metadata to audit schemas, extensions, and configuration limits. By analyzing version disparities and provider-specific constraints, the tool generates a high-fidelity compatibility roadmap. This approach allows architects to identify blockers early, estimate refactoring with precision and build a high-integrity execution plan. Attendees will learn to standardize pre-migration checks, transforming a high-stakes transition into a predictable, well-orchestrated architectural upgrade.

title: Press Start: From Gaming to Real-Time Analytics with Databricks Apps
abstract: What if classic video games could teach you new tricks — and what if community gameplay data could power automation? Join Andrew Sitz (Databricks MVP) and Scott Haines (Staff Developer Advocate) as they build a live gaming environment on Databricks. We'll load a Game from Unity Catalog Volumes, host interactive gameplay through Databricks Apps, and capture every input and state change as streaming data. Using Lakebase and Delta Lake, we persist player sessions, track progress, and serve real-time leaderboards with low latency and full ACID guarantees. From there, we explore how aggregate play data reveals community patterns — surfacing strategies and insights players might never find alone. Finally, we show how recorded gameplay can train simple automation strategies, closing the loop from observation to action. Come for the nostalgia, stay for the data engineering.

title: Privacy-Centric Identity Resolution for Analytics and Activation
abstract: Identity resolution sits at the core of modern data and AI. As signals disappear and privacy constraints tighten, the ability to unify fragmented customer records across partners directly impacts data quality, analytics accuracy, and model performance. In this session, we show how Databricks Clean Rooms enable organizations to build a trusted view of customer data by resolving identities across datasets without exposing raw PII. Join us for a technical deep dive with LiveRamp as we demonstrate how a durable identity backbone supports accurate, privacy-safe matching across organizations. You will learn how to standardize fragmented data into interoperable models, improve match rates, and unlock higher-fidelity analytics through governed collaboration using Clean Rooms. We will also cover practical implementation patterns, including enforcing privacy controls and scaling compliant collaboration across multiple partners. The result is a foundation for identity-first analytics that improves your marketing outcomes while maintaining strong privacy standards.

title: Proactive Cyber Defense with Global Cyber Threat Intelligence, Scaled Analytics and AI Acceleration
abstract: In 2025, the Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) provider ecosystem produced over 1.9 trillion data points delivered in over 100,000 data feeds that describe threat actors, their tactics, techniques & procedures (TTPs) and related indicators of compromise. To leverage this global CTI for proactive defense against these attacks, all the data must be consumed, analyzed and operationalized in real-time - any delays create exploitable gaps that can lead to infiltration, data theft, extortion and malicious outcomes. This session will provide insights into the challenges and successes in the designing of a scalable intelligence analytics and operations platform that streams global CTI from its sources into Databricks to enable human and autonomous classification, triaging and deployment of actionable threat indicators and context within minutes of ingestion.

title: Production Lakebase Patterns: OAuth Token Lifecycle, Async Pooling, and Caching for Databricks Apps
abstract: Lakebase gives you PostgreSQL on Databricks, but production applications need patterns the documentation doesn't cover. From deploying a conversation persistence layer for an energy sector knowledge assistant, we share battle-tested solutions: Proactive OAuth token refresh that recreates connection pools before credentials expire, async connection pooling with psycopg3 sized for Databricks Apps concurrency, LRU caching with TTL for high-frequency thread lookups, and upsert patterns with conflict resolution for concurrent agent writes. Every pattern is production code running on Databricks Apps today. This lightning talk is for developers who've tried Lakebase in a notebook and want to know what it takes to run it in a real application with real users.

title: Production Patterns for Multi-Tenant AI: Scaling to 800 Banks on Databricks
abstract: Serving 800 German banks on one AI platform required solving a fundamental multi-tenant challenge: maintaining strict data isolation while scaling to hundreds of QPS under banking regulations. We present two innovations:1. Metadata-driven capacity management: Delta tables track index capacity per endpoint in real-time. When thresholds are reached, the system provisions new Vector Search endpoints and rebalances indexes. This eliminates manual scaling interventions and provides a reusable pattern for any platform hitting infrastructure limits at scale.2. Hierarchical retrieval with RAPTOR: Plain Agents retrieve flat chunks. We implement recursive clustering and summarization to build tree structures, enabling retrieval across abstraction levels, from granular details to high-level themes. This approach significantly improves answer quality for complex financial documents.Takeaways: federated vector search patterns, metadata-driven auto-scaling architecture, RAPTOR implementation

title: Provisioning for the Agentic Era: How Databricks Built a Self-Serve Infrastructure Vending Machine
abstract: As Databricks' go-to-market organization grew past 7,000 people — and AI agents became first-class consumers of platform resources alongside human engineers — our field team ran into a familiar problem: shared demo environments couldn't keep up. Too many users needed admin-level access, platform limits became real constraints, and it was hard to see who was using what, whether that "who" was a person or an agent. In this session, we'll share how we addressed that by building the Field Engineering Vending Machine (FEVM), a Databricks App that gives every engineer — and every agent — just-in-time, isolated, and governed environments on demand. Instead of filing tickets or juggling shared workspaces, engineers describe what they're trying to do — build a demo, run a hackathon, reproduce an issue, spin up an agentic workflow — and FEVM delivers a fit-for-purpose environment in minutes, then cleans it up automatically when it's no longer needed. We'll show how this "vending machine" model has improved speed, control, and cost visibility for thousands of users and countless agent runs, and why building it as a Databricks App has become a blueprint for how we dogfood the platform internally — for the agentic era and beyond.
