title: Rakuten’s Journey from Data Silos to Unified Intelligence
abstract: Rakuten Group's 70+ businesses span e-commerce, fintech, mobile, and more across 30+ countries and regions, serving 2.1B+ global members and ¥48.7T (approx. $300B) global gross transaction value in 2025—one of the world's largest interconnected digital ecosystems. title: Rate the Hype: NL-to-SQL and Governance without the Vendor Tax
abstract: Every year the modern data/AI landscape gets more crowded. Honest opinions about what's worth building are rare. We took some of the loudest trends (open table formats, semantic layers, MCP servers, vector databases, data mesh, and data governance) and rated each one: Adopt Now, Experiment, Watch, or Ignore. Not based on vendor pitches but on what we've deployed at Abridge, an AI-native healthcare company where we process clinical conversations under HIPAA in real time. Then we will prove it. We will present a natural language to SQL interface that 10xed data-to-insight speed for our consumers. A HIPPA scanner that shows governance doesn't require a vendor. Two engineers, two demos, and field-tested answers on what to ship in production and what you can skip.

title: Real-Time Context Engineering for AI With Databricks
abstract: Just like we don’t put crude oil in a car, we refine it into gasoline. AI can’t run on raw data either. It needs continuous, refined context. Serving fresh context is the missing architectural layer for reliable AI. In this session, learn how Confluent Intelligence and Databricks turn operational data into low-latency context for AI agents and applications. See how Confluent’s fully managed streaming platform feeds trusted data into the Databricks lakehouse for Agent Bricks and AI/BI. We’ll demo real-time architectures for anomaly detection, product personalization, and AI-powered data enrichment, showing how to keep ML models and LLMs grounded in the live state of your business, not stale batch snapshots. You’ll leave with practical, streaming-native patterns to move from brittle pipelines and demos to production-grade AI on Databricks while reducing TCO.

title: Real-Time ML Features for Payment Fraud: Architecture Patterns at Scale
abstract: Checkout.com is a leading global digital payments provider, processing over $300 billion in e-commerce volume annually. Our fraud models depend on fresh features, but batch pipelines limited how quickly we could detect new fraud patterns. In this session, we’ll show how we built real-time feature pipelines using Spark Structured Streaming on Databricks, reducing feature computation to a few seconds and unlocking an eight-figure revenue opportunity. We’ll cover our technical approach, including custom stateful aggregations with transformWithStateInPandas, event-time watermarking for late payments, and TTL-based state management for deduplication. We’ll also discuss cost optimization at billion-event scale, and consistency between online and offline features. By incorporating real-time features into our fraud models, we achieved a 2% increase in PR-AUC, translating into millions in prevented fraud losses - offering a practical blueprint for real-time machine learning at scale.

title: Rebuilding the Data Foundation Behind 8% of Brazil's GDP
abstract: Cielo, a leading LATAM payment processor, operated a fragmented analytics landscape across AWS EMR, Oracle Exadata/DW, and decentralized governance. This architecture increased operational overhead, limited lineage and observability, and constrained AI adoption.In this session, we present how Cielo migrated multiple enterprise-grade platforms to a unified Databricks Lakehouse. Over 6,500 pipelines were assessed and over 3,000 legacy jobs eliminated. The migration leveraged Delta Lake, serverless compute, standardized engineering patterns, and Unity Catalog–ready governance.Key takeaways include a ~40% cost reduction in ingestion pipelines, improved reliability and reprocessing, and more than 1,000 users enabled through self-service analytics. We also share practical migration patterns from AWS EMR and Oracle Exadata/DW to Databricks, governance-by-design lessons, and how AI-assisted refactoring accelerated modernization while improving developer productivity.

title: Redact at the Speed of AI: De‑identifying PII in the Lakehouse with ai_query
abstract: Teams need to unlock data responsibly. This lightning talk shows how to use AI Functions—specifically ai_query—to automatically redact PII across both structured tables and unstructured documents in Databricks.We'll walk through how it works for tabular data, then show how the same pattern extends to free-text fields like clinical notes. We'll briefly touch on batching for throughput and checking output quality. A brief live demo runs against realistic unstructured healthcare notes, de-identifying patient information so analysts and ML teams can experiment without risk. You'll leave with reusable queries, sample prompts for both structured and unstructured redaction, and a practical starting point to operationalize PII redaction in your Lakehouse.

title: Redefining Detection Engineering With Interactive AI Agents in the SOC
abstract: AI is transforming how Security Operations Centers (SOCs) operate, with tools that augment detection engineers and analysts to combat threats. We show how one SOC at a major hedge fund adopted AI to enhance detection engineering, accelerating creation, and minimizing response time. By integrating the Mosaic AI Agent Framework with Databricks Notebooks & Apps, this SOC provided detection engineers an AI assistant within their existing workflow. This agent accelerates detection baselining, anomaly detection, and filtering false positives while giving engineers control over final logic, ensuring human expertise remains central. The modular architecture enables adding capabilities like MITRE ATT&CK mapping, threat intelligence enrichment, and custom patterns without rewriting core logic. We demonstrate this assistant and how Databricks AI tools, including Genie and MLflow Evaluation, contribute to faster development, increased efficiency, and shortened response times to emerging threats.

title: Reinventing Operational Scale through Agentic Underwriting
abstract: CFC as a Lloyd's of London leading Cyber speciality insurer, is globally scaling our business by amplifying every Underwriter. For this we've created the "Agentic Underwriter" in production to augment critical steps in the underwriting journey. By combining Databricks' delta lake architecture with modern LLMOps processes and open source frameworks like LangGraph we've rapidly created agents capable of creating fully fledged quotes. The agent is able to intelligently navigate our systems & the complexities of the speciality lines insurance process to deliver ready made quotes for our underwriters to confirm or adjust via a HITL process. The result is our underwriters have trusted quotes ready in 5 minutes vs 24 hours - a 99% time decrease. Equated to cost, we have quotes ready for £0.50 vs £5 - a 90% cost decrease. Our customers are feeling the impact with quotes arriving faster and prices more competitive. In this way, we have created the industry's first true agentic underwriter.

title: Replace your Legacy SIEM with Lakewatch: Build Your Own Custom Apps with Lakehouse & Lakebase
abstract: Many legacy SIEMs charge on ingestion, lock data behind proprietary formats, and limit AI customization. Databricks Lakewatch changes that. As the Open Security Lakehouse, Lakewatch lands 100% of your telemetry in open formats on Delta Lake — and because the data is open, security teams can pull any signal into custom apps built natively on Databricks. This session walks through a production SecOps platform on Lakewatch, ingesting 13TB/day across 22 sources at up to 80% lower cost. OCSF-normalized SDP pipelines deliver sub-15-minute detection with 94% MITRE ATT&CK coverage. A React + FastAPI app on Databricks Apps, backed by Lakebase, shows the art of the possible — AI threat hunting with Claude and custom analyst workflows no prebuilt SIEM could surface.

abstract: Supply chain volatility is the new normal, and the old playbook of siloed forecasting, batch EDI, and reactive logistics can't keep up. The next frontier of CPG-retail performance isn't just efficiency; it's collaboration. Leading companies are replacing linear supply chains with intelligent networks that sense and respond in real time, unifying retailer POS, demand signals, and inventory data to power AI models that continuously optimize forecasting, replenishment, and risk detection. And they're doing it on a single, governed platform where shared data fuels not just dashboards and insights, but AI agents that act autonomously— triggering replenishment, reallocating inventory, and adjusting plans the moment conditions change. In this session, hear directly from the retailers and CPGs making this shift. Learn how open data sharing, AI-powered demand sensing, and joint planning on Databricks are turning adversarial transactions into growth partnerships, and why the companies that collaborate on data today will own the shelf tomorrow.

title: Rethinking Database Cost with Lakebase Autoscaling
abstract: Traditional databases charge you whether you use them or not. title: Revolutionizing Construction Intelligence: Scaling Procore Analytics With Delta Sharing & AI
abstract: Procore serves as the backbone for global construction data. Historically, providing seamless access to large-scale analytics meant complex ETL pipelines and high egress costs. Attendees will learn how the open Delta Sharing protocol enables frictionless “Bring Your Own Warehouse” capabilities, reducing TCO and latency. We’ll share technical lessons on optimizing cross-cloud performance and building an AI-ready foundation for the world’s most complex industry.

title: Right Features, Right Time: Modernizing Real-Time Fraud Feature Serving on Databricks
abstract: Fraud does not wait for batch. To block funds from moving, Coinbase models need the right features at the right time—fresh, consistent, and served with predictable low latency.This session explains Coinbase’s Databricks-based feature platform for real-time fraud ML: Real-Time Mode on Structured Streaming; declarative Feature APIs + CI/CD (features as code); AI/agent-assisted migration and feature creation; and Lakebase feature serving targeting p99 90% streaming infra cost reduction and up to >95% p99 freshness improvement. Moving self-built batch feature sets to a managed feature store is also driving an estimated ~25–35% productivity gain by retiring bespoke pipelines and shrinking the on-call surface. Attendees leave with a reference architecture + migration playbook across latency, reliability, and TCO.

title: Running LLaMA at Scale: Production Inference on Databricks Model Serving
abstract: Serving LLMs at consumer scale stresses everything: throughput, latency, correctness and cost. At Superhuman—formerly Grammarly—we built a production system that serves a fine‑tuned LLaMA‑3B model for grammatical error correction to millions of monthly users on Databricks Model Serving. This talk shares what we validated and how: direct‑ingress patterns for high RPS, load testing toward 100K+ QPS targets, multi‑region failover and cold‑start mitigation, and observability. We’ll cover validation checks—A/B tests, golden sets—plus the cost model we used to compare against our internal vLLM-based stack, including levers like dynamic batching, autoscaling and speculative decoding. Expect concrete configs, dashboards and a candid readout of wins, incidents and unit‑economics tradeoffs that informed our ramp from pilot to majority traffic.

title: Safe Skies: Automating Trust at Scale With AI-Generated Contracts at Boeing
abstract: In aviation, "bad data" is an operational risk. For large enterprises with hundreds of data products, manual stewardship stifles innovation. To ensure "safe skies," we transformed governance and quality into engineering disciplines. This session explores our "Governance as Code" architecture using DQX and Ontos on Unity Catalog. We demonstrate using GenAI to bootstrap trust, scanning raw data to auto-generate Open Data Contract Standards (ODCSq). We then show how DQX acts as the enforcer, compiling contracts into pipelines that quarantine violations and alert on drift. AI-assisted contracts: Using LLMs to profile data and draft rigorous ODCS contracts, cutting onboarding time. Automated quality: Deploying DQX to enforce row-level quality, quarantine bad data and trigger drift alerts. Semantics-first: Using Ontos to map technical assets to business meaning for a discoverable data marketplace. Join us to learn how we replaced bureaucracy with automation and engineering rigor.

title: Santander's Move to Cloud: How One of the World's Largest Banks Rearchitected Its Data Foundation
abstract: The Move to Cloud initiative represents far more than a technological migration; it marks a milestone in the bank’s digital transformation journey. Delivered through collaboration across data platform, data engineering, infrastructure, architecture and centralized ingestion, it established a new foundation for data. The program migrated 16 petabytes from Cloudera and ScyllaDB environments to a modern, secure and scalable cloud architecture, increasing speed, efficiency and resilience for business growth and data-driven decisions. More than a project, it transformed how the bank manages and values data, positioning technology as a driver of competitiveness and future innovation.

title: Scale Trust, Not Headcount: AI-Powered Semantic Engineering at Southern Glazer’s Wine & Spirits
abstract: Trust in business decisions erode when reports, AI Agents, and operational systems provide different values for the same KPIs. The solution is a unified semantic fabric in which KPIs are managed as versioned, testable, and reusable assets—like software—implemented entirely within Databricks without added tooling overhead. Organizations no longer need hordes of data and semantic engineers, manually coding pipelines and maintaining definitions. With AI agents automating data transformations, semantic alignment, and business rule updates, organizations can reduce manual engineering effort, accelerate delivery, and lower operating costs while improving data trust. This session showcases how Southern Glazer's Wine & Spirits is implementing an AI-augmented approach to build their Metrics Bank and Semantic Layer in Databricks. You'll discover real-world results: reduced manual engineering effort, accelerated time-to-insight, and scaled decision-making capabilities across the enterprise.

title: Scaling AI Agents at Mercedes-Benz: Unified AI Governance in a Multi-Cloud Enterprise Ecosystem
abstract: Managing AI at the scale of Mercedes-Benz requires more than just models—it requires a unified AI ecosystem. With thousands of practitioners across global business units, the challenge was providing a single point of entry for AI capabilities while maintaining strict governance across multi-cloud and multi-model environments. In this session, we go under the hood of the Mercedes-Benz. AI Ecosystem. We will detail the technical architecture that integrates Databricks Agent Framework, Model Serving, and AI Gateway to create a governed interoperability for AI agents. We’ll discuss the "how-to" of: Centralizing discovery: Building an internal marketplace for foundation models and reusable agents Unified governance: Integrating Mercedes-Benz AI Marketplace into Databricks AI Gateway Operationalizing agents: Deploying and publishing AI agents for self-service at Mercedes-Benz Attendees will leave with a technical blueprint for building an interoperable enterprise AI agent platform.

title: Scaling App Development Beyond the Data Team
abstract: The next wave of enterprise app development isn't coming from IT or data engineering alone — it's coming from everyone. Business users are building apps and agents. And admins are left figuring out how to govern an explosion of applications they didn't deploy and can't fully see.In this session, we'll cover where enterprise app development is headed, what it means for the teams responsible for keeping things secure and cost-effective, and how Databricks Apps is evolving to give builders the freedom they need and admins the control they require. Tune in for the Apps roadmap, vision, and a look at what's coming soon.

title: Scaling at Scale: The Journey of RAIP and Genie Code at Repsol
abstract: Since launching its digital transformation program in 2018, Repsol has developed RAIP, Repsol Artificial Intelligence Products, a framework that encapsulates years of analytical expertise and supports hundreds of production-grade AI models across the organization. Within RAIP, solutions such as REPSENS for time series forecasting have been validated in demanding industrial environments. With the rise of generative AI, rather than treating it as a separate paradigm, we focus on integrating generative capabilities with proven AI assets to maximize impact. In this session, we present ho Genie Code builds on RAIP to automate advanced workflows such as time series forecasting. We also compare this approach with foundation models such as TimeGPT and Chronos, and discuss how this agentic paradigm extends to pricing and optimization use cases. It augments existing AI models while preserving governance, reliability, and operational control and democratizes access to RAIP across business units.

title: Scaling Custom LLMs with vLLM and Databricks Model Serving: Fast, Flexible, and Production-Ready
abstract: Databricks Model Serving supports deployments ranging from classical ML models on custom-CPU workloads to foundation models with dedicated provisioned throughput endpoints. But what about the use-cases that need any of the 1000s of other open-source or fine-tuned LLMs? Deploying them efficiently can be challenging. This breakout session explores deploying LLMs on custom-GPU endpoints with vLLM. In it, we’ll examine: Serverless GPU Compute: How it simplifies the deployment process, saving hours on configuration work alone. vLLM + GPU workloads: How they work in tandem on the platform to deliver high-throughput inference with scalable infrastructure. Implementation: A step-by-step code walkthrough for packaging models, configuring vLLM runtime, and deployment! Serving LLMs on GPUs doesn’t have to be scary. Learn more about how Databricks enables you to deploy even your most demanding model serving workloads!

title: Scaling Cybersecurity Analytics Without Scaling Costs
abstract: Cybersecurity teams often struggle with the cost and scale of analyzing massive telemetry. JetBlue solved this by building a security-first analytics platform on the Databricks lakehouse. By leveraging Delta Lake, Auto Loader, and Databricks SQL, JetBlue ingests high-cardinality data into low-cost cloud storage, applying compute only when necessary. This enables long-term retention and flexible analysis that legacy tools find prohibitively expensive. Using Databricks SQL, they developed a fastly-focused security layer to: Detect anomalies and bot abuse Measure CAPTCHA effectiveness Analyze attack trends by IP, geography, and path Support real-time and historical investigations Decoupling storage from compute resulted in faster investigations, better visibility, and significant savings. Attendees will learn how to use Databricks to scale detection and investigation workflows cost-effectively.

title: Scaling Data and AI Trust: How Credicorp Built a Cross-Institution Data Product Marketplace
abstract: As financial groups scale across regions and subsidiaries, the challenge is no longer collecting data; it’s governing, sharing and trusting it at an enterprise level. Eduardo Torres, CDO at Credicorp and Alvaro Villanueva, Credicorp’s Data Marketplace Product Owner, will share their team’s journey to building a data product marketplace that spans financial institutions and countries using Databricks Unity Catalog. Torres & Villanueva will share how they built a reliability layer at the foundation of their data product marketplace with data and AI observability, enabling multiple subsidiaries to publish and discover trusted data products without costly duplication or security risk. They will dive into the team’s approach to key challenges, including operating models, incentives and change management when subsidiaries are also competitors. Attendees will learn how trusted data across a data product marketplace unlocks a unified customer view, and real business impact at enterprise scale.

title: Scaling Databricks Genie 10x at GSK Global Supply Chain: Building a Production AI/BI Factory
abstract: Most organizations don't struggle to prototype conversational AI—they struggle to get it reliably into production at scale. At GSK's Global Supply Chain, operating across 37 GMP-regulated manufacturing sites with thousands of daily decisions, we built an AI/BI factory designed to move Databricks Genie from early experimentation to enterprise-grade production—serving analysts, planners and decision-makers across a complex, regulated environment. This talk explores the journey from pilot to platform: how we scaled Genie 10x by treating it not as a standalone tool, but as a production system embedded in a broader agent operating model—one that fuses technology, process, governance and organizational ways of working into a repeatable delivery engine. What we’ll cover: Genie Spaces lessons learned and best practices Enterprise observability dashboard for Genie CI/CD migration and deployment automation for DevOps Semantic caching for Genie

title: Scaling Energy Deal Evaluation With Databricks Lakebase
abstract: Quantum Capital Group screens hundreds of energy investment opportunities each year, supported by more than 1.5 billion records across public, premium and proprietary datasets. While its Databricks Lakehouse already provided a scalable and governed foundation, the next challenge was enabling teams and downstream tools to work more efficiently from the same trusted data as deal volume and complexity increased. In this session, Quantum shares how it extended its Lakehouse with Databricks Lakebase to introduce relational structure and familiarity without sacrificing openness or scale. Attendees will learn how Lakebase integrates with Delta Lake, Unity Catalog and Lakeflow to support governed, materialized datasets that teams can access using SQL, geospatial tools and existing analytics platforms. The talk focuses on how relational access and governance helped Quantum scale human-led diligence across engineering and investment teams, evaluate complex deals with greater confidence.

title: Scaling Executive-Ready Insight With Databricks AI Query on AI/BI
abstract: Creating executive-ready metric summaries is harder than it looks. Leaders expect insights that are accurate, consistent, action-oriented, and concise, yet many organizations still rely on manual reporting — driving high effort, slow turnaround, and inconsistent interpretation. In this session, we share a real-world example of sales strategy and analytics teams automating daily pipeline summaries using Databricks AI Query within an AI/BI dashboard. Each summary previously took ~30 minutes per territory—an estimated 36,000 manual hours annually. By standardizing business logic, strengthening the Databricks data foundation, and applying AI selectively, we scaled executive-ready insights to hundreds of leaders. The key lesson: 80% of impact comes from clear strategy logic and trusted data — AI delivers the final 20% by generating consistent natural-language summaries at scale. Attendees will learn a practical model to encode executive expectations, govern AI outputs, and reduce time to insight.

title: Scaling for MHHS: Octopus Energy’s 50x Cost-Efficient Margin Data Engineering
abstract: As the global energy system moves to intermittent renewables, the challenge for data engineering is providing a clear signal to consumers for when the energy is at cheapest and cleanest. This talk is for data engineers and leaders navigating the UK’s Market-wide Half-Hourly Settlement (MHHS) transition. Facing a 48x surge in data volume for 8M+ customers, Octopus Energy re-engineered its margin systems to bridge the gap between monthly billing and half-hourly settlement.The Results:Data Efficiency: 98.8% reduction in rows processed (from 25B to 300M).Cost Savings: 50x cost reduction per settlement date, avoiding $1M in annual infrastructure increases.Velocity: Improved data freshness from weekly to daily.By decoupling the pipeline into grain-specific modules and applying Spark and Incremental optimisations, we transformed a regulatory hurdle into a scalable engine for margin visibility. Aligning your data architecture with the business logic enables a sustainable energy future.

title: Scaling Governed AI Beyond PoCs: A Public Sector Agent Architecture With Lakebase and AgentBricks
abstract: Many AI pilots succeed, but productionisation remains difficult in regulated environments where governance, auditability and state management are required. This session is grounded in Skills SA’s Organisational Self-Assessment (OSA) process, a compliance-driven workflow combining structured operational metadata and unstructured free-text submissions. Around 200 assessments are reviewed annually, requiring significant assessor effort (~1,800 hours) We present a multi-agent architecture built on Databricks Lakebase and AgentBricks. A single Databricks App invokes specialised agents via AgentBricks. OSA data is stored in Delta tables, with Lakebase providing operational state management and governance. Agent prompts and scoring rules are versioned as governed data, and AI/BI Genie is used for natural-language queries over operational metadata. Attendees will learn practical patterns for running production AI systems in regulated environments.

title: Scaling Micro-Offers With Hybrid AI
abstract: This work proposes a pipeline for responsible investment offer personalization in Brazilian Open Finance, integrating data governance, segmentation (K-Means), propensity modeling (Random Forest) and an ethical filtering layer via LLM-based digital twins. Applied to 427,929 Caixa Econômica Federal customers, the model achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.57. Digital twin validation reduced the high-propensity pool from 213,764 to 6,543 eligibles, applying suitability rules and generating auditable justifications to mitigate overcontact. Distributive analysis indicated a concentration of offers among higher-income profiles. In a pilot within the My Wallet app, the approach yielded a 21.0% positive intention rate, surpassing the 3–5% generic average. Results suggest that combining Open Finance, ML and GenAI enhances assertiveness and algorithmic governance, highlighting the need for formal fairness metrics and large-scale causal experiments.

title: Secure External Data Access with Connections, Secrets, and Functions in Unity Catalog
abstract: Modern data platforms are rarely islands; they exist in a sprawling ecosystem of external databases, APIs, and third-party services. However, managing the "connective tissue"—JDBC drivers, secret rotation, and custom logic—often creates security silos and governance gaps. In this session, we will hands-on demonstrate how the next generation of Unity Catalog Connections, Secrets and Functions work in concert to centralize external data access, eliminate hardcoded credentials, and deploy governed UDFs across any compute type. Attendees will learn how to build a "zero-trust" data architecture that simplifies the user experience while providing full lineage and auditability from the source to the final insight.

title: Securing Agentic AI on Databricks: From Experimentation to Enterprise Grade Systems
abstract: Agentic AI systems—where LLM-powered agents plan, reason, and act across data and tools—are rapidly moving from proof-of-concept to mission-critical production. However, this shift introduces a new security surface: autonomous decision-making, dynamic tool use, and data access at scale. How do you innovate without compromising security, governance, or compliance? In this session, we explore how to build secure, enterprise-ready agentic systems on Databricks. Designed for practitioners and architects, we break down the unique risks of agentic workflows and map them to concrete controls. We will introduce the Databricks Agentic AI Security Framework developed with top researchers from OWASP, NIST, and Fortune 100 companies. Key Takeaways: Reference architectures for deploying secure agentic AI at scale. A framework to operationalize and explain your security posture to cyber teams. Actionable tools, including a worksheet and live demo, to test your deployments and MCP security.

title: Securing Data and AI for the Enterprise: What’s New in Databricks Platform Security
abstract: Databricks is shipping a wave of platform security, networking and compliance capabilities that make enterprise-grade protection the default — not an afterthought. In this session, we cover the highlights including Private Network Gateway for managed, secure connectivity to your data sources, context-based ingress policies that bring adaptive network controls to Genie, apps, AI/BI, and agentic workloads and cloudless compute with a cross-cloud backbone that simplifies networking across environments. We’ll also showcase automatic identity management (AIM), which automates identity provisioning and enforces least-privilege at scale. Plus, secure cross-workspace access, serverless egress logs, account frontend private link, CMK for UC Catalogs and more. Come see how Databricks is making security a platform advantage.

title: Securing the Grid: Modernizing E&U Security Operations with Lakewatch (AI-Native SIEM)
abstract: Energy & Utilities (E&U) face a perfect storm: surging OT/ICS ransomware, strict NERC CIP/TSA regulations, and an explosion of IT/OT telemetry. Traditional SIEMs, hampered by ingest-based pricing and data silos, can no longer keep pace. Enter Lakewatch: Databricks’ open, AI-native SIEM, built natively on the Lakehouse. This session provides insights from Energy Queensland's journey of navigating the challenges of traditional SIEM and the impact a security lakehouse on Databricks can deliver. We'll discuss how Databricks Lakewatch, the lakehouse-native SIEM, eliminates "ingest taxes" and unifies IT, cloud, and OT logs through OCSF-aligned schemas; how SQL-based detection engineering and agentic threat hunting open up petabytes of historical data in seconds; and how an open, decoupled storage and compute architecture delivers the visibility, long-term retention, and AI-readiness critical infrastructure operators need to increase their situational awareness.

title: Security at Anthropic: Building D&R for an AI-Native Company
abstract: As AI systems become critical infrastructure, security teams face a new challenge: how do you defend an AI-native company at the speed and scale that modern threats demand? In this session, Jackie Bow, Technical Lead of Threat Detection Engineering at Anthropic, shares how her team thinks about building detection and response capabilities purpose-built for an AI company including the architectural decisions, tradeoffs, and lessons learned along the way.Jackie will offer a practitioner's perspective on what it takes to operate a security function inside one of the world's leading AI labs, including incorporating agentic workflows alongside more traditional D&R tooling.In the final segment, a Databricks product leader will connect these themes to Lakewatch, Databricks' new open, agentic SIEM and explore how the Security Lakehouse architecture is designed to help security teams modernize detection and response at enterprise scale.

title: Self-Healing Product Catalogs: Drift-Aware Computer Vision for Retail & CPG on Databricks
abstract: Product catalogs are living things — new packaging, regional variants, seasonal SKUs are always cycling through — and every change impacts the model's accuracy. Neurolabs runs image recognition across 20,000+ SKUs in 28 markets, generating millions of shelf crops every month. Most are routine; only a handful contain the signal that makes the next model better — a new pack variant, a misclassified flavour, a confused competitor. We've moved that selection loop onto Databricks. Inference results land in Delta, every crop is scored for training value, and Unity Catalog governs which crops feed the next model and surfaces catalog-health metrics back to the CPG brands that own the SKUs. The result: a product catalog that heals itself, and a computer vision model that gets sharper with every shelf photo.

title: Semantic Modeling Best Practices for BI and AI
abstract: AI is making self-service data real, but it creates a new challenge: ensuring humans and AI interpret data the same way. When logic is fragmented across tools, inconsistencies emerge, trust erodes, and AI insights become unreliable.Databricks addresses this with a unified approach to semantics across BI and AI. UC Business Semantics provide governed definitions, AI/BI Dashboards add local semantics, and the Genie Knowledge Store adds domain context to improve how AI answers. Together, these layers enable consistent BI and accurate AI. We’ll cover best practices for designing and operationalizing semantics across Unity Catalog, dashboards, and Genie:- Define and manage UC Business Semantics for governed metrics and dimensions- Use Dashboard Semantic Models and Metric Views for report logic- Use Genie Knowledge Store to improve AI accuracy with domain context and SQL- Combine central semantics and local curation across BI and AI- Avoid common pitfalls in semantic modeling

title: Serverless at Bank Scale: NAB's Complete Workload Migration to Serverless at Enterprise Scale
abstract: Explore how National Australia Bank (NAB) adopted Databricks Serverless across notebooks, jobs, declarative pipelines, SQL Warehouses and Model Serving—delivering platform reliability, cost efficiency and performance without compromising security or governance. Hear NAB’s blueprint: phased migration, workload prioritization and cross‑team operationalization. Learn the essentials—Unity Catalog for fine‑grained governance, plus Private Link and Secure Egress Gateway for private connectivity—and hard‑won lessons from uplifting Spark to declarative pipelines (DLT/LDP), moving SQL to serverless warehouses, and operationalizing model serving with observability and guardrails. Walk away with actionable patterns, checklists and success criteria for regulated environments. Outcomes include broad serverless adoption, faster MLOps cycles, better SQL performance, lower ingestion cost and sustained query scale—a pragmatic path to bank‑grade serverless at enterprise scale.

title: Serverless Compute at Petabyte Scale: Latest Launches, Roadmap, and Deloitte's Migration Story
abstract: Serverless Compute for Notebooks, Jobs, and Pipelines has reached a turning point. What started as a convenience for ad hoc workloads now runs petabyte-scale production and mission-critical SLAs at some of the largest Databricks customers. This session covers the most recent launches across runtime, performance, and cost for Notebooks, Jobs, and Pipelines, as well as upcoming. Then we share how Deloitte moved its global audit data platform, serving 60,000+ auditors with 20,000+ daily jobs across three geos, from classic compute to serverless: the migration path, the architecture changes, and the results. If you have been waiting for serverless to be ready for your hardest and largest workloads, this is the session to recalibrate.

title: SharePoint to Lakehouse with Lakeflow Connect — Top 5 Powerful GenAI Patterns
abstract: Many organizations have rich SharePoint data but struggle to use it at scale for intelligence, reporting, and automation. In this demo-heavy session, we demonstrate how to leverage valuable SharePoint content as a first-class data source for data intelligence and analytics by ingesting it into your lakehouse. Using the new Lakeflow Connect SharePoint connector, we will demonstrate incremental, governed pipelines (via Unity Catalog) that ingest both structured data (Excel, CSV, lists) and unstructured content (PDFs, Office files, images). Data lands as streaming tables enriched with SharePoint metadata to power downstream analytics, search, and AI. We will walk through five low-lift, high-impact patterns: driving an AI-powered BI dashboard from Excel and list data, summarizing and analyzing PDF reports, querying PowerPoint decks via natural language in a secure Genie Room, OCR’ing scanned images for text extraction, and consolidating many CSV reports into a single streaming table.

title: Ship Faster: Dev Workflows with Lakebase Branching
abstract: Developers branch their code constantly, but the database has always been the exception: shared, stateful, and a constant source of friction. Someone runs a migration in the dev environment and breaks everyone else's work. Test data gets polluted. Schema changes get deferred because coordinating them is painful. Lakebase branching fixes this by letting you spin up an isolated, zero-copy clone of your database in seconds, one per feature branch, one per pull request, one per developer if you want. In this lightning talk, you'll see how database branching slots into the workflows you already use: local development, CI pipelines, and staging environments, without the overhead of maintaining separate database instances. The result is a development workflow where the database finally moves at the same speed as the rest of your stack.

title: Spark DSV2: Growing Up Fast
abstract: Spark’s DataSource V2 integration has taken a major step forward, beginning with the addition of a procedure catalog and row identifier support to enable richer table management and row-level operations across modern data sources. Building on this foundation, recent updates improve MERGE INTO with safer schema evolution and enhance partition filtering for more efficient query planning and execution. DML summaries now provide clearer visibility into write behavior, while key cache fixes resolve long-standing correctness issues in Spark execution. DataSource V2 has also been extended with first-class SQL features such as table constraints, complex default values, and generated columns, laying the groundwork for more advanced table semantics. We’ll also look ahead to deeper Change Data Feed (CDF) integration in Spark to support robust incremental processing, highlighting what’s available today and what’s coming next as Spark continues to close the gap with traditional warehouse systems.

title: Sponsored by: Acceldata | Trust at the Speed of Agents: Reliable AI and Data on Databricks
abstract: As enterprises deploy AI agents across Databricks at unprecedented pace, trust at production speed requires a complete trust platform. This session covers how Acceldata integrates three layers — data observability, agentic data management, and Agent Observability — into a single operating model for reliable AI on Databricks. Each layer reinforces the next: observability without action is alerting, action without observability is guessing, and agents without governance is risk. From anomaly detection through autonomous remediation to agent trust, this approach points toward the self-governing lakehouse where data, agents, and policies stay in lockstep without humans in every decision.

With the convergence of SAP Business Data Cloud (BDC) and the AI/ML capabilities of SAP Databricks, finance organizations are re-architecting their close cycles - shifting from reactive reporting to proactive, insight driven decisioning. Accenture’s adoption of SAP Databricks as the AI and data science backbone for Financial Close operations represents a major leap forward. Working hand in hand with SAP & Databricks, the ecosystem has been engineered to support predictive insights, automated commentaries, real time monitoring, and fully integrated treasury operations. This transformation isn’t just technological - it delivers tangible, measurable business impact. This presentation highlights the KPIs and metrics that demonstrate how SAP Databricks reshapes the Financial Close process end-to-end.

title: Sponsored by: Actian | Scaling AI: Data Products and Contracts as the Foundation
abstract: Forget the models. Unstructured, unowned, uncontracted data is where AI goes to underdeliver. Most Gen AI initiatives deliver zero ROI, and Gartner expects 40% of agentic AI programs to be canceled by 2027. The analogy writes itself. Lufthansa Cargo doesn't ship freight without a manifest, a container, and a contract between shipper and carrier. Yet we routinely ship data to AI with none of that. Data products are the containers. Data contracts are the manifests. Open standards like ODCS and ODPS, part of the Linux Foundation's Bitol project, serve as a shared language that makes them readable across the supply chain. You've invested in a lakehouse. But even the best Delta Lake architecture breaks down when AI agents can't verify data quality, trace lineage, or resolve ownership when something goes wrong. Your infrastructure is solid. The contract layer above it is missing. And organizations that close that gap are 3.4x more likely to put AI into production. We'll show how Lufthansa Cargo's Data Cargo Platform puts that principle into practice, unifying 100+ real-time sources into a governed foundation for operational intelligence, powered by the Actian Data Intelligence Platform, and delivering measurable ROI at enterprise scale. Takeaways: Why data products and contracts are non-negotiable for AI-ready data How open standards like ODCS and ODPS de-risk AI without vendor lock-in A working blueprint from Lufthansa Cargo: many sources, one platform, measurable ROI
description_raw:
Forget the models. Unstructured, unowned, uncontracted data is where AI goes to underdeliver. Most Gen AI initiatives deliver zero ROI, and Gartner expects 40% of agentic AI programs to be canceled by 2027. 

The analogy writes itself. Lufthansa Cargo doesn't ship freight without a manifest, a container, and a contract between shipper and carrier. Yet we routinely ship data to AI with none of that. Data products are the containers. Data contracts are the manifests. Open standards like ODCS and ODPS, part of the Linux Foundation's Bitol project, serve as a shared language that makes them readable across the supply chain.

You've invested in a lakehouse. But even the best Delta Lake architecture breaks down when AI agents can't verify data quality, trace lineage, or resolve ownership when something goes wrong. Your infrastructure is solid. The contract layer above it is missing. And organizations that close that gap are 3.4x more likely to put AI into production. We'll show how Lufthansa Cargo's Data Cargo Platform puts that principle into practice, unifying 100+ real-time sources into a governed foundation for operational intelligence, powered by the Actian Data Intelligence Platform, and delivering measurable ROI at enterprise scale.

Takeaways:

  • Why data products and contracts are non-negotiable for AI-ready data
  • How open standards like ODCS and ODPS de-risk AI without vendor lock-in
  • A working blueprint from Lufthansa Cargo: many sources, one platform, measurable ROI

speakers.name: Jean-Georges Perrin
speakers.bio: Jean-Georges Perrin (“JGP”) is a Senior Product Manager at Actian, leading initiatives in Data Products and Data Contracts. With 25 years of experience in data architecture—including a tenure as Principal Architect at Expedia—he now chairs the Linux Foundation’s Bitol project, driving the Open Data Contract Standard (ODCS). The author of Implementing Data Mesh and Spark in Action, JGP is a recognized thought leader, Lifetime IBM Champion, and Data Mesh MVP dedicated to balancing data governance with innovation.

title: Sponsored by: Alteryx | The Foundation Comes First: Building a Tax Data Strategy That Scales with AI
abstract: AI, agents, predictive modeling and the next wave of tax innovation depend on something deceptively simple: the right data, in the right place, ready to use. In this session, Cheria Coram, Director, Tax Technology and Data Enablement at Starbucks, shares her vision for evolving tax data strategy from reactive data wrangling to intentional foundation building. Drawing on her experience leading data and automation for a global tax function, she'll cover how Alteryx unlocked efficiency in data transformation and why the next critical unlock is centralizing, governing and designing tax-processed data for reuse across the tax lifecycle. She'll also share where the team is headed next, using Alteryx with Databricks to build a scalable foundation that enables tax-ready modeling today and positions the team to layer on analytics, AI and whatever comes next.

title: Sponsored by: AMD | Run Databricks More Efficiently on AMD CPUs Lessons from AMD’s GPU Telemetry Team
abstract: As Databricks workloads scale, the efficiency of the underlying CPU platform directly impacts performance, cost, and infrastructure utilization. In this session, we introduce AMD’s latest CPU platform, Turin, and show how it compares to prior generations in both performance and efficiency across analytics workloads. AMD engineers will then demonstrate how their internal GPU telemetry team runs large‑scale analytics workloads on Databricks—and why those workloads perform more efficiently on AMD CPUs. Using a production telemetry pipeline processing minute‑level signals across thousands of nodes, we highlight measurable gains in throughput, efficiency, and reduced infrastructure requirements for the same job. Attendees will learn how to replicate these results and explore a new AMD–Databricks pilot program to validate performance improvements through guided proof‑of‑concepts.

title: Sponsored by: Artefact | The Workforce You Won't Recognise: Building the Hybrid Organization with AI Agents
abstract: Most AI strategies are stuck at the POC stage, not because the technology isn’t ready, but because the data foundation isn’t. In this session, we explore what high-performing organizations are actually building: hybrid workforces where AI agents and humans coordinate through a shared, governed data layer. We’ll show how leading organizations are structuring hybrid teams, why most agent deployments fail to reach production and what it looks like when agents truly work alongside humans, not as assistants, but as part of the workforce, driving faster decisions, execution and outcomes. We'll also hear directly from the field. Joining us is the CTO of Danone, who will share how one of the world's leading consumer goods companies is thinking about this shift. Join us to see a live multi-agent system in action and learn a practical blueprint for moving from isolated AI experiments to a production-grade hybrid workforce.

title: Sponsored By: Astronomer | Unifying Data and AI Orchestration with Apache Airflow
abstract: In a high-pressure kitchen, great service depends on mise en place — everything prepared, organized, and ready before the rush. Production AI demands the same discipline. This talk shows how Apache Airflow unifies data pipelines and AI workflows in one observable control plane and system of record — replacing fragmented observability, failure handling, and team handoffs. We'll walk through real projects covering multi-agent orchestration, AI-driven pipeline branching, and vision model integration — each illustrating a distinct production pattern and all running on Airflow. The best kitchens don't just execute recipes — they make the rush look effortless.

title: Sponsored by: Astronomer | Your AI Strategy Has a Context Problem. Orchestration Solves It.
abstract: Every enterprise has an AI strategy. Few have the foundation to deliver on it. Most treat context as something defined upfront and consumed downstream. Semantic layers define metrics. Ontologies model relationships. Neither captures what actually ran. Enterprise context is not static. It is evidence that accumulates continuously: which pipelines ran, what changed upstream, what humans corrected. Orchestration is the only layer where that evidence accumulates naturally, not as declared truth, but as a continuous record of what actually happened. That is what production AI runs on. This talk outlines the architectural pattern that makes it possible.

speakers.name: Vikram Koka
speakers.bio: Vikram Koka is Chief Strategy Officer at Astronomer and a member of the Apache Airflow PMC, with a deep passion for data engineering and open-source orchestration. He has been a key contributor to Airflow since 2019, helping lead its evolution from a data orchestration platform into ML and now AI workloads, a journey reflected in both his architectural contributions and the platform's growing community of data, ML, and AI engineers. His design contributions span Airflow's entire modern history: Scheduler High Availability in Airflow 2.0, Data-Driven Scheduling, Dynamic Tasks, Setup/Teardown, and the program management of Airflow 3, the largest release in Airflow's history. He is currently leading Airflow's evolution into AI-native orchestration, introducing Human-in-the-Loop capabilities that allow AI pipelines to incorporate human judgment natively and enabling Airflow's vast connector ecosystem to be leveraged by Agentic workloads. Vikram's open-source roots trace back to his early work on the GNU Debugger (GDB), where he co-developed its remote debugging capabilities. With patents in distributed computing and cryptography, he brings a strong technical foundation alongside extensive experience leading globally distributed engineering and cross-functional teams spanning R&D, UX, product, services, and business development.

title: Sponsored By: Atlan | Mastercard's "Context by Design": Engineering AI-Ready Data Products at Scale
abstract: At Mastercard, trust has always been the product. For six years, that trust has been engineered in layers: privacy by design, then data by design, and now context by design — each evolution built on the last. Now, as AI agents begin transacting at the speed of commerce, the latest layer matters most — an Enterprise Context Layer, built on Databricks, that machines can read, reason over, and act on without human intervention at every step. Join Fabien Thiaucourt and Vivek Radhakrishnan of Mastercard, and Austin Kronz of Atlan, to learn how engineering and enablement co-own context as a dual mission — and why the productive tension between them is the reason governance actually sticks — how automated metadata and human-centered product thinking combine to build AI-ready data products on Databricks, and how this foundation sets the stage for text-to-SQL and conversational search — and every AI use case that follows.

title: Sponsored by: Atlan | The Enterprise Context Layer: Why Agents Fail — and the Fix — Demystified and Demoed
abstract: Everyone's talking about context layers. Nobody agrees on what one is — a semantic layer with a better name? A knowledge graph in a trench coat? AI is moving from pilot to production — and it made data teams into janitors: cleaning up hallucinations, debugging agents. But the context agents need most is what data teams already own. The definitions, the lineage, the institutional knowledge. That's not a cost center. It's your most strategic AI asset. You already have Databricks — maybe Unity Catalog too. But your agents still don't know which "revenue" definition to use, which tables to trust, or what the business actually means. The gap between pilot and production isn't a model problem. It's a context problem. Join Prukalpa Sankar and Varun Banka to see it live: dark Databricks tables become AI-ready — automated lineage mapped, AI-bootstrapped definitions added, Context Quality Score green — and a Genie query returns a governed response via MCP. All live. All on stage.

title: Sponsored by: AWS | Breaking Data Silos with Multi-Engine Catalog Federation
abstract: Mastercard moved beyond the "Multi-Catalog" struggle and successfully federated Databricks Unity Catalog to AWS Glue. This allows Apache Spark engines to consume data in Apache Iceberg tables that register in Databricks Unity Catalog and sync seamlessly across AWS services like Amazon EMR, enabling ACID reliability and multi-engine interoperability without vendor lock-in. Mastercard achieved a Single Source of Truth for governance allowing engineers to use the best engine for the job without metadata fragmentation. Mastercard achieved seamless catalog federation, allowing domain teams to choose optimal compute engines. This open-format strategy created a sustainable, future-proof architecture supporting machine learning, streaming, and governed data sharing across the enterprise.

title: Sponsored by: Capgemini | The Foundations for a Million Agents
abstract: Every organization can build an agent — almost nobody is ready to manage a million of them. This session lays out what it actually takes, starting with AI Persona definition: how the business delegates to an agent as a team member, not a system. It then breaks apart four disciplines that must scale independently. Integration & Ecosystem spans MCP, Unity Catalog, and the governance of AI through MLflow, grounding agents in trusted data and policy. Development and Discovery use Genie and Databricks Marketplace to build and evolve agents. Business Management, through Mosaic AI and MLflow, drives accountability. AI Resource Management makes IT the HR function for the AI workforce. Underpinning it all is why a streaming Delta Lake architecture is central to an AI future. This is the architecture for a million agents.

abstract: Despite high AI adoption, few enterprises see meaningful impact because traditional governance and security methods slow innovation. title: Sponsored By: Datadog | 4,500 Jobs, No Blind Spots: AccuWeather's Serverless Databricks Migration with Datadog
abstract: AccuWeather delivers forecasts to 1.5 billion people daily. When their pipelines fail, severe weather warnings don't reach the people who need them. The team used to wait 90 minutes before responding to any alert — not because fixes were hard, but because monitoring that fires on every transient failure trains teams to ignore everything. This session shows how AccuWeather migrated to Serverless Databricks Workflows and operated approximately 4,500 weekly Lakeflow jobs with Datadog Data Observability. We’ll cover how AccuWeather using serverless cut compute costs in half, and the pre-flight pattern that catches failures before expensive cluster jobs run. Additionally, Datadog turns Databricks system table data into alerts built around weather-specific logic, leading to over 50% fewer unactionable alerts and 80% faster incident response — this is due to firing incidents only after five failures in a 45-minute window, and only when multiple forecast models fail in the same critical hour.

title: Sponsored by: Datadog | Experimentation and Product Analytics in the Agentic World: Bringing User Signals to Every Release
abstract: When developing software with autonomous agents, the bottleneck shifts from writing code to evaluating it. Agents can generate changes continuously. What limits progress is how quickly you can tell whether those changes are acceptable. Agentic development looks less like traditional software engineering and more like reinforcement learning: a loop of build, release, evaluate, where the fastest signals dominate. If your unit tests return in seconds and your conversion data takes two weeks, guess which one shapes the product. Teams need fast proxies for signals that arrive too slowly to influence an agent's build loop, and governance is needed to reason about signal quality, noise and coverage. This session introduces an evaluation infrastructure that orchestrates synthetic tests, production telemetry, analytics and controlled releases to gate autonomous changes. Datadog is building toward this layer, but the framework applies to any team rethinking infrastructure for an agentic world.

In this session, Evri's Chief Data Officer, Harvinder Atwal, and Datafold CEO, Gleb Mezhanskiy, share how Evri migrated and modernized all data processing on Databricks, leveraging Datafold's AI Migration Agent and Knowledge Graph for value-level validation across thousands of datasets. Both legacy platforms were decommissioned on time, in under a year, with zero disruption to operations.

title: Sponsored By: DataHub | Agents That Get it Right: How FIS Grounds Databricks Genie in Enterprise Context
abstract: FIS processes 75 billion transactions a year for 20,000+ clients. They're building a client-facing analytics product that lets financial institutions ask plain-English questions about their customers' data, a business capability that simply didn't exist before. The bottleneck wasn't the AI model. It was the context. Fragmented across spreadsheets, Unity Catalog, and Snowflake, context was nearly impossible to iterate on. Every Genie model change meant tearing down the space, restaging it, and resyncing from scratch. The fix: centralize all business context in DataHub, let Unity handle the technical layer, sync bidirectionally. Because DataHub context is editable and syncable in one place, the team could iterate fast, tuning Genie models without rebuilding every time. With DataHub as the context layer, Genie knows which tables to trust, which metrics are current, and how the organization actually uses its data. Agents stop guessing. Answers become ones analysts can stand behind. In this talk, Frank Showalter, VP of Data Engineering and Governance at FIS, walks through the architecture and what it took to go from metadata chaos to demoing a net-new analytics product to clients, one that doesn't replace existing analyst workflows but opens an entirely new line of business.

We’ll show how structured, tested, and semantically-rich data flows from dbt into Unity Catalog, and from Unity Catalog into any AI application running on Databricks. We'll deploy a live-managed app on Databricks that pulls governed assets directly from Unity Catalog with lineage, contracts, and semantic definitions built end-to-end in dbt. The result is an architectural blueprint where your AI apps aren't guessing at the data beneath them — with dbt, they have the required context to be governed, reliable, and right. You’ll leave with a Well-Architected reference pattern for AI apps on Databricks, and a clear picture of how dbt and Unity Catalog become the governed data infrastructure every AI use case depends on.

title: Sponsored by: dbt Labs | Your BI Copilot Is Blind - Crafting an Agent That Goes Beyond the Dashboard
abstract: BI copilots can answer questions about what's on screen: filters, dimensions, chart values. But ask "why is this number wrong?" or "where does this column come from?" and they hit a wall. They can't see past the dashboard. Integral Ad Science built an AI agent that goes deeper. Directly within the BI layer, it connects to your dbt project through MCP and validates findings in Databricks SQL (Unity Catalog) via the Databricks SQL MCP server. The agent extracts context from the report, reads compiled SQL, traces column-level lineage from mart to source, explains the business logic in each transformation, and confirms what the data shows in the warehouse. For analysts, it eliminates hours spent following DAGs and reading model code. For business users, a persona switch delivers clear, natural language answers. Mars Dauer will show how MCP makes this possible across dbt and Databricks and share an end-to-end investigation, from BI report to root cause to Jira ticket, all in one chat.

Mars Dauer will show how MCP makes this possible across dbt and Databricks and share an end-to-end investigation, from BI report to root cause to Jira ticket, all in one chat.

title: Sponsored By: definity | From Observability to Agentic Data Engineering: What It Actually Takes
abstract: Data observability is now standard in lakehouse platforms, but it stops at reactive monitoring. As teams push toward proactive agentic workflows, LLMs alone aren’t enough. Without production-aware context, ability to take action in-flight, and automated guardrails, AI remains limited to suggestive copilots trained on generic data. title: Sponsored by: Deloitte | Generating Realistic, High-Fidelity Synthetic Financial Data on Databricks
abstract: Access to customer financial data is often slowed by privacy regulations, hindering innovation in risk management and personalization. Deloitte’s dual-model solution on the Databricks Platform generates high-fidelity synthetic data to overcome this challenge. It combines generative adversarial networks for structured data (demographics, creditworthiness) and LLMs for behavioral insights (price sensitivity), complete with an AI-automated quality review. This provides a safe foundation for developing models, testing risk algorithms and simulating market strategies. This session demonstrates how this approach accelerates financial innovation while reducing compliance risk by replicating customer data utility without exposing sensitive information.

title: Sponsored by: Domo | Eliminating the Warehouse “Tail Problem”: AI-Powered Optimization on Databricks + Domo
abstract: Warehouse operations don’t fail at the start of the day—they fail at the end. As real-world conditions diverge from static planning assumptions, bottlenecks emerge across palletizer lanes, creating a costly “tail problem” that requires constant manual intervention. This session explores how one logistics operator reimagined warehouse automation by combining Databricks and Domo to create a self-adaptive system. As palletizers fall behind, go offline, or deviate from expected performance, the platform continuously analyzes live data from Databricks and recommends exactly what actions to take—what to move, where to move it, and why. Through an interactive Domo application, supervisors can execute AI-driven recommendations, simulate changes, and respond instantly to disruptions with automated evacuation workflows. The result: a self-aware, adaptive system that replaces reactive firefighting with proactive optimization—improving efficiency, reducing downtime, and delivering measurable ROI.

We explore how combining Databricks serverless SQL warehouses with Domo Cloud Amplifier unlocks unprecedented speed on billion-row datasets — cutting cycles from 20+ hours to just 1–2. But speed is only half the story — with Domo Publish, you can deploy curated, governed content to dedicated child Domo instances, giving your customers their own fully interactive analytics environment to explore, update, and build on. Paired with Domo Everywhere, you can scale governed, read/write data products across your entire customer base — all managed from a single parent instance. Finally, we'll showcase how Domo AI and MCP accelerate MVP development, turning complex data into high-impact insights faster than ever. If you're looking to operationalize analytics, deliver data products your customers truly own, and respond to change at speed, this session is your blueprint.

title: Sponsored by: Domo | From Prediction to Action: Agentic AI for Ambulatory Care on Databricks
abstract: Healthcare organizations don’t suffer from a lack of data—they suffer from a lack of timely action. No-shows, late arrivals, and provider delays create millions in lost revenue and poor patient experiences, yet most systems stop at reporting the problem. In this session, we demonstrate how Databricks powers real-time predictive intelligence, while Domo operationalizes it through agentic AI workflows that take action. Using live appointment, patient, weather, and traffic data, AI agents continuously evaluate no-show risk and dynamically decide the next best action—triggering SMS outreach, recommending overbooking strategies, and alerting staff before disruptions occur. Attendees will see how this closed-loop system transforms static analytics into autonomous decisioning, with full governance, auditability, and human-in-the-loop validation. The result is a proactive care model that reduces no-shows, stabilizes clinic throughput, and delivers measurable ROI within weeks—not months.

title: Sponsored by: F5 | Who’s Controlling Your Agents?
abstract: You’ve built and deployed your agents, but once they’re live, how do you ensure they stay within bounds? Agents don’t fail loudly. Poisoned vector data, prompt injection, or dangerous tool calls aren’t flagged, they’re executed. That can lead to data leakage, unauthorized actions, and silent drift outside intended boundaries. In this session, F5 shows how to enforce runtime guardrails that give full visibility into agent behavior, tool usage, and decision paths, so teams can secure agents without breaking workflows. Key Takeaways Enforce boundaries on agent behavior, tool use, and data access at runtime Gain visibility into agent actions across multi-step workflows Use red teaming to uncover vulnerabilities before production and auto remediate

title: Sponsored by: Fireworks AI | Own Your AI: Beat Frontier Models With Your Own Data — Presented by Fireworks AI
abstract: The best AI companies aren't renting intelligence from closed model APIs — they're building their own. In this session, Roberto from Fireworks AI busts three common myths about training open models: that closed models are always better, that training is hard and that you need massive labeled datasets. Drawing on real production examples from real-world examples from clients, he'll show how supervised training, direct preference optimization and reinforcement training turn your production data into a compounding moat — and why the best model for your product is the one you own.

abstract: As Superhuman expanded its AI platform across Grammarly, Coda, Superhuman Mail and Superhuman Go, more of the business began to rely on timely data from Salesforce, Outreach, Pardot, Stripe, Zendesk, Qualtrics and other third-party systems. The challenge went far beyond moving data into Databricks. Go-to-market, finance and customer teams needed faster, reliable access to trusted data without turning every new data request into weeks of custom engineering. In this session, Superhuman shares how it standardized third-party ingestion on Fivetran, built a self-serve operating model in Databricks and used Connector SDK plus AI-assisted development to cut specialized connector work from months to days. The result: faster reporting and alerting for a $300M ad program, support for internal AI-ready workflows and a broader data foundation that contributed to a 10% lift in LTV.

title: Sponsored by: Glean | From Analytics to Action: Powering Databricks Insights with Full Enterprise Context
abstract: Great AI answers need more than governed data alone. They need enterprise context — the people, documents, conversations and workflows that turn an insight into action. In this session, we’ll show how Glean and Databricks bring those pieces together in one natural-language experience. With Glean connected to Databricks through AI/BI Genie, employees can ask business questions in plain English and get answers grounded in Databricks governance and permissions, enriched with the broader company context around it. The result is a faster path from analytics to decisions, with trusted insights that are more accessible, more actionable and more useful across the business. In this session, we’ll demonstrate how this unified experience works by showing how sample questions are routed from Glean to Databricks Genie, returning answers with a clear path back to the underlying data — so organizations can make data-driven decisions more accessible, trustworthy and actionable across the business.

title: Sponsored by: Hightouch | How XP Drove a 72% Lift in Account Opens and 35% Activation Increase with Agentic CRM
abstract: XP is one of the largest financial institutions in Brazil, and they didn't get there by treating onboarding as a generic funnel. After proving the value of their first-party data in Databricks, XP teamed up with Hightouch to tackle a stubborn problem: millions of sign-ups that never became active accounts in traditional CRM campaigns. In this session, XP will show how they implemented Agentic CRM by turning their Databricks lakehouse into an AI decisioning engine that continuously tests offers, channels and timing on governed first-party data, then activates those decisions in real time across XP's marketing stack via Hightouch. By putting AI decisioning at the center of onboarding, XP drove a 72% lift in account open rates and a 35% increase in activation conversion in their first few weeks — while maintaining full control of experimentation, governance and monitoring. You'll leave with a blueprint covering data pipelines, decision policies, measurement and cross-functional buy-in.

title: Sponsored by: Imply | From Splunk to Databricks: Unlocking Open, Scalable Observability in the Lakehouse
abstract: Databricks offers a lakehouse-native model for security and observability built on open formats and an open ecosystem. It enables teams to ingest, retain, and analyze large volumes of telemetry data while reducing cost and eliminating vendor lock-in. But for organizations running Splunk today, realizing this promise requires more than simply moving data.In this session, we show how teams transition from Splunk to Databricks by moving data into open lakehouse tables and querying it directly. Instead of pre-indexing everything or moving data between systems, queries run in place across large historical datasets while maintaining performance. Teams can adopt the lakehouse without changing dashboards or workflows. We cover how to make lakehouse data interactive, reduce infrastructure overhead, and make machine data fast and accessible for real-world observability use cases.

title: Sponsored by: Insight| Beyond the Sandbox: Using Lakebase Instant Branching for High-Stakes AI Agent Deployment
abstract: As AI agents evolve from chat-based assistants into autonomous systems, the cost of data errors and unintended actions grows. How do you let an agent update pricing or modify records without exposing production systems safely? Enter Lakebase. In this session, we demonstrate a safety‑first architecture using Lakebase’s serverless Postgres and Instant Branching capabilities. You’ll see a live demo of an Autonomous Pricing Agent responding to real-time market signals. Instead of writing directly to production, the agent triggers an Instant Branch — a zero‑copy, isolated clone of the operational database created in seconds. Here, we run automated pre‑flight validations, business rules, and AI/BI impact analysis before selectively merging approved changes back to the primary database. Attendees will learn how to implement Git‑for‑Data style workflows, manage agent state and memory using pgvector, and continuously sync changes using Lakehouse Sync for auditability and downstream analytics.

abstract: Databricks SQL has transformed how teams interact with their data, delivering fast query performance, seamless scalability and lakehouse architecture that brings together the best of data warehousing and data engineering. It’s an incredibly powerful platform, but getting the most out of it requires constant attention to cost and performance. Warehouse workloads are dynamic. Query demands shift around the clock, teams grow and what was perfectly tuned last week may be wasteful or underperforming today. Maximizing efficiency on Databricks SQL is not a one-time task. It’s an ongoing challenge. That’s where Keebo comes in. In this session, we’ll show how Keebo uses reinforcement learning to learn your unique workload patterns and continuously optimize your Databricks SQL warehouses in real time, maximizing performance while reducing costs. No manual tuning. No trade-offs. Just a warehouse that gets smarter over time.

title: Sponsored by: KPMG | Building a Governed Synthetic Data Lakehouse for AI Agents
abstract: Synthetic data + AI agents is very hot for Databricks right now. The objective of the talk is to propose exploring the idea of synthetic Lakehouse designed specifically for AI agents rather than traditional approach to data collection. The motivation is that teams want to build and evaluate agents over conversations, documents, tickets, and knowledge bases, but real enterprise data is often sensitive or regulated, which blocks experimentation and validation. We will show how synthetic data can be used as a safe, realistic test to develop and evaluate production grade AI agents. We will explore how to design agent-ready synthetic data and why a synthetic Lakehouse is a practical foundation for testing agents even before touching real data.

title: Sponsored by: LakeFusion | When MDM Meets Ontology: A New Architecture for Enterprise Data Intelligence
abstract: Every enterprise has data. But most struggle to extract true meaning. We've spent decades building separate systems for analytics and operations, separate tools for data quality and governance, separate platforms for master data and transactional data. The result: fragmented records, conflicting hierarchies and business processes that can't trust the data they depend on. This talk introduces the concept of an operational ontology: a data architecture that doesn't just describe what your data should look like, but enforces it at scale, in real time, inside the lakehouse. Drawing from production deployments that consolidated 100M+ records across dozens of source systems in weeks (not months), we'll show how LakeFusion’s lakehouse-native entity resolution, streaming data quality, and AI-powered stewardship combine to build something traditional MDM and top-down knowledge graphs never could: a living, governed, operational model of your business that AI agents can actually act on.

title: Sponsored by: Lovelytics | Automating High-Stakes Finance Workflows with AI Agents
abstract: Finance back office teams spend significant time on manual, document-heavy workflows like remittance reconciliation and proof of delivery validation. We present how we deployed two production-grade automation use cases for Lippert, saving 250+ hours monthly with over 90% model accuracy. We first cover remittance reconciliation from lockbox PDFs spanning hundreds of pages. The solution uses a deterministic extraction pipeline that segments documents, normalizes headers, cleans OCR noise, validates line items and applies customer enrichment to produce finance-ready tables and exception-focused audit trails. Next, we detail proof of delivery automation, where standard OCR struggles with crossed-out quantities and signatures. This use case combines computer vision and LLMs using Azure Document Intelligence and OpenCV smart cropping with a safety-first validation layer. We share design tradeoffs, failure modes and lessons learned from deploying finance agents in production.

abstract: At 7-Eleven, operational resilience at scale depends on how quickly data can be converted into action. With thousands of stores generating structured sensor telemetry, equipment failures can directly impact revenue, yet traditional development approaches were too slow to scale predictive maintenance solutions efficiently. This session explores how 7-Eleven accelerated ML delivery using Databricks and an agentic AI–driven workflow. Built on Delta tables and a medallion architecture, the solution enabled scalable ingestion, governed access, and ML-based failure detection. Using Windsurf, GitLab, and Databricks Asset Bundles, the team significantly accelerated code generation, integration, and deployment. The end-to-end solution was delivered in under two weeks versus an estimated six weeks, reducing development effort, accelerating time-to-market, and helping protect millions in revenue.

title: Sponsored By: MinIO | How a Fortune 500 Manufacturer Runs Databricks AI on 250 TB of On-Premises Data
abstract: A Fortune 500 semiconductor manufacturer generates hundreds of terabytes of production data across facilities in two international regions. That data must stay on-premises for regulatory compliance, latency sensitivity, and economics of scale — but the data science team depends on Databricks for the AI modeling that drives yield improvement and quality assurance. Rather than replicating data to the cloud or building custom ETL pipelines, they deployed MinIO AIStor with native Delta Sharing embedded at the storage layer. Databricks queries live Delta and Iceberg tables on-premises through Unity Catalog with zero data movement — no copies, no pipelines, no additional infrastructure. In this session, hear how the solution was architected, what decisions were made and why, and what the team learned operating it in production. Includes perspectives from MinIO and Databricks, a technical walkthrough, and a live demo of AIStor Table Sharing connected to a Databricks workspace.

title: Sponsored By: Monte Carlo | Building the Foundation for Trusted AI in Regulated Industries
abstract: The enterprises with the most to gain from AI are often the slowest to deploy it, and in regulated industries, that caution is rational — the risk is real. Data quality failures don't just break pipelines in financial services — they break compliance, erode model trust, and end careers. The bar for "production-ready" AI is fundamentally different when your data touches trades, audits, or PII. In this session, Barr Moses, CEO of Monte Carlo, joins Lenny Rosenfeld, VP of Data Science & Software Engineering at Nasdaq, for a conversation on what it takes to get trusted AI into production in financial services. They'll cover AI observability, data lineage, and governance frameworks built for regulators — sharing the failures they've seen, the patterns that work, and what they'd do differently.

title: Sponsored by: Monte Carlo | Why Your Agents Keep Failing (And What to Do About It)
abstract: Every company is shipping AI agents right now. Most of them are failing, and nobody knows until a customer or an exec calls it out. The problem isn't the models. It's that teams are building agents on top of data they don't monitor, running them without observability and trusting outputs no one has tested. In this session, I'll walk through the three places agents actually break in production: the data going in, the agent's own behavior and what comes out the other side. I'll share a framework for catching these failures before your users do. The goal is simple: stop shipping pilots that quietly die, and start shipping agents that hold up when it matters.
