title: Sponsored by: Nagarro | The Agentic Enterprise: What has to be True Before AI can Act Autonomously
abstract: Most companies have shipped AI by now: copilots, dashboards, recommendation engines. The models work, the data platforms exist, yet AI still usually sits behind a human. It advises, but rarely acts. That gap comes down to orchestration, governance and organization design. This session will explore what must be in place before AI can run autonomously, and what changes when it does. We’ll walk through enterprise scenarios where agentic AI runs on a Databricks backbone, and the architecture and governance choices that made it possible. We’ll also cover where human oversight still belongs and it's importance. Highlights: Why AI programs get stuck between "working demo" and "running in production," and what closes that gap Walkthrough of agentic workflows on Databricks including decision movement between AI and people Nagarro's Fluidic Intelligence framework for treating AI as a continuous system What leadership teams need to start doing as well as stop doing

title: Sponsored by: Neo4j | Teaching Genie to See Connections: Graph Intelligence for the Databricks Lakehouse
abstract: Databricks Genie gives analysts a natural language way to ask questions of governed Lakehouse data. But some of the highest-value questions are relationship questions: which accounts are connected to suspicious activity, which merchants sit inside unusual communities, and which patterns only appear two or three hops away? In this 20-minute lightning talk, Neo4j shows a graph pattern for enriching Delta Lake data with graph-derived context that Genie can query like ordinary dimensions. Using a financial crime investigation, we'll show how connected scores and communities can turn flat results into explainable, relationship-aware answers without changing the analyst workflow.

abstract: Enterprises often struggle with slow, manual data migrations & fragmented data quality processes, limiting their ability to adopt AI at scale. This session introduces our approach to data modernization driven by our framework of ‘NeuFlow,’ an autonomous, no-code data engineering approach designed to accelerate data journeys and deliver AI-ready data. Our approach towards AI driven Data modernization unifies intelligent migration (DataBridge), automated data quality (TrustFlow) and reconciliation (MatchFlow) into a single AI-powered framework represented by Neuflow. Attendees will learn how organizations can reduce migration timelines by up to 25%, automate nearly 50% of data quality operations, and achieve 20–30% lower operational costs, while improving trust, governance, and readiness for AI-driven use cases.

title: Sponsored by: Nimble Gravity | When Agents Should Ask for Help: Designing Human Escalation in Agent Bricks
abstract: Autonomous agents can handle a lot, until they can't. The real challenge isn't building an agent that runs, it's building one that knows when to stop and who to ask. In this session, we walk through a practical pattern for connecting AI agents to the humans they work alongside, without pulling those people out of their day. Using Agent Bricks, Databricks-native AI functions, and MLflow evaluation, we show how an agent can assess its outputs, escalate to colleagues when needed (via Teams or Slack), and continue autonomously once it has what it needs. Through a live demo, you'll see the full cycle: an agent processes and reasons over documents, evaluates its own work, routes targeted questions to people, handles partial and non-responses gracefully, and logs timing and feedback for future improvement. You'll leave with a reusable pattern for building agents that augment human decision-making and a clear picture of how Databricks makes the oversight layer part of the platform.

Projects that demanded months of specialized engineering now ship in days. Less code. Less dependency on specialized talent. More governed, AI-ready data at enterprise scale. Leaders will leave with a clear understanding of how AI-assisted development compresses time-to-insight, reduces engineering overhead and enables data platforms to scale without scaling headcount.

title: Sponsored by: Onehouse | From JVM Gymnastics to Vectorized Performance in One K8s Operator Deploy
abstract: You open the Apache Spark™ UI and watch your executors doing full JVM gymnastics. Heap/off-heap flips, Tungsten memory juggling, GC pauses and shuffle spills everywhere. Dynamic allocation struggles, podTemplate nightmares and memoryOverhead prayers are the daily norm. In this 20-minute lightning talk I’ll show you how to drop a new Kubernetes Operator into your Spark-on-K8s cluster and instantly unlock a high-performance vectorized native execution engine. Zero code changes, no new APIs, no rewrites. You’ll see exactly how the operator reconciles every SparkApplication CR and SparkExecutorPod, replacing the JVM gymnastics with true native performance. Plus real production results: 3x+ faster workloads and 40-60% lower cloud spend. Leave with a clear, actionable playbook to upgrade Spark on Kubernetes in one operator deploy.

In this live demo, we will show how OpenAI Codex and Databricks help builders move from business context to a usable artifact: reasoning through the task, generating the first build, connecting the right data, and iterating toward something a team can inspect and improve. The session will show a practical path where a developer can use Codex to write code that connects to Databricks Lakebase and deploy it securely in Databricks Apps. This allows developers to quickly build, iterate, and deploy applications quickly from trusted Databricks data, with Codex helping accelerate the build process at every step.

abstract: What does it take to move from AI potential to AI systems the business can actually use? Databricks provides the trusted data, governance, evaluation, and deployment foundation. OpenAI brings the reasoning, coding, and the ability to do knowledge work with GPT 5.5, ChatGPT, and Codex. Attendees will leave with a practical pattern for how they can use frontier models and agents from OpenAI to empower every user in their organization to do real work while leveraging the data and governance controls within Databricks.

title: Sponsored by: Open AI | Turn Data Signals Into Intelligent Action With OpenAI and Databricks
abstract: A signal in the data is only valuable if a team can act on it. In this live demo, we will show how GPT-5.5 and Databricks can turn governed enterprise data into clear actions: identify what changed, reason through why it matters, and prepare a reviewable action autonomously that a person can approve, edit, or send. That action might be a Slack update, a brief, a plan, or a draft for the team that needs to respond. The session makes the shift from insight to automated actions, showing how AI can help teams respond to the business, not just analyze it.

title: Sponsored by: Perficient | From Second Gear to Full Throttle: Unlocking Trapped Value in Your Databricks Investment
abstract: Most Databricks customers are driving a race car in second gear—access to 12+ products while actively using only 2-3. The problem isn't adoption; it's activation. This session reveals how one organization transformed from standard data engineering to full platform activation, lighting up a dozen products without platform migration. Through two parallel workstreams, we'll explore the journey from foundational data engineering to production-ready agentic AI. The first workstream demonstrates real-time Customer 360 integration, moving from batch reports to sub-100ms queryable APIs. The second showcases autonomous AI agents performing production work humans cannot do at scale—all governed by the same Unity Catalog managing traditional data assets. You'll learn the utilization gap framework, pattern-based approaches that replaced 20-30 weeks of bespoke engineering, and proof that the path from data engineering to agentic AI doesn't require buying more—it requires using what you own.

title: Sponsored by: Pogo | You're Overthinking It: What Analyzing $500B in Consumer Spend Taught Us About Building AI Agents
abstract: At Pogo, we built AI research agents to help brands analyze hundreds of billions in consumer spending data. Our biggest lesson: the breakthrough came after we threw most of it away. We started with a complex system of specialized agents. It was fragile, unreliable, and impossible to iterate on. When we simplified to a single agent, everything changed. In this session, we’ll share why simpler agent architectures dramatically outperform complex ones, what the frontier AI labs’ own designs reveal about where the industry is heading, and how this approach powers Pogo’s AI research agent — where brands analyze purchase data from 3M Americans and interview thousands of verified buyers through an AI video interviewer, with results in hours.

title: Sponsored by: Polestar Analytics | Real-Time Working Capital on Databricks: From Siloed P2P, O2C & Inventory to Cash Flow Action
abstract: Over $1.8 trillion remains trapped in working capital globally — not due to a lack of data, but because that data is fragmented, delayed and disconnected from decision-making. Most finance teams operate across siloed P2P, O2C and inventory systems — each capturing only part of the picture. The gaps between them are where visibility is lost and cash leakage begins. This session is about closing that gap on the Databricks platform. We'll walk through how: To unify P2P, O2C, and inventory data into a single, governed financial model using Delta Lake and Unity Catalog Lakebase enables real-time querying across that unified layer Mosaic AI continuously monitors working capital metrics like DSO, DPO, and cash conversion cycle, detects anomalies as they emerge, diagnoses root causes, and surfaces corrective actions So, instead of reacting to static reports, finance teams get a closed-loop system: detect, diagnose, simulate and execute — enabling faster, data-driven action at scale.

title: Sponsored by: Precisely | Architecting Agentic-Ready Data Pipelines with Databricks and Precisely
abstract: Agentic AI is accelerating how enterprises operate and make decisions, but most data isn't ready to support it. High-value customer data is buried in unstructured sources — support tickets, call center transcripts, and scanned documents — creating a gap where agents act fast but not always correctly. In this session, we show how Precisely and Databricks Agent Bricks transform this untapped data into agentic-ready data: accessible, contextualized, current, reliable, governed, and automated — so AI agents can act, decide, and execute with accuracy and confidence. Using a multi-agent architecture on Databricks, we demonstrate how free-form text becomes structured information. We extract key customer attributes and improve record integrity using Precisely's native capabilities for data integration, quality, governance, location intelligence, and enrichment—embedded directly into Databricks pipelines via native UDFs, unifying structured and unstructured data to ensure accuracy and reliability.

title: Sponsored by: Prophecy | Accelerating Investment Decisions with Specialized Claude Code
abstract: Portfolio managers at Waterfall Asset Management evaluate hundreds of loans daily and track performance on Databricks. But loan “tapes” arrive as spreadsheets in high volume and inconsistent formats across originating institutions, making bids dependent on time-consuming data cleaning and harmonization before standard metrics and dashboards can be computed. Waterfall Asset Management and Prophecy built a specialized Claude Code “harmonization” agent that automates onboarding into a common schema, requiring only a final validation pass where users review AI confidence, reasoning, and lineage and make any edits. In production, WFAM achieved 93% first-pass accuracy — now approaching 100% — reducing reliance on data experts and materially accelerating investment decisions.

title: Sponsored by: Prophecy | From Weeks to Minutes: Democratizing Marketing Analytics with Governed AI Agents on Databricks
abstract: Enterprise marketing analytics is constrained not by data, but by specialization and handoffs. Translating business intent into reusable strategies takes weeks across multiple teams. In partnership with Acxiom, Prophecy built a specialized AI agent that transforms business intent into production-grade, governed data pipelines. The agent learns schema, relationships and data distributions, understands business intent, automatically invokes analytical models (propensity, affinity, segmentation) and compiles deterministic Spark and SQL workflows executed on Databricks under Unity Catalog governance. What once required multiple teams and weeks of iteration is reduced to a swift, flexible, governed conversational workflow executed by a single marketer - no SQL, no handoffs. This architecture embeds institutional knowledge into reusable AI skills, enabling marketers while maintaining full auditability, lineage and reproducibility, fundamentally reshaping how marketing teams operate.

title: Sponsored by: Qualytics | Your Agents Are Flying Blind: How to Close the Data Control Gap
abstract: Traditional quality frameworks validate data at rest, after ingestion, after transformation, and at the end of the pipeline. But AI agents don't follow that path. They query on demand, pulling from Unity Catalog tables that may have drifted, and they ingest new data from APIs and external sources that have never passed through a quality gate. This is the control gap: the space between where you enforce quality and where AI actually consumes data. In this session, Gorkem Sevinc (CEO, Qualytics) introduces validate-at-use, the principle that data quality should be enforced when an agent reads or receives data. He walks through a live Databricks lakehouse pipeline where an agent encounters stale-validated data and net-new inputs, then closes the gap in real time using Qualytics as the data control layer. You'll leave with a concrete architecture pattern for making your pipelines agent-ready by embedding validate-at-use controls directly into the agent loop.

title: Sponsored By: Qubika | Building a Modern Data Foundation on Databricks: Lessons Learned From FanDuel Migration
abstract: Modern data platform migrations are no longer purely technical initiatives — they are business programs that reshape the foundation for operations, compliance, real-time decision making, and future AI adoption. In this session, Qubika shares how we partnered with FanDuel to migrate core workloads from Amazon Redshift to the Databricks lakehouse in a highly regulated, real-time environment. We cover the key engineering challenges, including rebuilding governance and metadata in Unity Catalog, validating data consistency at scale, and preserving developer velocity across large, multi-team migrations. We then show how these lessons led us to design an AI-powered Migration and Governance Agent — built natively on Databricks and powered by Lakebase as its persistent memory layer — to manage long-running workflows, reason over dependencies, and automate Databricks-ready governance artifacts. Attendees will leave with a practical blueprint to industrialize migrations and reduce risk.

title: Sponsored By: Quest | From Back Office to Boardroom: The New Era of Data Modeling for AI
abstract: For decades, data modeling lived quietly in the back office — essential, but overlooked. AI has changed that. Today, data modeling is no longer a technical afterthought — it is the difference between AI that works and AI that hallucinates, breaks, or fails compliance. Yet most organizations are still applying yesterday’s modeling practices to tomorrow’s AI problems. This session challenges that mindset. We’ll explore how data modeling is evolving into a strategic, AI-era discipline — powering trusted data products, enabling semantic clarity for GenAI, and more! This is not your grandfather’s data modeling. Learn how modern approaches — augmented by automation, metadata intelligence, and AI — are transforming modeling from static documentation into a dynamic, living system that drives business outcomes. See how solutions like Quest Erwin Data Modeler help organizations move faster, reduce risk, and turn data models into a competitive advantage in the age of AI.

We'll walk through how Quest's portfolio of solutions drives a complete data management journey — from foundational modeling through integration, quality, cataloging, and all the way to publishing data products into an internal marketplace for self-service access inside Databricks. Whether you're an executive accountable for data value, an engineer building and managing pipelines, or a business user tired of waiting on IT to get you what you need — this session will show you a better way to manage data end-to-end.

title: Sponsored by: Red Hat | Why AI Evaluation Breaks at Scale — and How to Fix It End-to-End
abstract: Most teams evaluate AI in pieces — one script for agent behavior, another for safety, another for adversarial testing — with no shared results, no audit trail, and no defensible answer to "is this ready to deploy?" The accumulation of disconnected tools isn't a gap you can close by adding another tool. It's an organizational and architectural failure, and it compounds as models and agents move into regulated or high-stakes environments. This session confronts the gap directly. We leverage Evaluation-Driven Development (EDD): a structured methodology that connects behavioral, safety, and adversarial evaluation layers into a single, reproducible workflow — with an audit trail your compliance team can actually use and demonstrate it with open-source tooling that integrates with MLflow. Whether you own the model, the platform, or the risk, this session gives you a shared framework for answering the question that matters: Is this AI-enabled capability ready to be deployed?

title: Sponsored by: Red Panda | The Lakehouse Blind Spot: Querying Streaming Data Before It Lands
abstract: Your Iceberg lakehouse gives you open access to structured, historical data via SQL. But what about events that arrived in the last five seconds — data still in motion? Most data teams have a blind spot: they can query history, but not the present. Skilled engineers can build Flink or Spark jobs to access Kafka/Redpanda, but mere mortals can’t. Some events arrive late. Others simply don’t exist in the lakehouse. These gaps matter: delayed fraud reports, stale ML features, AI agents reasoning on yesterday's context and making bad decisions. Bad agent! In this session, Redpanda's Matt Schumpert explores how streaming data and Iceberg tables can be unified in a single SQL query. Streams are just tables in Redpanda SQL. You'll see how a Postgres-compatible query layer bridges live events and Iceberg tables in S3 transparently, and what that means for your analytics and AI stack.

You’ll see how acting on signals earlier can help your teams adjust plans sooner, resolve issues faster and influence the decisions that matter most.

abstract: Enterprise AI success is not just about models or platform selection. It depends on prioritizing the right work for AI, proving measurable business value, enabling the organization to adopt new ways of working and reducing the drag of legacy systems. In this session, Slalom shares a practical framework for scaling AI on Databricks using accelerators mapped to each part of that equation. Attendees will leave with a simple, actionable model for connecting modernization, value realization and AI adoption at scale.

title: Sponsored by: Snorkel AI | The Art and Science of Benchmarking Agents
abstract: Our ability to measure AI has been outpaced by our ability to develop it, and this evaluation gap is one of the most important problems in AI. We need more enduring benchmarks to close this gap, and consequently advance entire new vectors of capabilities for the field. In this talk, I'll share our learnings evaluating agents, drawing from experience working with nearly all global frontier labs and leading academics. We'll discuss the science (i.e., mechanics that make benchmarks rigorous and effective) and art (i.e., intangibles driving ambitious and enduring benchmarks) of building great benchmarks. I'll close by sharing some of the learnings from Open Benchmarks Grants — a $3M initiative in partnership with Hugging Face, Together AI, Prime Intellect, Factory and others.

title: Sponsored by: Snowplow | The Missing Layer Between Your Lakehouse and Genie: Customer Context with Snowplow
abstract: Genie lets anyone ask data questions in plain English. But ask about customer intent, real-time behavior, or why conversions dropped, and most teams don’t have the data to work with. In this session, we'll show how Snowplow delivers a validated customer context layer directly into your lakehouse, i.e., every digital interaction, human and AI agent alike, governed through Unity Catalog. Pre-built semantic models plug into Genie's knowledge store so business users self-serve behavioral insights without the data team. No custom engineering. No modeling from scratch. We'll also unpack the flywheel: every interaction generates richer data, which sharpens Genie answers and agent decisions. Walk away with a practical architecture for turning Genie into the customer intelligence layer your teams actually trust.

title: Sponsored by: Soda | How Nubank Automates Data Quality Scores with Soda
abstract: As data scales, maintaining trust across decentralized teams becomes a critical challenge. At Nubank, we tackled this by transforming how we measure and scale data health. This presentation details our journey of building a comprehensive Data Quality Strategy using Soda and Databricks. We began by automating standard technical checks across high-priority datasets. To make these metrics actionable for non-technical stakeholders, we aggregated them into a unified Data Quality Score. Managed via Soda Cloud, this framework triggered a massive cultural shift: visibility empowered our business units to move beyond technical compliance and proactively design their own domain-specific business quality checks. Join us to discover the technical architecture and organizational playbook Nubank used to democratize data quality ownership, bridge the gap between engineering and business, and scale automated data trust across the enterprise.

Intelligent routing delivers data to AI agents, edge systems, and business domains simultaneously — no bottlenecks, no point-to-point integrations. Solace's Event Mesh spans AWS, Azure, GCP, on-premises, and edge natively — keeping data governed and discoverable across your estate. Walk away with a concrete architecture and a repeatable pattern your team can deploy in weeks.

title: Sponsored by: Starburst | Unlocking Enterprise AI With Databricks and Starburst
abstract: Databricks has become a foundation for modern data and AI, giving organizations a powerful lakehouse to unify analytics, data engineering, and machine learning. But as adoption grows, many teams still face challenges with fragmented data, inconsistent governance, and the need to move or duplicate data to make it usable. Starburst CEO Justin Borgman explores how Starburst extends the Databricks ecosystem to deliver true enterprise intelligence. Starburst enables fast, federated access across distributed data sources, allowing teams to query data where it lives while integrating seamlessly with the lakehouse. We’ll highlight how Starburst works with Unity Catalog to provide consistent governance, security, and lineage across Databricks and beyond ensuring that AI and analytics are built on a shared, trusted foundation. Learn how to get more from Databricks, accelerate AI innovation, and give your teams the flexibility and control to move faster without compromising governance or cost.

title: Sponsored by: Stardog | Implementing Agentic AI on Databricks with an Ontology-Driven Semantic Layer
abstract: Building reliable AI agents on Databricks requires more than pipelines and models — it demands a semantic foundation that encodes business meaning and context. In this session, we’ll show how to implement an ontology-powered semantic layer that integrates with Delta Lake and Unity Catalog to ground LLM-based agents. You’ll learn how to bootstrap ontologies, enable real-time semantic queries and go beyond traditional RAG approaches. We’ll walk through patterns for evaluating agent performance against natural language queries across use cases like supply chain, drug discovery and compliance. Leave with a practical architecture for deploying explainable, production-ready agentic AI on Databricks.

abstract: Enterprises are reimagining supply chains by consolidating fragmented data into a unified Lakehouse, enabling real-time decisions, AI-driven forecasting, and end-to-end visibility from factory to last mile. In this session, we will showcase how we innovated with AI to accelerate migration, modernization, and transformation of supply chain operations for global customers. This solution addressed critical business challenges like demand volatility, misaligned inventory, shipment risks, and decision latency due to fragmented systems and batch-era architectures that significantly impact cost and performance of operations. Our real time and event-based solution is powered by Structured Streaming, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Agent Bricks and AI/BI Genie architecture to drive ~20+% faster operations, ~$15M+ cost savings, and ~60% reduction in manual effort leading to resilient supply chain operations at scale.

title: Sponsored by: ThoughtSpot | What AI Agents Get Wrong and How Semantics Fixes It
abstract: AI agents are only as good as the context they're given. Yet most enterprise AI stacks leave agents to guess what "revenue," "active customer," or "churn" actually means-producing answers that are confident but wrong. In this session, we'll show how a governed, agentic semantic layer becomes the contract between your data and every AI agent in your stack. You'll see how human-verified business definitions, deterministic SQL, and purpose-built AI context work together in ThoughtSpot to make every agent response accurate, traceable, and trusted by business users-not just data engineers. We'll walk through a live integration between our semantic layer and Databricks Unity Catalog Metric Views, demonstrating a two-way semantic sync that brings governed business logic directly into your AI-native workflows. Whether you're building analytics agents, enterprise copilots, or data products, you'll leave with a replicable pattern for grounding AI in your organization's source of truth.

title: Sponsored by: Weil | Goldmines and Minefields: Building AI Systems for High-Stakes Work
abstract: Most organizations treat AI as a tooling upgrade. Weil treated it as a systems architecture problem — and rebuilt how legal work gets done. This session is for builders — executives, engineers and product leaders — deploying AI where data is messy, stakes are high and trust is non-negotiable. We’ll share what we’ve built — and what it means for deploying AI in real-world, high-stakes environments.

title: Sponsored by: You.com | Building AI Search Infrastructure for the Agentic Era
abstract: AI agents will soon interact with the web more than humans, but the internet's infrastructure was built for people, not agents. This talk explores what open agentic infrastructure actually looks like and why building it matters for anyone developing AI applications. There's a concerning trend towards consolidation in the new era of agentic-driven economics; as major platforms close APIs and wall off their ecosystems, we risk a future where every business becomes a mere data provider to dominant platforms. To solve this, we need to rebuild the infrastructure layer between foundation models and working applications specifically for agents, and we need to keep it open. Saahil Jain, CTO of You.com, will share concrete examples of what this new infrastructure requires, the technical and business challenges of keeping it accessible, and how developers and companies can help build the foundation layer that enables sophisticated AI applications without platform lock-in.

title: Sponsored by: Zipher | Dynamic Compute Allocation: Runtime Placement to Reduce Costs by up to 60%
abstract: Choosing compute for data workloads is often treated as a static decision: this job runs on Serverless, that pipeline on Classic compute, this workload uses a pool, and this stream runs on an all-purpose cluster. But production environments are dynamic: load changes by run, day, week, and business cycle. The same job may process twice as much data during business hours while facing the same tight SLA constraints. Supply conditions also shift constantly: spot pricing, instance availability, and spare capacity in pools or clusters. This session frames compute selection as a runtime placement problem and gives teams a practical toolbox for efficient allocation across SKUs.

title: SQL Is Still Your Superpower: Building Production Ready Data Pipelines Using Only SQL
abstract: SQL didn’t get weaker, data platforms got better. In this session, we demonstrate how modern data engineering on Databricks can be delivered end-to-end using SQL alone on the Lakehouse, without dependency on Python or external frameworks, including SQL AI functions and Geospatial Functions. Designed for organisations with strong BI/SQL foundations, this session shows how to transition to production-grade data engineering with minimal upskilling. We showcase how pipelines are built using Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines via the Pipeline Editor, with ingestion, transformation, and data quality rules all defined declaratively in SQL. This demonstrates how SQL moves beyond querying into full pipeline engineering. Governance is implemented by design using Unity Catalog, providing fine-grained permissions, lineage, and auditability across the entire pipeline. We also showcase AI/BI Genie, configured using SQL-only approaches (metrics, dimensions, instructions, and evaluation queries), enabling natural language access to trusted data. This session reframes SQL as a first-class engineering language on the Lakehouse, capable of handling streaming, transformation, data quality, governance, and AI consumption, while unlocking existing talent and accelerating adoption without increasing complexity.

title: SQL Programming and Procedural Logic
abstract: In this hands-on course, you will explore core SQL programming and procedural logic skills within Databricks, focusing on how to build modular, maintainable, and production-ready analytics workflows. You’ll start by learning about key SQL constructs—such as Common Table Expressions, temporary views, and User Defined Functions—that make your SQL development cleaner and more reusable. The course then guides you through advanced SQL scripting techniques using compound statements, variables, control flow, conditionals, loops, and robust error handling to create structured and flexible SQL processes. Finally, you’ll discover how to orchestrate and modernize complex workflows with Lakeflow Jobs and migration strategies, transforming legacy tasks into modular, automated pipelines that leverage the full capabilities of the Databricks platform. Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. title: SQM: From Fragmented Data Silos to Real-Time ML Operations with Delta Sharing
abstract: SQM set out to increase production efficiency by improving how raw materials are converted into finished product. But, it faced a classic data engineering challenge: critical operational data was trapped in silos (plant historians, lab systems, simulation tools) with no scalable way to unify it with enterprise data in Databricks. Operating decisions relied on operator experience rather than predictive models, leading to excess raw material use and inconsistent output. Instead of building custom ETL pipelines to move data across systems, SQM leveraged Delta Sharing to create a governed, real-time data backbone. AVEVA’s cloud-based industrial intelligence platform, CONNECT, seamlessly shared data with Databricks on Azure using zero-copy and no data movement. This enabled operational data to be unified and refined into consistent minute-level views, and used to develop machine learning and optimization models.

title: Stateful Apps for Thousands of Users: Horizontal Scaling, Session Affinity, and Sharding in Databricks Apps
abstract: Databricks Apps make it easy to stand up a powerful internal app, but most teams don’t have a clear mental model for what happens when usage jumps from a handful of users to hundreds or thousands. In this advanced, under-the-hood session, we’ll walk through how Databricks Apps can remain stateful at scale: horizontal scaling across multiple app instances, session affinity to keep user context and in-memory state attached to the right replica, and sharding to distribute traffic and load safely across your fleet. By the end, you’ll have a practical architecture playbook and checklist you can apply to take an existing Databricks App—from LLM agents to analytics UIs—and harden it for real production scale without giving up the fast developer experience you already enjoy.

title: Stop Arguing About Numbers: How Zalando Scales Governance With Unity Catalog and Metric Views
abstract: At Zalando’s scale—serving over 50M European customers via a decentralized microservices architecture—data governance quickly turns into a "Data Swamp." Domain teams shipped fast, but without a unified semantic layer, "Net Revenue" on a marketing dashboard rarely matched the finance report. We faced a familiar dilemma: centralize and create bottlenecks, or stay decentralized and lose trust in our numbers. This session will focus on our implementation of Unity Catalog, scaled across an organization with over 1,000 data engineers. This setup fosters team autonomy, enabling rapid data creation. We will also detail the governance mechanisms we've put in place to facilitate data sharing while maintaining minimal compliance risk. We’ll then go deep into how we use metric views to move business logic out of siloed BI tools and directly into the lakehouse. This metric-as-code approach ensures that whether users query via notebooks, dashboards or AI agents, they get the same trusted answer.

title: Stream into the Future: Mastering Stream processing for All Workloads
abstract: The data world isn't slowing down—it’s streaming faster than ever. And if you're still thinking batch-first, it's time to flip the script. title: Streaming at Scale With Real-Time Mode: Sub-Second Train Telemetry Across the Netherlands
abstract: In this talk, we showcase how NS (Dutch Railways) built an end-to-end Databricks solution that processes train telemetry in real time, enabling live detection of carriage failures and improving overall reliability. The platform handles more than 100 billion data points per day with sub-second end-to-end latency. The session features a live demo of real train telemetry, giving the audience a direct, in‑room experience of real time. We explain how the solution was engineered using the new Real-Time Mode for Spark Structured Streaming. The entire stack is built in PySpark and SQL, so no microservices, no separate streaming framework, just Databricks. Throughout the session, we connect to other high velocity domains with cases like real time parcel rerouting, live airport baggage tracking and real-time signals feeding analytics and AI. Attendees leave with practical insights into bringing real time data into the modern data stack without the complexity of traditional streaming systems.

title: Streaming NASA Data with Lakeflow and Agent Bricks: A Data Engineer's Guide to Databricks AI
abstract: This Data + AI Summit session walks you through a streaming application that analyzes live NASA space data using Lakeflow and Agent Bricks. Lakeflow is the foundation layer of every AI application. I explain how Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP) ingests from one of the very few public Kafka topics that exist and how it works in symbiosis with Agent Bricks to turn real-time NASA circulars about cosmic events into an AI-powered knowledge base with Databricks Apps UI. The AI stack covers AI Gateway, guardrails, Vector Search, agent evaluation, and MLflow tracing, all from a data engineer's perspective. The second part focuses on Time to Value. I used several Databricks AI tools: Genie Code, Claude Code, the AI Dev Kit, and others. Each capable of taking you from zero to a working application in days rather than months. I share the trade-offs and best practices learned. Grab the full application from GitHub afterward — and play with data from exploding supernovas.

title: Streaming the Game: Scaling Real-Time Intelligence at DraftKings With Kafka, Databricks & Sigma
abstract: DraftKings set out to build a real-time analytics capability before the use cases were fully defined. Rather than waiting for perfect requirements, we invested in the streaming foundation first — allowing meaningful use cases to emerge from the platform itself. We assembled an initial solution to deliver second-level visibility into transactions, active users, and revenue. As stakeholders gained live insight, new needs surfaced — including real-time liability tracking and deeper financial monitoring — many not originally envisioned. title: Supporting Fine-Grained Access Control with Server-Side Scan Planning
abstract: Open table formats such as Iceberg allow organizations to run multiple engines on shared data, but this openness makes governance difficult. Unity Catalog already supports universal table-level access control for external engines like Starburst via credential vending, but that alone cannot support fine-grained policies like column masking or row filtering. UC’s move to server-side scan planning, built on Iceberg REST Catalog Scan APIs, allows enforcement of fine-grained access control in Starburst: policies are defined and applied server-side, and Starburst uses the filtered scan plan from UC to respect them, with no bespoke policy logic. Starburst and Databricks share how they collaborated to bring fine-grained access control to Starburst on UC-managed Iceberg tables.

title: The 52x Multiplier: How Zepto Mastered AI Agent Evaluation at Scale
abstract: In quick commerce, delivery windows are measured in minutes, making AI reliability existential. At Zepto, scaling to 80,000 daily autonomous support tickets demanded more than “vibe-based” testing—it required treating evaluation as core infrastructure. This session unveils the comprehensive dual-loop framework (powered by MLFlow 3.0 and DSPy) that transforms operational risk into a competitive advantage. We achieved a verified 52X ROI on evaluation infrastructure, slashing support costs by 65% while boosting CSAT by 20.5%. By shifting from reactive fixes to real-time tracing, we compressed issue detection from 3 hours to 5 minutes and reduced social media escalations by 74%. We will deconstruct the technical blueprint for establishing “Evaluation as Infrastructure”—covering LLM-as-a-Judge calibration, strategic sampling, and automated feedback loops—enabling teams to deploy complex, multimodal AI agents with absolute confidence and control.

title: The Agentic Stack: A Founder Conversation on the Open Infrastructure Powering AI Agents
abstract: The next great platform shift isn't a model. It's the infrastructure that turns models into autonomous action. Just as cloud produced a layered stack of open technologies, the agentic era is producing its own, defined right now, in the open. This panel brings together the founders building each layer: how agents are constructed, how they collaborate as teams, how context is processed and made agent-ready, and how they're governed at scale. Together, they'll discuss what the "Linux moment" for agents looks like and what it means when the most consequential software in an enterprise writes itself. The big questions: Where does the open platform stack land in next 2-3 years - a thriving ecosystem or a consolidated stack? What happens when agents become the primary consumers of infrastructure, not humans? When does multi-agent coordination actually outperform a single well-built agent and when is it just complexity for complexity's sake? Who owns accountability when an open-source agent takes an autonomous action on production data? How do agents process context differently than humans? What are the implications on how context must be processed and exposed through tool interfaces?

title: The Data Gap in Women's Football & How FIFPro and Databricks Are Helping to Close It
abstract: As the FIFA World Cup kicks off in the USA days before this summit, billions will follow the men's game, but women footballers still fight for visibility and basic protections. FIFPro, representing 65,000+ professional footballers, is using data to change that. For over a decade, FIFPro has surveyed women footballers worldwide on working conditions, welfare and employment rights. But that data lived on laptops in fragmented spreadsheets with critical insights locked away. In this session, Blend shares how we built a data platform on Databricks to power evidence-based advocacy. We'll cover designing a medallion architecture for messy survey data spanning multiple tournament cycles, configuring AI/BI Genie so non-technical researchers can query data in natural language, and building Power BI dashboards that surface cross-confederation trends. When women's football data sits on laptops, it's easy to overlook. In a lakehouse, it's impossible to ignore.

title: The Databricks Big Book of AgentOps: The New DevOps Principles for AI Agents
abstract: The journey from traditional machine learning models to AI systems demands a new, specialized set of operational practices. This talk traces the evolution of core DevOps principles from the decade of MLOps to the Agents era, where we must plan for deploying and maintaining autonomous, multi-step AI agents that can reason, plan, and take actions in the real world using external tools.The talk will show how classic DevOps tenets like continuous deployment must be radically re-engineered to tackle core AgentOps challenges. Authors of The Databricks Big Book of Agent Ops will cover:Ensuring Maturity of Operational Controls: How critical operational controls must evolve to support multi-agent architectures.Distributed Tracing and Observability: Transforming single-step I/O logs into traces essential for debugging and explaining agent behavior.Governed Deployment and Rollback: Establishing AgentOps CI/CD pipelines that treat configurations (prompts, tools, routing logic) as code

title: The Enterprise Guide to Agentic AI Risk: Security, Governance, and the Cross-Functional Playbook
abstract: When AI systems shift from analyzing to acting, the threat model changes fundamentally. Most enterprises are not ready. Agentic AI amplifies both the speed of innovation and the magnitude of risk, creating new attack surfaces and governance gaps that no single team can close alone. The organizations getting this right are building cross-functional response models that unite security, data, legal, and technology leadership around a shared risk framework. In this session, Databricks CISO Omar Khawaja introduces the lethal trifecta of agentic risk, the three converging conditions that create enterprise-scale exposure and the organizational playbook for neutralizing it. You'll walk away with a prioritized set of actions your enterprise can begin implementing in the next 30 days, and a model for the cross-functional partnerships that make agentic AI governable at scale.

title: The Evolution of Prompting: From Artisan Craft to Algorithmic Optimization
abstract: LLMs unlocked advanced capabilities for users of all technical abilities precisely because of their natural language interface. Building enterprise solutions involved prompt engineering - a process of trial and error. This talk explores how automated prompt optimization represents a paradigm shift in how we build high quality, maintainable enterprise solutions with LLMs. We'll examine the core limitations of hand-crafted prompting, then dive into how prompt optimizers solve these problems. The session will cover the current state of the art in prompt optimization, including the latest algorithms such as GEPA. We'll demonstrate measurable performance gains that prompt optimizers achieve over manual engineering - often discovering counterintuitive prompts that humans would never write but dramatically outperform our best handcrafted attempts. You'll leave understanding how prompt optimizers work and why they are essential for building high quality, maintainable GenAI solutions.

title: The Full Databricks App Experience
abstract: What does a real Databricks App look like in production? In this session, we walk through an internal tool we use every day: an agentic Lakeflow generation system built entirely on the Databricks platform. Starting from raw Unity Catalog tables, the app uses foundational models orchestrated in a LangGraph loop to profile data, design pipelines, validate transformations and generate fully deployable Lakeflow artefacts from Silver through to Gold. We’ll show how application state, specifications, and user preferences are managed in Lakebase, enabling a seamless, iterative build experience inside Databricks. Forget the quick toy POC Apps you've been seeing. This is a practical blueprint for building intelligent, stateful data applications natively on the lakehouse.

title: The Future Is Self-Serve: Lessons Learned on Democratized Data and AI Agents at OpenAI
abstract: OpenAI isn’t just building breakthrough AI—it’s reinventing how teams work, grow, and scale in an AI-first world. In this session, hear directly from Jeff Canada, Marketing Operations Lead about how OpenAI is transforming its organization to support rapid and sustained growth. He’ll share how OpenAI built a trusted system of record on Databricks and how composable technologies built on Databricks, such as Hightouch, enable accurate, self-serve access to data and AI across the business. You’ll walk away with practical lessons on modern data foundations, democratized access across teams, and AI-powered operations—but more importantly, you’ll get inspired by how OpenAI empowers every team member to move faster and make better decisions in an AI-driven future.

title: The Future of Cross-Company Collaboration on Databricks
abstract: For years, cross-company collaboration meant sharing files, tables, and dashboards. That era is ending. In this session, we explore the next era of collaboration — one where organizations share intelligence, not just data. Databricks is reimagining what it means to work across organizational boundaries. Instead of exchanging static assets, partners and customers will interact through AI-native experiences — governed, secure, and designed for a world where every company runs on agents. We'll paint the picture of a new ecosystem of tools and services that turns every data relationship into something dynamic, conversational, and instantly valuable. If you believe the future of B2B is agentic, this session will show you where it's all heading. You'll leave with a new mental model for what collaboration looks like when AI is the interface.

title: The Genie Effect: Real-World Conversational Analytics Across Healthcare & Life Sciences
abstract: Conversational analytics promises to democratize data, but the path from promise to production looks different in every organization. In this session, cross-industry leaders pull back the curtain on their Genie deployments spanning four distinct functional domains: global supply chain, commercial sales and marketing, workforce staffing optimization, and healthcare intelligence for reducing readmissions. You'll hear what drove adoption, where implementation got messy, and how each team defined, and measured, value. Whether you're evaluating conversational AI for the first time or scaling an existing deployment, this cross-industry conversation delivers the unfiltered perspective you won't find in a case study.

title: The Lakehouse Behind a Modern CDP
abstract: Building a CDP isn’t just a UI and APIs—it’s a data platform problem at scale. This talk shows how Warner Bros. Discovery built the Databricks-powered “back of house” for Mosaic, supporting audience segmentation and activation across millions of subscribers. We’ll walk through the data plane that converts high-volume first-party events (client SDK + server events) into governed Delta tables using Spark Structured Streaming, then runs incremental batch pipelines to produce custom attributes and curated event views for segmentation across identity grains. We’ll also cover the audience evaluation engine: drag-and-drop audience definitions are stored as rule trees, compiled into Spark plans and evaluated at scale to generate deterministic audience outputs for downstream delivery. Key production patterns include table modeling, join/partition strategies, observability and separation between the metadata plane (API-driven config) and the Databricks execution plane.

abstract: In the race to outpace automated threats, AI is no longer optional, it is the primary defense. We will dive into the practicalities of:Operationalizing Safety: How to deploy AI-driven detection and response without introducing new enterprise risks.The Velocity Gain: Leveraging AI to radically compress vulnerability lifecycles and patching windows.Guardrails for Autonomy: Implementing the essential governance "kill switches" and oversight needed when moving toward an Agentic SIEM.This session provides a practical roadmap for security leaders trying to navigate the "Speed vs Risk" dilemma of deploying modern AI technology.

title: The New Genie: From Data Q&A to Enterprise Agent
abstract: In this session, we'll introduce the new Genie, a unified, multi-agent AI that doesn't just answer questions about your data, it acts on it. We'll show how Genie connects enterprise knowledge stores and unstructured content to deliver richer insights, how it orchestrates across Genie Agents to complete complex work, and how it can take governed actions on your behalf, including automating recurring tasks and skills. Attendees will leave understanding why Genie is not just a data Q&A chatbot, but an enterprise AI that connects your people, your data, and your systems — and gets work done.

abstract: AI agents are reshaping how engineers and teams work, but the path from experimentation to real production looks different than anyone expected. title: The Open Handshake: Scaling Multi-Cloud Delivery via Delta Sharing and Iceberg
abstract: Client demand is shifting. They don’t want our data; they want it in their platform. We solved the “Vendor Lock-in” crisis by building an Open Data Passport. This session deconstructs how we leveraged Delta Sharing and Apache Iceberg UniForm to deliver high-scale healthcare products to clients without moving a single byte of raw data. We’ll share the engineering “scars” of managing cross-cloud permissions and how we turned an interoperability headache into a competitive product advantage for our global ecosystem. Demo: A live cross-platform “handshake” between a Databricks source and a non-Databricks consumer with zero ETL. Takeaways: Architecting zero-copy delivery via Delta Sharing Managing multi-platform governance Building vendor-agnostic data products

title: The Open Security Lakehouse: Building Agentic Cyber Defense with Lakewatch
abstract: Legacy SIEMs are drowning security teams in alerts but starving them of insight. As threats grow more complex and attackers operate at machine speed, cybersecurity must be treated as a data and AI problem at scale. In this session, we'll walk through a Cybersecurity Intelligence Platform powered by Lakewatch, Databricks' open, agentic SIEM. We'll show how to streamline security data ingestion and automated cloud log collection, then rapidly normalize it into the OCSF standard to cut time-to-value. From there, we'll explore large-scale analytics, behavioural ML, and Detection-as-Code workflows that bring software engineering rigor to detection and response. The highlight is Agentic Threat Hunting with Lakewatch: AI agents that reason over security signals alongside business and application data, leveraging internal knowledge to add critical context, reduce false positives, and automate complex triage. Join us to see how modern SOCs can move beyond the traditional SIEM toward true security intelligence with Lakewatch and the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform.

title: The Recipe for Data Transformation at Scale: How GM Financial Built a Governed, AI-Ready Enterprise
abstract: Most enterprise data transformations stall because they solve the technology problem without solving the people and governance problem. GM Financial, General Motors' finance arm, chose a different path. Guided by a clear enterprise data vision and a multi-year transformation on Databricks, they moved from fragmented reporting to a governed, AI-enabled analytics ecosystem without sacrificing SOX compliance or data trust. In this session, CDAO Latha Subramanian shares the institutional 'recipe' that made it work: a data strategy board, formal stewardship councils, communities of practice that drove enterprise-wide literacy, and a Databricks Center of Excellence that turned adoption from aspiration into culture. She'll show how Genie, their Databricks-powered natural language interface, democratized self-service analytics for non-technical users, and how their FinOps framework gave leaders pipeline-to-query cost visibility for the first time. If you're responsible for an enterprise data program that needs to deliver both innovation and auditability, this session is your playbook.

In this session, CDAO Latha Subramanian shares the institutional 'recipe' that made it work: a data strategy board, formal stewardship councils, communities of practice that drove enterprise-wide literacy, and a Databricks Center of Excellence that turned adoption from aspiration into culture. She'll show how Genie, their Databricks-powered natural language interface, democratized self-service analytics for non-technical users, and how their FinOps framework gave leaders pipeline-to-query cost visibility for the first time. If you're responsible for an enterprise data program that needs to deliver both innovation and auditability, this session is your playbook.

title: The Right Model for the Job: A Practical Framework for AI
abstract: Not every problem needs the biggest model — and not every model works out of the box. With frontier models, small open models, and fine-tuning all on the table, the hardest question isn't "can we do AI?" It's "which model is actually right for this?"In this session, we walk through how to match models to use cases across real enterprise workloads. You'll see when a frontier model earns its cost, when a small open model wins on latency, and when fine-tuning turns a generic model into a specialist that knows your business. We'll put the tradeoffs in action — quality, cost, latency, control — using concrete examples across customer support, document processing, and analytics.You'll leave with a repeatable framework for choosing, customizing, and deploying the right model on Databricks every time — and the patterns to keep those decisions sharp as new models land.

title: The Road to Delta 5.0
abstract: Marking its ninth anniversary this year, Delta Lake has grown significantly since its 2017 debut, spanning four major versions and 33 individual releases. As a premier ACID-compliant open table format globally, it sees 40M+ downloads per month and powers the daily processing of hundreds of exabytes of data. While the current roadmap includes the recent launch of Delta 4.3, the project is undergoing foundational shifts as it moves toward Delta 5.0. This session explores these paradigm shifts through two primary lenses: Evolution and Unification. Key topics will include: The transition of Delta into a catalog-first table format. Modernizing Delta on Spark by leveraging Data Source V2 APIs. The convergence of the Delta and Iceberg formats. Harmonizing the Delta Kernel across Java and Rust implementations.

title: The Upcoming Apache Spark™ 4.2: The Next Chapter in Unified Analytics
abstract: AI workloads demand real-time feature pipelines, multimodal data support, and seamless AI-assisted development. Apache Spark™ 4.2 brings these capabilities into the engine, unifying batch and streaming while optimizing them at the planner level. Metric views provide a first-class semantic layer to define measures once and ensure consistent results. Catalog-managed flows make incremental and streaming queries lifecycle-aware catalog objects. A language-agnostic UDF protocol enables portable user logic across Python and emerging Spark Connect languages. Enhanced LLM discoverability and local performance improvements, including Arrow-backed caching and shuffle-free execution, make development faster and more interactive. Apache Spark™ 4.2 evolves into a governed, incremental, and AI-native platform built for the demands of the AI age.

title: The Write Way: Building Bi-Directional Data Pipelines in the Lakehouse
abstract: Ever wondered how to bridge the gap between analytical data and operational workflows without breaking your lakehouse architecture? What if business users could edit data directly in a web app while maintaining a single source of truth? Traditional lakehouses excel at analytics but struggle with user-driven updates, often creating silos or complex workarounds. There’s a better way—in this session we’ll cover a full writeback loop where lakehouse (Unity Catalog) syncs to PostgreSQL (Lakebase) for operational speed, a Databricks app offers an intuitive editing interface and Lakeflow jobs sync changes back every 5 minutes. The lakehouse stays the source of truth while users get flexibility. We’ll explore scenarios including form-based data entry, table editing and data quality workflows, all built with Dash and Databricks Asset Bundles. By the end, you'll have a clear blueprint for building bi-directional data flows that empower users without sacrificing governance or reliability.

title: Thinking Fast & Slow: How Databricks Built High-Speed and Deep Research Agents
abstract: In today's competitive agentic search landscape, two operating modes are mission-critical. The first is a low-latency, low-cost mode for consumer-facing scale. It must meet strict tail-latency budgets for real-time, high-throughput use cases at minimal per-query cost, without sacrificing quality. The second is a compute-intensive deep research mode enabling expert-level analysis—from financial due diligence and technology mapping to clinical review and manufacturing diagnostics. The system must plan multi-step retrieval, triangulate sources, and synthesize coherent answers. Using our Instructed Retriever and Aroll frameworks, we built a unified agentic harness supporting both modes in a single architecture. Our system sits at the Pareto frontier of cost, speed, and quality. Instant mode delivers single-digit second latency maintaining accuracy, while Thinking mode achieves SoTA-level performance across enterprise domains.

title: Three Steps to Red Team Your LLMs on Databricks (Using Tools You Didn't Know You Had)
abstract: You added guardrails, PII filters and safety controls. Then someone Base64-encodes a prompt injection and your model hands over data like it was asked nicely. This session is a live walkthrough of how to red team your LLMs on Databricks using BlackIce, Databricks' own open-source containerised toolkit. 14 security tools. One Docker image. Five minutes to deploy. In three steps we will spin up a model serving endpoint with AI Gateway guardrails, launch BlackIce on a single-node cluster with NVIDIA's Garak, Microsoft's PyRIT, Meta's CyberSecEval and 11 more tools ready to go, then point Garak at the endpoint and run attack probes, encoding attacks, jailbreaks, prompt injection and system prompt extraction — to get an Attack Success Rate in minutes. You'll leave fully understanding how to use BlackIce to secure your LLMs, whilst feeling slightly more paranoid about just how easy they are to break. Better you find out here than in production.

title: Tips and Tricks for Postgres Observability at Scale
abstract: Running Postgres in production gets harder as your application grows — logs pile up, metrics live in one tool, schema changes live in another, and when something breaks, you are stuck stitching it all together under pressure. This session shares practical tips and tricks for getting ahead of common Postgres operational challenges — we will cover how to spot configuration issues before they hit production, how to unblock application updates when schema changes go sideways, and how to quickly connect application failures back to the database changes that caused them. Along the way, we will show how bringing Postgres operational data together with modern AI tooling can take a lot of the manual work out of diagnostics — so you spend less time hunting for root causes and more time shipping. Whether you are running a handful of Postgres instances or managing them at scale, you will leave with concrete techniques you can apply to your own environment.

title: Train and Fine-Tune AI Models Without Managing GPUs
abstract: Enterprise AI is entering a new era. Organizations are moving beyond small models to train and fine-tune increasingly sophisticated AI systems—from foundation models and recommendation engines to forecasting, computer vision, and reinforcement learning workloads. Yet scaling AI often means managing GPUs, distributed training, and complex infrastructure. In this session, we'll introduce AI Runtime, Databricks' new serverless GPU training experience. Powered by on-demand GPUs and tightly integrated with Lakehouse data, AI Runtime gives data scientists and ML engineers instant access to high-performance compute for training and fine-tuning models at scale. We'll cover the latest trends in deep learning, transformer architectures, and open-source foundation models, and demonstrate how AI Runtime works seamlessly with PyTorch, Hugging Face, and other leading frameworks. You'll also see how Databricks delivers a unified deep learning experience across MLflow, Lakeflow, Unity Catalog, Genie Code, and Notebooks. Join us to learn how to accelerate experimentation, optimize GPU workloads, leverage coding agents, and move from idea to production faster with AI Runtime—with no infrastructure management required.

title: Translating Nubank’s Data Lake Access Control Model Into Databricks Unity Catalog
abstract: Nubank implemented consistent, fine-grained access control across its multi-platform data environment by translating its internal data lake access control model into Databricks Unity Catalog permissions. This model uses centrally managed "Permission Groups" (based on geography, data domains and column sensitivity) to govern access to over 300K tables for 5K+ users, enforcing control at the table and column level. The presentation will detail the architectural implementation, the programmatic translation process using Unity Catalog APIs, and the application of read-time masking for sensitive columns. It will address practical challenges in modeling fine-grained permissions and operating at scale, providing attendees with a reusable architectural pattern and concrete lessons for designing scalable, enterprise-grade access control on Databricks.

Fragmented data environments had long made it difficult to build a focussed, timely view of customer needs, slowing decision‑making and limiting the value we could return to customers. In this session, we’ll share how NAB is using Databricks to bring customer data together into a unified, trusted platform and how Genie is making those insights accessible across the bank. By enriching transactional data and making it accessible in reusable, product‑ready datasets, our teams can spot customer needs faster, design more relevant experiences, and respond with greater consistency across channels.You’ll hear how this shift is helping NAB move from isolated insights to shared customer signals, supporting everything from day‑to‑day service improvements to more personalised products and smarter risk decisions. Join us to explore how a modern data platform is enabling NAB to deliver simpler, more responsive banking, and what this approach could mean for the future of customer‑centred financial services.

title: Turning Data Requests Into Self-Service: Building an AI-Powered Analytics Product Users Love
abstract: Ticketmaster's operations team was drowning in data requests. Every "how many fans showed up to buy tickets last week?" question cost engineering hours. We were spending over 8 weeks/year being human query engines. We needed to give users the power to answer their own questions.We built OMT Wizard: a conversational analytics tool that lets non-technical users ask questions in plain English and get instant answers. Powered by Databricks Genie, it launched to 500+ users and achieved high stickiness. The users who try it keep coming back. This session shares product lessons from building AI-powered internal tools — how we identified the right problem to solve, designed for trust and transparency, trained the AI on business logic, measured real adoption and turned skeptics into champions. You'll learn what worked — suggested questions, showing your work — what didn't — hiding complexity — and how to build AI products that solve real problems instead of looking for problems to solve.

title: UC Managed Tables: What's New and How to Decide, Adopt, and Scale
abstract: UC managed tables built on Delta and Iceberg table formats deliver faster query performance, lower storage costs, and automatic optimizations out of the box — and they've improved significantly in the last year. This session covers what's new, what UC managed tables unlock, and what you need to know to make an informed decision. We'll walk through the latest capabilities now available on UC managed tables. Highlights include Catalog Commits that enable writes from external engines and multi-statement transactions, Managed Disaster Recovery, Automatic Upgrades, Auto-TTL, Auto Indexing, Automatic Liquid Clustering and Predictive Optimization which can increase query speeds by 20x and reduce storage costs by 50%. From there, we'll address the questions we hear most and share best practices. How can I easily convert to managed tables if I access my external tables today by path? How can I segregate my data? How can I access these tables externally? You'll leave with a clear understanding of what UC managed tables offer today, what's changed, and a framework for deciding when and how to adopt them.

title: Ultra Low Latency Streaming for Real-Time Feature Engineering
abstract: Feature freshness is critical for fraud-detection, ad tech, real-time recommendations, dynamic pricing, etc. Historically, ML engineers have had to maintain two separate systems for feature engineering, leveraging Spark and Spark Structure Streaming for batch/near real-time features, while building bespoke pipelines when they needed sub-second feature freshness. In this session, we'll learn about Real-Time Mode in Apache Spark Structured Streaming, the engine behind the Databricks Feature Store, and how companies like DraftKings are using it to power real-time features with millisecond-level freshness. You'll learn how to pair Real-Time Mode with Lakebase to build a state-of-the-art online feature store and leave with a practical blueprint for a unified feature engineering platform that eliminates logic spread across different systems and shifts the focus from infrastructure orchestration to semantic feature modeling.

title: Under the Hood: Scalable Ingestion Strategies for Databases, Applications, and File Sources
abstract: Data engineers spend far too much time maintaining fragile scripts for a fragmented landscape of databases, applications, and file sources. In this technical session, we’ll explore how Lakeflow Connect allows you to build robust pipelines without the operational burden of DIY infrastructure. We’ll dive into: Database ingestion: A look under the hood at efficient CDC for sources like Oracle, MySQL, and Postgres, alongside query-based ingestion for sources like Teradata, Redshift, and Synapse. Application and file ingestion: What’s new—and happening behind the scenes—across our newest connectors for customer 360, employee 360, financial analytics, and more. Cost and performance optimization: Technical best practices for networking, security, and minimizing impact on source systems—plus how to use new features to slash TCO and boost performance. We’ll wrap up with how to create your own application and database connectors. Stop managing infrastructure and start delivering data.

title: Unified Governance for Enterprise Analytics and AI
abstract: We implemented a unified governance architecture for enterprise analytics leveraging Databricks Unity Catalog as the authoritative control plane. The platform designed with a configuration-driven, dynamic attribute-based access control (ABAC) model with fully enforced row-level security (RLS) and column-level security (CLS) ensuring precise, policy-driven data access across the organization — including hierarchical visibility for cost owners and business leaders aligned to their reporting structures. This design prevents governance drift, reduces operational complexity, centralizes policy management, and enables secure self-service analytics across domains. Governance policies extend natively to AI/BI dashboards and Databricks Genie, ensuring consistent, compliant data access without duplicating or redefining security frameworks. Impact Eliminated decentralized access control models across 40+ dashboards. Enabled secure self-service analytics for 300+ users across 20+ teams.

title: Unified SRE Observability: How Workday Democratizes Multi-Platform Insights with Databricks Genie
abstract: As Workday’s infrastructure scaled across multi-cloud environments, the Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) teams faced a common hurdle: fragmented data silos. Monitoring reliability across Databricks, Snowflake, ServiceNow and FiveTran required pivoting between tools, leading to delayed insights and manual reporting toil. To solve this, Workday built a unified cross-platform KPI dashboard on Databricks, centralizing telemetry into a single pane of glass for platform adoption, job performance and ITSM health. This session explores the architecture behind this “one-stop shop” — leveraging third-party integrations for seamless ingestion and the power of Databricks Genie. By embedding conversational AI into the SRE workflow, Workday enables stakeholders to “talk to their data” — getting instant, natural-language answers without SQL. Learn how this shift from static charts to AI-driven insights has accelerated incident response, improved governance and freed SREs to focus on engineering.

title: Unifying Upstream Intelligence with Generative AI
abstract: PetroWizard & IntelliSense utilizes an agent-based generative AI architecture on Databricks to address PETRONAS's challenge of fragmented, largely unstructured upstream data (90% unstructured, across OSDU, PI, SQL, etc.). Engineers previously spent 3–5 days locating data. This solution, featuring a Central Orchestrator and four specialized agents (Subsurface, Surface, Sensor, Model Router), enables cross-domain reasoning and model-agnostic, governed data intelligence. Outcomes include reducing data discovery time to 30–45 seconds, achieving 90%+ query accuracy, high user satisfaction (4/5 across 3,000+ users) and full audit traceability, fundamentally transforming upstream decision-making.

We'll also cover how to apply consistent policies across providers — so developers can move fast with coding agents while maintaining the control, visibility, and compliance production environments demand.You'll walk away with the patterns to unlock coding agents safely across your organization — without creating a new compliance liability.

title: Unity Catalog 101: Unified Governance for data, AI and applications
abstract: As organizations build AI-powered applications and autonomous agents, governance becomes more complex. Data, models and tools must be discovered, understood and securely accessed across teams, platforms and engines, yet governance is often fragmented across catalogs, security systems and AI tooling. Unity Catalog is the unified governance solution for all AI agents, applications and data on the Databricks Platform. It enables organizations to discover trusted data with shared business context, apply consistent governance policies across data and AI assets and automate governance workflows using built-in intelligence, all while governing open data formats and assets across clouds and platforms. In this introductory session, we’ll walk through how Unity Catalog works and how it enables three foundational capabilities: discovery with business context, unified AI governance and AI-powered automation. You’ll learn how organizations use Unity Catalog to simplify governance, reduce data and AI sprawl and build trusted AI systems on an open and governed data foundation.

title: Unity Catalog External Locations: Extending Governance to OneLake and Beyond
abstract: Unity Catalog External Locations are how Databricks connects to storage. Users define a path to the storage, attach a credential, and UC governs everything built on top: managed tables, views and other assets. Currently, it supports S3, ADLS, GCS and Cloudflare R2. We are expanding this functionality to include support for Microsoft OneLake. In this session, we'll show how External Locations provide a consistent, extensible pattern for connecting Databricks to any storage platform — and walk through what it takes to create External Location for Microsoft OneLake. You'll see the architecture, the setup end-to-end, and a demo reading and writing UC-governed assets directly into OneLake storage without needing to setup any ETL pipelines. We will close the session with what’s next: extending the same model to on-premise storage, so Unity Catalog becomes a single governance layer across your data estate.

title: Unlock radical speed-to-market with agentic execution powered by Celonis Process Intelligence
abstract: Companies struggle to keep pace with shifting consumer demand and strict regulatory mandates because their go-to-market process is bogged down by isolated processes, disparate data, and limited visibility. This lack of transparency across R&D, sourcing, manufacturing, sales, and distribution leads to missed seasonal windows and penalties, putting millions in revenue at risk. title: Unlocking Antibody Space With Databricks Vector Search
abstract: Antibodies form the bedrock of human health, and the body’s ability to create what is estimated to be a quintillion unique variants creates an impressive scaling issue for their study. Molecules derived from antibodies are now the fastest growing therapeutic category, and our understanding of how to design and modify antibodies requires solutions that scale. Databricks Vector Search provides an engineered solution for scaling up similarity search to 1 billion embeddings per endpoint, and by embedding antibody sequences with the protein language model AMPLIFY we will describe how this system might be used with the Observed Antibody Space dataset. The potential throughput of this system, at ~30 queries returned per second, would demonstrate state-of-the-art search. Using this scalable approach, we would then be positioned to explore advantages that this embedded representation affords for metadata lookup and statistical analysis.

title: Unlocking Cross-Engine Governance With Scan APIs
abstract: While companies have embraced the data lakehouse architecture and benefits it provides, maintaining data governance has become a much more complicated story. Many companies today implement cumbersome workarounds, such as processing and maintaining multiple copies of datasets, duplicating access policies in different systems, or worse bypassing access controls altogether. In this talk, we'll explore some of the current problems with data governance and the data lakehouse architecture and how Scan APIs can address some of those challenges.

title: Unlocking the potential of multimodal data at scale
abstract: AI is becoming a very powerful commodity tool to turn unstructured data into structured data. This has greatly improved the importance of unstructured data and is posing new challenges in the world of data analytics: how to govern the data, how to store the data, how to access the data efficiently, and how to make the data available to ML models. In this talk, we will discuss how we're approaching these problems given the state of the world with open table formats such as Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg, as well as new file formats such as LanceDB.

title: Unlocking Video Data at Scale: VLM Batch Inference with Ray on Databricks
abstract: Organisations sit on vast video archives (surveillance, manufacturing, inspections), yet lack scalable methods to extract insights. This session presents a production-ready architecture for distributed video analytics using Vision Language Models (VLMs) on Databricks.We'll walk through a three-stage accelerator: (1) video ingestion into Unity Catalog Volumes, (2) VLM registration with MLflow for reproducibility, and (3) distributed batch inference using Ray and VLLM with Qwen2.5-VL-32B. You'll see how Ray orchestrates GPU-accelerated inference across video datasets and how to extract structured entities from VLM outputs using Databricks AI Functions.Attendees will leave with:A reusable pattern for multi-modal video intelligence at scaleWorking code integrating Ray, VLLM, and Unity CatalogPrompt engineering techniques for video inputsCost and performance considerations for VLM workloadsWhether your use case is retail, manufacturing, or public safety—this pattern applies.

title: Unstructured Data Ingestion with Lakeflow Connect
abstract: Your enterprise runs on unstructured documents that live everywhere: SharePoint folders, Google Drive shares, cloud storage buckets, email attachments. Pulling them into one governed place has historically meant stitching together custom scripts, brittle APIs, and pipelines that break the moment a vendor changes their template. In this lightning talk, we'll show how Lakeflow Connect makes unstructured data ingestion fully managed, incremental, and production-ready. We'll set up a SharePoint connector in minutes, land unstructured documents in Delta with Unity Catalog governance, and turn them into structured, queryable content using AI Parse Document, our research-backed AI Function for intelligent Document Processing. Walk away knowing how to turn the unstructured documents stored across external sources into a queryable data layer that powers smarter agents, dashboards, and analytics for every part of your business.
