title: Using AI to Migrate Semantic Models and Dashboards to Databricks Metric Views and AI/BI
abstract: At HP, we are working to integrate more of our business intelligence and analytics directly into the Databricks platform. To minimize impacts on analytics teams and their partners across organizations, we needed a way to automate and accelerate migrations of legacy semantic models and dashboards into Databricks. We developed a scalable AI based approach to parse existing BI artifacts, translate semantic models into Metric Views, convert existing visualizations into Databricks Dashboards and validate the results. This presentation shares lessons learned across multiple migrations, including both our key challenges and successes.

title: Vendor Sprawl to Lakeflow: Scaling a Governed, Multi-Tenant Platform in Financial Services
abstract: Highly regulated organizations struggle to balance data democratization with governance, operational overhead, and tool sprawl. In this session, we share how we scaled a Databricks-centered platform using a governed multi-tenant model that separates interactive self-service analytics from production-grade data services. We outline the architecture and operating patterns that enabled growth—governance, tenancy, and automated deployments—and how we implemented Lakeflow, including Lakeflow Connect, to standardize ingestion and consolidate third-party tools into Databricks-native services. Attendees will gain practical strategies to define workload boundaries, enable repeatable low-risk deployments, operationalize ingestion as a product, and execute phased consolidation with measurable outcomes.

title: Versionless and Environments for Notebooks, Jobs, Pipelines: Safe DBR Upgrades and Cached Packages
abstract: On classic compute, upgrading a DBR version and stitching together cluster libraries, init scripts and Spark configs consume a meaningful share of a platform team’s time, and every upgrade risks breaking production pipelines. Serverless eliminates both with versionless runtime and Databricks’ Environment model. This session covers the two pieces that make versionless trustworthy at enterprise scale. Lakehouse Replay continuously replays a representative sample of real production workloads to validate Databricks runtime changes before they ship, catching regressions with zero customer effort. Environments deliver a unified, portable dependency strategy with faster startup, tighter governance and clearer observability for notebooks, jobs, and pipelines. Attendees leave with a clear picture of how versionless and environments fit together and how to plan their move off manual DBR upgrades.

abstract: Viktoria Semaan walks you through two ways to build data apps on Databricks, using a real-world use case: extracting insights from public company 10-K filings, storing structured financial data in Databricks, and running analytics on it immediately. The first path uses Claude Code with the Databricks AI Dev Kit, the production-grade approach for enterprise developers who want full control, governance, and deep Databricks integration. The second path uses Lovable, the natural fit for vibe coding, rapid prototyping, and getting non-developers building fast. Both connect directly to Databricks. You will leave with a clear view of the trade-offs between the two approaches, the resources to get started the same day, and a new benchmark for how fast intelligent data apps can be built and deployed.

title: Vibe Investigating with Lakewatch and Genie
abstract: For decades, security investigations have required equal parts query-language incantations, instinct, and raw persistence. Lakewatch and Genie use AI to change the game, allowing analysts to investigate by simply asking questions in natural language, extracting patterns, pivoting, and getting results fast. In this session, we'll demonstrate "vibe investigating" using Genie against real-world security datasets. We'll uncover multi-stage attacks including prompt injection, credential theft, C2 beaconing, lateral movement, and a few more surprises! We'll show the full investigation arc — establishing baselines, detecting anomalies, pivoting across data sources, and building attack timelines. No query languages — just questions, answers, and a faster path to results. Attendees will leave with practical patterns for using Lakewatch Genie, crafting effective investigation prompts and supercharging their security investigations.

title: Vibe Your Data Model, Supercharge Your Genie
abstract: Nobody loves data modeling. It takes weeks, requires dozens of meetings, and by the time you ship a schema the business has already changed. But skip the model and your Genie Spaces pay the price: wasted tokens on join definitions, ambiguous metrics, and answers you can't trust. In this session we show you how to break out of that trap. We introduce Vibe Data Modeling, where AI agents generate complete, validated business data models from a plain English description of your organization and iterate on them in minutes, not months. Then we connect the dots to Genie: a solid data model paired with Metric Views eliminates the token tax, letting Genie focus on understanding your questions instead of navigating your schema. The result is a Genie that is cheaper, faster, and dramatically more accurate. We will walk through a real customer engagement that produced a 679-table enterprise model across 21 domains in days and show how it feeds directly into Genie Spaces that actually deliver.

title: Vibes to Validation: AI Eval for Partners
abstract: Stop eyeballing Genie answers — start measuring them. In this hands-on session you'll attach a labeled evaluation set to a Genie Space, run the built-in benchmark, and read per-question scores to find out where it actually fails. Bring the Genie Space you built yesterday, or spin one up from a track. You'll write 15 questions across five failure-mode categories, label acceptable answers, and run the benchmark to pinpoint your weakest category. Then change one line of instructions, re-run, and watch the score move — sometimes the wrong way, which is a real finding. You'll leave with a completed benchmark run and a repeatable method you can use on a customer's Genie Space next week. Hands-on workshop - Bring a laptop - Free Edition account required - Lunch will be served.

title: Virtual Delta Tables: Building a Multimodal Lakehouse
abstract: Managing multimodal inference is one of the defining challenges facing AI teams. LLMs now consider documents, images, and videos, producing higher quality results and reducing time wasted with data prep. The lakehouse architecture solves part of the problem but many teams are struggling to incorporate an increasing variety of data into their workflow. Rather than ingesting, re-encoding, or modifying massive troves of existing data, multimodal teams are looking to work with original artifacts. This talk introduces Virtual Delta Tables and the associated open source code designed for multimodal inference. Virtual Delta Tables incorporate original data from different sources into a singular logical structure for ease of use by data scientists and ML engineers. By offering a Delta Lake interface the entire ecosystem from Databricks to DuckDB can be used in multimodal work. We'll highlight just how far you can push the lakehouse architecture in the rapidly changing AI data landscape!

title: We Killed ETL: Unstructured.io Foundation
abstract: You’ve known Unstructured as the company to power your RAG applications; first we transformed your PDFs to JSON, then we built ETL pipelines for delivering chunked, embedded JSON to Delta Tables that enabled LLMs with low-latency RAG. Now we’re changing the model entirely. Imagine if agents could take context from your whole enterprise, without having to copy every document into Databricks? Foundation builds enterprise-wide context on demand. Source documents stay where they are. Extracted data lands in ephemeral Postgres provisioned via Neon, with pointers for the agent back to the originals. All your data outside the Databricks ecosystem is now workable from inside it. This talk is for every team still maintaining a pipeline.

title: Weaving Data Into the Financial Fabric: How Nasdaq Uses Databricks to Power the Innovation Economy
abstract: Nasdaq is the trusted fabric of the world’s financial system, and data is at the heart of everything we do. Learn how we’re using Databricks to drive insights, support decision-making and deliver industry-leading financial solutions. Using Delta Lake’s open formats and Unity Catalog, we’ve consolidated disparate data stores into a unified corporate data lakehouse to create a single source of truth for enterprise data. We’ll demo how we’re using AgentBricks and Databricks Apps to democratize access to data while maintaining oversight and governance. You’ll also discover how our Capital Access Platforms division has built its core data platform on Databricks. With exchange and index data, alternative datasets and institutional data for more than 110,000 public and private‑market strategies and funds covering over $90 trillion in institutional assets, the platform enables rapid product development, creates value from our data assets and forms the foundation of our AI strategy.

title: What Worked, What Didn’t: Virgin Atlantic’s Flight to Trusted Generative BI
abstract: As decision-making at Virgin Atlantic sped up, our BI stack creaked. Leaders wanted answers in hours and questions increasingly cut across commercial, operational, and customer data. Like many teams, we turned to GenBI to close that gap. Our first attempt didn’t go well. Answers arrived faster, but confidence dropped. Without shared metric definitions, visible lineage, or governance designed in from the start, ambiguity scaled faster than trust. “Is this right?” became the default question again. In this session, we share how we rebuilt GenBI on trusted foundations using Databricks. We’ll show how Unity Catalog and UC Metrics Views anchor AI answers to signed-off metrics, how Databricks Genie enables users to interrogate and explain results, and why explainability became part of the user experience. Attendees will leave with practical lessons for moving to decision-grade GenBI, drawn from real production use cases and delivered as a visual, story-led case study.

title: What’s New in Apache Spark™ 4.1?
abstract: Explore the exciting new features of Apache Spark 4.1 with major new capabilities for both data engineering and analytics workflows. We introduce Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP) to let users define what their data pipelines should accomplish while Spark orchestrates execution, dependencies, parallelism and retries, an official Real-Time Mode in Structured Streaming for sub-second, continuous low-latency processing, and extensive improvements to the PySpark ecosystem with Arrow-native UDFs/UDTFs, Python Data Source filter pushdown, and better Python worker logging. The release also brings Spark Connect enhancements including GA support for Spark ML on the Python client and increased stability for large workloads, and expands SQL support with GA SQL Scripting, the VARIANT type with shredding optimizations, support for recursive CTEs, and new approximate data sketch functions. Spark 4.1 prioritizes higher-level abstractions, real-time performance, richer Python support, and more.

title: When 75% of Your Builders Aren't Engineers: Enterprise Vibe Coding Meets Databricks
abstract: The Replit × Databricks integration was built on a bet: that non-technical business users, not just developers, should be able to build production data apps on enterprise data. That bet is paying off. 75% of users building with our integration are non-technical, and they're shipping governed apps that deploy directly into Databricks with full Unity Catalog permissions, data masking, and platform-team observability. This session covers what happens when you put vibe coding tools in the hands of LOB and data teams at Fortune 500 companies. We'll discuss the architecture that makes this possible, the trust model that convinced security teams to say yes (apps deploy to .databricks.com), and the adoption we are seeing in leading companies using AI tools with a data foundation set in Databricks.

title: When Anyone Can Build Anything: The New AI-Native Stack
abstract: The act of building, whether software, knowledge systems or workflows, is being fundamentally democratized. Natural language is becoming the new interface between human intent and outcome. Natural language is becoming the new programming language. Ideas are becoming applications in minutes, not months. This panel brings together the founders of AI-native tools that are collapsing the distance between human intent and running software. Together, they'll explore a near-future where dramatically more people can ship products, and where the primary bottleneck shifts from technical skill to creative vision. The big questions: What happens when the cost of building software drops by orders of magnitude? Are we heading toward a world with far more software, fewer traditional developers or both? When AI agents can build, test, and deploy autonomously, how does engineering culture evolve? What's still hard and what will remain uniquely human in the development process? Where do AI agents break down and are we moving fast enough to find out before it matters Join the founders reshaping the most fundamental act in technology for a candid look at where this lands in the next 2–3 years.

title: When Data Saves Lives: Scaling Precision Medicine for Childhood Cancer
abstract: CCIA currently manages more than two petabytes of cancer patient data from over 2800 patients participating in the Zero Childhood Cancer Program (ZERO), a world-leading precision medicine program for children and young people with cancer that is built upon the Databricks Lakehouse. Databricks has fundamentally transformed precision medicine research and clinical workflows at ZERO. Previously, variant data was stored across thousands of text files, making comprehensive searches across the entire cohort intractable. Scientists were limited to analyzing predefined gene panels, severely constraining hypothesis-driven research. With Databricks, we can now search across all 14+ billion variants from our entire patient cohort simultaneously, allowing researchers to test novel hypotheses and rapidly identify patients with related variants across any genomic region, a capability that was previously impossible, and represents a key capability in helping CCIA scale from 2800 to over 4000 patients

title: When Good Creds Go Bad: The New Failure Mode of AI Agents
abstract: Authenticated AI agents introduce a new failure mode. Using valid credentials, they can perform actions that are policy-compliant but semantically incorrect, such as retrieving sensitive data into the wrong context or executing unintended changes. Traditional IAM systems evaluate identity and permissions, not intent or correctness at runtime. As agents begin using valid credentials to act across enterprise systems, security teams must move beyond static identity and permission checks. This session explores contextual authorization, just-in-time access, and runtime auditability as the next layer of enterprise agent security, including what it means to verify not just who an agent is, but whether the environment it’s running in can be trusted.

title: When Redis Isn’t the Answer: Serving Lakehouse Data at Scale
abstract: As our feature and operational use cases grew, maintaining separate Redis/DynamoDB stacks alongside the data lake added latency, skew and ops burden. At Superhuman (formerly Grammarly), we adopted Lakebase to serve low‑latency data directly from Databricks, simplifying our architecture while meeting strict SLAs. This session details our setup and results: how we modelled entities and keys, tuned Lakebase capacity and read replicas for high QPS and enforced freshness with Change Data Feed–driven syncs. We’ll show code and configs for provisioning online stores, publishing tables, and querying endpoints, plus before/after latency and maintenance metrics. Attendees will leave with reference patterns to consolidate online serving on Lakebase without sacrificing performance.

title: Where AI Governance Is Headed: Best Practices for Unifying Data, Models and Agents
abstract: AI is shifting from single models to multi-agent systems, and governance must evolve with it. Traditional approaches break down when agents dynamically access data, tools, APIs and multiple AI models across platforms. In this session, Databricks and Thoughtworks introduce a unified approach to AI governance built on a data-centric foundation. Learn how to extend governance from data to models, agents and tools using Unity Catalog, consistent identity-based controls and end-to-end observability. We’ll explore where AI governance is headed, including multi-AI governance with Unity AI Gateway, open and interoperable controls across frameworks and real-time monitoring to detect risk and manage cost. Thoughtworks will share architectural principles for building governed agentic systems at scale. Walk away with a clear path to move fast with AI without losing control.

title: Who Goes There? Enterprise Auth and Identity Management on Databricks Apps
abstract: For an application to move from a prototype to a core business asset, it must meet the highest standards of enterprise security and compliance. This session explores the advanced security architecture of Databricks Apps, demonstrating how it inherits and extends the robust governance of the Data Intelligence Platform. We will move beyond basic access to explore sophisticated identity management patterns, including On-Behalf-Of (OBO) authentication for user-scoped actions and secure compute resource delegation. You will also learn how the platform is hardening the application lifecycle with features like automated secret rotation and dedicated network namespaces to ensure total isolation. Whether you are handling sensitive PII or building internal tools for thousands of users, this session provides the blueprint for building apps that are secure by design, fully audited, and ready for the most regulated environments.

title: Why Caresource Chose Databricks AI/BI Over Traditional BI for Regulatory Reporting
abstract: CareSource initially planned to migrate hundreds of state-mandated SQL Server Reporting Services (SSRS) reports to Power BI Paginated Reports. However, with a mature Databricks platform already in place, that approach would have required added data movement, duplicated governance logic, and new licensing costs. CareSource and West Monroe share how a Databricks AI/BI pilot reshaped the strategy. By keeping regulatory reporting in Databricks, CareSource eliminated downstream exports, improved reliability, and reduced runtimes from hours to minutes. We’ll review the scalable architecture, including a custom extract framework that generates state-specific files and automates secure SFTP delivery, plus a business-friendly interface that drove adoption among non-technical users. Attendees will gain practical guidance on building governed regulatory pipelines and knowing when AI/BI is a strong alternative to traditional BI tools.

title: Why Data-Intelligent Agents Win: A Side-by-Side Benchmark
abstract: Vibe coding is fun until it hits production. In this session, we benchmark two agents running the identical LLM on identical enterprise workloads — one armed with raw SQL and good intentions, one grounded in the Databricks Data Intelligence stack: a Unity Catalog semantic layer, governed metric views, UC functions with LLM-readable docstrings, and Vector Search over enriched business context. We run the benchmark live, on real questions including the ambiguous, multilingual ones your users actually ask. Then we step back and look at what the trajectories tell us about where production agent cost actually comes from — and why the platform underneath your agents matters more than the model running on top of it.

We run the benchmark live, on real questions including the ambiguous, multilingual ones your users actually ask. Then we step back and look at what the trajectories tell us about where production agent cost actually comes from — and why the platform underneath your agents matters more than the model running on top of it.

title: Why It's Time to Take AI/BI Seriously
abstract: I'm a Power BI developer by trade, and for years I've refused to engage with other data visualization platforms. Every time I did, I just found it was lacking capabilities or had serious deficiencies compared to Power BI. Then 2025 hit and Databricks invested heavily in improving AI/BI, metric views and Genie. Now, AI/BI is ready to be a legitimate challenger in the Data Visualisation space. In this talk I will show you how you can use AI/BI, metric views and Genie to get the most out of your data. We will start from basics, building a metric view, using it to build a dashboard and then setting up a Genie space. I'll then walk you through my top tips on how you can get the most out of each of them. We'll talk about the types of work where AI/BI thrives and discuss where I see it going in its pursuit of being the next big data visualization platform. AI/BI is here and it's ready to be taken seriously.

title: Why Vector Stores Are Not Enough: Using Lakebase as a Durable Memory Layer for Autonomous Agents
abstract: We're often told that Vector Databases are the "memory" for AI Agents. But vector search only gives you a probabilistic similarity score. In enterprise workflows, "probably" isn't good enough. Agents need deterministic, transactional state—and they need the ability to compound their knowledge over time. In this session, we'll move beyond stateless "goldfish" chatbots and build a truly self-improving agent system using Databricks Apps, Databricks Jobs, and Lakebase Autoscaling. We'll demonstrate how to build a production-ready "Stateful Worker" agent, featuring asynchronous batch "dreaming" distillation jobs that allow your agents to distill insights and get smarter overnight. To ground these concepts, we'll walk through the architecture from three critical perspectives: The Agent User Experience: How can we ensure an agent knows a user's role, preferences, and past context? We will demo the stateless stateful agents on Databricks Apps and see how users can benefit from user and agent scoped memory. The Database Admin Experience: How do we audit what an agent is learning? We'll explore Lakebase's intuitive UI/SQL, understand the Agent's thinking with observability tools, and leverage database branching and Point-in-Time Restore (PITR) to create isolated simulation sandboxes where agents can test destructive actions (e.g., "Delete User") safely. The Agent Developer Experience: How can I go from nothing to a fully deployed, memory-enabled enterprise agent in minutes, while still maintaining full control over the underlying code? We'll be showing how simple it is to author custom code agents with full integration with Databricks resources. Attendees will leave with a reusable architecture, deployment templates, and a concrete framework to build high-performing, autonomous, and secure agents in production.

title: Your AI Strategy is Only as Good as Your People Strategy
abstract: As AI moves from experimentation to enterprise impact, success depends on workforce readiness, not just technology. Market leaders have upskilled over 50% of their employees and are redesigning workflows around AI, while 60% of organizations still struggle to generate value from their investments. In this session, Robin Sutara and Melanie Botha explore how to build an AI-enabled workforce by aligning culture, people, process and enablement with your data strategy. You'll learn how to assess your data and AI maturity, close critical skills gaps at scale through structured learning programs, and integrate AI agents into teams in ways that elevate human talent. Drawing on customer proof points and the Databricks data and AI maturity framework, this session provides a practical roadmap for treating upskilling as a core investment—so every project becomes a data and AI project and every employee contributes to AI-driven outcomes.

title: Your guide to fine-grained access control: Permissions, ABAC, and RBAC in Unity Catalog
abstract: Fine-grained access control in Unity Catalog isn’t a set of disconnected features; it’s a unified framework. Understanding how permissions, RBAC and ABAC work together is key to governing data and AI at scale. In this session, we’ll break down each approach and when to use it. Learn how granular permissions enforce least privilege, how RBAC creates clear isolation boundaries and how ABAC uses governed tags to apply row filters, column masks and policy logic across entire catalogs automatically. We’ll walk through this as a progression — from dynamic views and table-level controls to scalable, tag-driven policies — so you know how to evolve your approach as your data estate grows. We’ll also cover performance considerations, how to avoid conflicts when combining methods and real-world patterns for production environments. Finally, we’ll preview what’s next, including extending fine-grained governance to AI assets and unstructured data, along with new visibility and impact analysis capabilities in Unity Catalog. Walk away with practical guidance to design, scale and future-proof access control.

title: Your Guide to Open Table Formats — Delta, Iceberg, Best Practices, and What’s Next!
abstract: Open table formats had a breakthrough year—and now the focus shifts to how to use them effectively. In this session, we’ll break down what’s new across Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg, including an early look at Delta 5.0 and the Iceberg v4 Adaptive Metadata Tree, which brings the two formats closer together at the metadata layer for high-performance, multi-engine workloads. More importantly, we’ll share best practices for working across formats today. Learn how teams are using the Unified Delta Kernel (now GA, written in Rust) across Spark, Flink, and DuckDB, and how Catalog-Managed Commits enable safer multi-engine writes, stronger governance, and multi-table transactions. We’ll also cover Auto CDF for building efficient incremental pipelines. Finally, we’ll highlight innovations for AI workloads, including the FILE data type and VARIANT shredding. Walk away with practical guidance to build, optimize, and future-proof your open data architecture.

title: Zero-Copy Federated Energy Analytics: ADME + Databricks in Action
abstract: Oil and gas companies have standardized on Azure Data Manager for Energy (ADME) as their subsurface system of record, but running analytics and AI on that data has meant copying massive OSDU datasets into downstream platforms, breaking governance and slowing every workflow that follows. In this jointly developed Microsoft and Databricks session, we introduce the ADME connector for Azure Databricks: a zero‑copy, federated path that brings Databricks compute directly to OSDU data, with native Unity Catalog governance and serverless scale. The connector is on track to land as an official Lakeflow Community Connector, giving Databricks customers a governed, supported path into ADME out of the box.We walk through the architecture, show the connector in action against live ADME, and share how operators across the industry are accelerating subsurface analytics while keeping ADME as the single source of truth.

title: ZeroETL Was Just the Start: Operational Databases belong in the Medallion Architecture
abstract: The medallion architecture dictates how we typically think about data, but that framework has historically been limited to the data lifecycle strictly within the Lakehouse. Lakebase takes this a step further by expanding the architectural blueprint to redefine how data enters your Bronze layer and how it is consumed from Gold. Rather than extracting and moving data across system boundaries, your operational database natively acts as the Bronze foundation to immediately feed downstream analytics. On the other end, Lakebase closes the loop by directly serving those refined Gold datasets to production applications with operational low latency, eliminating the need to export data out of your ecosystem.
